'''David Wallace Wotherspoon''' (born 16 January 1990) is a professional [[association football|soccer]] player who plays as a [[midfielder]] for [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]]. Born in Scotland, he represents the [[Canada men's national soccer team|Canada national team]].

==Club career==

===Early career===
He played at youth level with Abernethy Cubs, Bridge of Earn AFC, and the [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone Academy]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.canadasoccer.com/canada-soccer-announce-squad-for-fifa-world-cup-qatar-2022|title=Canada Soccer announces squad for FIFA World Cup Qatar 2022|date=November 12, 2022|work=[[Canadian Soccer Association]]}}</ref>

Wotherspoon was part of [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]]'s youth setup, but moved to [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] in the belief that he would have more opportunity to break into senior football.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/football/spl/2009/03/18/hibs-hand-first-team-chance-to-seven-starlets-86908-21207211/ |title=Hibs hand first team chance to seven starlets |work=[[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]]|location=Glasgow|access-date=3 September 2010 |date=18 March 2009}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/football/spl/hibernian/2009/10/08/i-had-to-quit-celtic-to-live-my-football-dream-admits-hibs-star-david-wotherspoon-86908-21731469/ |title=I had to quit Celtic to live my football dream, admits Hibs star David Wotherspoon |work=[[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]]|location=Glasgow |date=8 October 2009 |last=Cameron |first=Neil |access-date=3 September 2010}}</ref>

===Hibernian===
He was part of the [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] youth side that won both the [[Scottish Youth Cup]] and the Scottish league in the [[2008–09 in Scottish football|2008–09 season]], with Wotherspoon contributing eight goals from midfield.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/Wotherspoon-has-a-Hibs-double.5215487.jp |title=Wotherspoon has a Hibs double on his mind|publisher=Johnston Press |work=[[Edinburgh Evening News]] |date=29 April 2009 |access-date=3 September 2010 |last=Hardie |first=David}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/scottish_fa_news.cfm?page=1133&newsCategoryID=4&newsID=4618 |title=Hibs Lift Scottish FA Youth Cup |publisher=[[Scottish Football Association]] |work=scottishfa.co.uk |date=29 April 2009 |access-date=16 August 2009 |archive-date=16 June 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110616060821/http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/scottish_fa_news.cfm?page=1133&newsCategoryID=4&newsID=4618 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Wotherspoon made his senior debut in the 2–1 home win over [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] at the start of the 2009–10 season, scoring Hibs' first goal.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://sport.scotsman.com/hibernianfc/Hibernian-2---1.5558080.jp |title=Hibernian 2 – 1 St Mirren: Late Benjelloun strike gets Hibs off to winning SPL start |work=[[Edinburgh Evening News]] |publisher=Johnston Press|last=Hardie |first=David |access-date=3 September 2010 |date=15 August 2009}}</ref> After establishing himself in the Hibs first team as a [[defender (football)|right back]], Wotherspoon signed a contract with Hibs until 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/h/hibernian/8420850.stm |title=Wotherspoon extends stay at Hibs |publisher=BBC Sport |date=18 December 2009}}</ref>

During the [[2010–11 Hibernian F.C. season|2010–11 season]] Wotherspoon was more often used as a [[right midfielder]], and in early 2011 he scored two goals against [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] and [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] to help his team go on a six-match unbeaten run. He had previously not scored in 63 matches and said that he wanted to start scoring more goals for Hibs.<ref>{{cite news   | url =  http://www.scotsman.com/sport/hibs-david-wotherspoon-hopeful-two-goals-in-six-matches-will-lead-to-further-net-gains-1-1530532 | title =  Hibs: David Wotherspoon hopeful two goals in six matches will lead to further net gains  | publisher = Johnston Press |work = Edinburgh Evening News | date =   7 March 2012 | access-date = 16 April 2012}}</ref>

Wotherspoon's form improved in the early part of the [[2012–13 Hibernian F.C. season|2012–13 season]]. He scored a late winning goal in the [[2012–13 Scottish Cup|Scottish Cup]] tie against holders and [[Edinburgh derby]] rivals [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20483951 |title=Hibernian 1–0 Hearts |first=Colin |last=Moffat  |publisher=BBC Sport |date=2 December 2012 |access-date=2 December 2012}}</ref> A decline in Hibs' fortunes during the season was mirrored by Wotherspoon personally, who lost his place in the side.<ref name = "sjfc">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23147403 |title=St Johnstone sign David Wotherspoon from Hibernian |publisher=BBC Sport |date=2 July 2013 |access-date=2 July 2013}}</ref> He left Hibs at the end of his contract in the 2013 close season.

===St Johnstone===
Wotherspoon signed a two-year contract with his hometown club [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] on 2 July 2013.<ref name = "sjfc"/> On 10 July 2013, Wotherspoon scored a goal from a free-kick from 21 yards in a pre-season friendly against [[Cowdenbeath F.C.|Cowdenbeath]]. This was his first appearance and his first goal for St Johnstone.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/newsitemsdetail.php?param=2601|title=Wotherspoon goal enough to secure win at Cowdenbeath|publisher=St Johnstone FC|date=11 July 2013|access-date=13 July 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140521143113/http://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/newsitemsdetail.php?param=2601|archive-date=21 May 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> He scored his first league goal for the club with a free kick in a 4–0 win against [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] on 17 August, and had a [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalty kick]] saved in the same game.<ref name = "ross co">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23740656 |first=Kenny |last=Crawford |title=Tommy Wright wants clarity over Stevie May's future|publisher=BBC Sport |date=17 August 2013|access-date=18 August 2013}}</ref> Wotherspoon helped the club win the [[2013–14 Scottish Cup]].<ref name = "2015 deal"/> He signed a new two-year contract with St Johnstone in January 2015.<ref name = "2015 deal">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30920914 |title=St Johnstone: David Wotherspoon commits to club until 2017|publisher=BBC Sport |date=21 January 2015 |access-date=30 January 2015}}</ref>

In February 2019, Wotherspoon extended his contract with St Johnstone for another two years.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47277780 |title=St Johnstone: David Wotherspoon signs contract extension|publisher=BBC Sport |date=18 February 2019 |access-date=18 February 2019}}</ref> On 26 October 2019, he made his 250th appearance for the club, and marked the occasion by scoring twice as St Johnstone won 3–2 against [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]].<ref>{{cite web|title=St Johnstone 3 Hamilton 2 as Callum Hendry hits late winner to break Saints' Premiership duck|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/st-johnstone-3-hamilton-2-20731035|work=Daily Record|location=Glasgow|date=26 October 2019|access-date=31 October 2019}}</ref> In 2021 Wotherspoon played a critical role in helping St Johnstone achieve the cup double, winning both the [[Scottish Cup]] and the [[Scottish League Cup]]. In the [[2021 Scottish Cup Final|Scottish Cup Final]], Wotherspoon had an assist on [[Shaun Rooney]]'s goal and was named Man of the Match for his efforts.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/soccer/canadian-david-wotherspoon-wins-scottish-cup-1.6037624|title=Canada's David Wotherspoon helps St. Johnstone capture Scottish Cup|date=22 May 2021|work=[[Canadian Broadcasting Corporation|CBC]]}}</ref>

In November 2021 Wotherspoon suffered an [[Anterior cruciate ligament|ACL]] injury during St Johnstone's [[2021–22 Scottish League Cup|Scottish League Cup]] semi-final against [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]], ruling him out for eight months.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/st-johnstone-midfielder-david-wotherspoon-25684569|date=13 December 2021|title=St Johnstone midfielder David Wotherspoon out for eight months with ACL injury|work=[[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]]|location=Glasgow|first=Matthew|last=Gallagher}}</ref> He returned to training in August 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/st-johnstone/3616816/david-wotherspoon-tony-gallacher-st-johnstone-comeback/|title=St Johnstone duo David Wotherspoon and Tony Gallacher just two weeks away from comeback|date=22 August 2022|first=Eric|last=Nicolson}}</ref> Two months later Wotherspoon made his first appearance for St Johnstone since his injury on 15 October, subbing into their league match against [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] which ended in a 1–0 defeat.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/news/article/livingston-1-0-saints-1|date=15 October 2022|title=Livingston 1-0 Saints}}</ref> At the end of the [[2022–23 Scottish Premiership|season]], St Johnstone announced Wotherspoon would not be offered a new contract, ending his time with his hometown club after a decade.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/news/article/squad-update-1|date=May 30, 2023|title=Squad Update}}</ref>

===Inverness Caledonian Thistle===
In October 2023, Wotherspoon joined [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] on a deal until January 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ictfc.com/david-wotherspoon-signs-for-ictfc/|date=October 17, 2023|title=David Wotherspoon Signs For ICTFC|work=[[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]]}}</ref> He made his debut for his new club on October 28 against [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]], and scored the only goal in a 1–0 victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://keepup.com.au/news/david-wotherspoons-debut-goal-seals-caley-win-against-airdrieonians/|date=October 28, 2023|title=David Wotherspoon's debut goal seals Caley win against Airdrieonians|work=Keep Up}}</ref>

===Dundee United===
After leaving Inverness at the end of a short-term contract, Wotherspoon signed with [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] for the rest of the 2023–24 season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.stv.tv/sport/dundee-united-sign-former-hibs-and-st-johnstone-player-david-wotherspoon |title=Dundee United sign former Hibs and St Johnstone player David Wotherspoon |website=STV News |first=Peter |last=Cassidy |date=15 January 2024 |accessdate=16 January 2024}}</ref>

=== Dunfermline Athletic ===
Wotherspoon was signed by [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] in July 2024, after his six-month contract with Dundee United expired.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hart |first=Ross |date=2024-07-01 |title=Dunfermline: Ex St Johnstone star David Wotherspoon signs |url=https://www.dunfermlinepress.com/sport/24423595.dunfermline-ex-st-johnstone-star-david-wotherspoon-signs/ |access-date=2024-07-02 |website=Dunfermline Press |language=en}}</ref>

=== Inverness Caledonian Thistle (Second spell) ===
In July 2025, Wotherspoon returned to Inverness Caledonian Thistle in Scottish League One.<ref>{{cite web | title=Caley Thistle confirm return of fans' favourite on one-year deal | date=24 June 2025 | url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/inverness-caledonian-thistle/6785344/caley-thistle-return-fans-favourite-one-year-deal/ }}</ref>

==International career==
===Youth===
Wotherspoon represented Scotland at [[Scotland national under-18 football team|under-18]]<ref name = "sfa18">{{cite web |url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/football_player_profile.cfm?page=106&playerID=39123&squadID=11 |title=David Wotherspoon – U18 Squad |publisher=[[Scottish Football Association]] |access-date=3 September 2010}}</ref> and [[Scotland national under-19 football team|under-19]]<ref name = "sfa19">{{cite web|url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/football_player_profile.cfm?page=106&playerID=39123&squadID=9 |title=David Wotherspoon – U19 Squad |work=scottishfa.co.uk |publisher=[[Scottish Football Association]] |access-date=3 September 2010}}</ref><ref name = "een"/> levels before he made his first team debut for Hibs. He was called into the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|under-21]] squad soon after he made his senior club debut,<ref name = "een">{{cite news |url=http://sport.scotsman.com/sport/Young-gun-David-is-in.5710201.jp |title=Young gun David is in with more than a shout |work=[[Edinburgh Evening News]]|publisher=Johnston Press |date=7 October 2009 |access-date=3 September 2010 |last=Dempster |first=Martin}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/internationals/8281458.stm |title=Scots call Forbes and Wotherspoon |publisher=BBC Sport |date=29 September 2009}}</ref> and he made his first appearance at that level in a 4–0 win against [[Azerbaijan national under-21 football team|Azerbaijan]] in November 2009.<ref name = "sfa21">{{cite web |url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/football_player_profile.cfm?page=106&playerID=39123&squadID=5 |title=David Wotherspoon – U21 Squad |publisher=[[Scottish Football Association]] |access-date=3 September 2010}}</ref> He scored his first goal for the team, a late equaliser in a 1–1 draw against [[Sweden national under-21 football team|Sweden]], in August 2010.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://sport.scotsman.com/sport/Late-strike-draws-better-picture.6470632.jp |title=Late strike draws better picture for Scotland Under-21s |last=Wright |first=Angus |work=[[The Scotsman]] |publisher=Johnston Press |date=12 August 2010 |access-date=12 August 2010}}</ref> His second goal was the match-winner in a 2–1 victory against the [[Netherlands national under-21 football team|Netherlands]] in November 2011.<ref>{{cite news|publisher=BBC Sport |date=14 November 2011 |access-date=14 November 2011 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/scotland/15727776 |first=Clive |last=Lindsay |title=Netherlands U21 1–2 Scotland U21}}</ref>

===Senior===
Wotherspoon was eligible to play for [[Canada men's national soccer team|Canada]] as his mother was born there.<ref name = "canada">{{Cite web|url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/st-johnstone/729430/david-wotherspoon-fighting-to-get-back-into-the-st-johnstone-first-team/|title=David Wotherspoon fighting to get back into the St Johnstone first team|first=Eric|last=Nicolson|date=22 September 2018|work=The Courier}}</ref> He was selected for the Canada squad in March 2018 for a friendly against New Zealand without ever having been to Canada.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43442816 |title=St Johnstone's David Wotherspoon is called up by Canada after switch from Scotland |publisher=BBC Sport |date=17 March 2018 |access-date=17 March 2018}}</ref> He was again called up for a pair of [[2019–20 CONCACAF Nations League A#Group A|CONCACAF Nations League A]] matches against [[Cuba national football team|Cuba]] in September 2019.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Davidson |first1=Neal |title=TFC's Richie Laryea, Cavalry FC's Marco Carducci called up for Canada games against Cuba |url=https://www.thespec.com/sports-story/9570996-tfc-s-richie-laryea-cavalry-fc-s-marco-carducci-called-up-for-canada-games-against-cuba/ |publisher=Hamilton Spectator |date=28 August 2019}}</ref> In May 2019 Wotherspoon was named to the provisional squad for the [[2019 CONCACAF Gold Cup]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.canadasoccer.com/canada-soccer-announces-provisional-roster-for-the-2019-concacaf-gold-cup|title=CANADA SOCCER ANNOUNCES PROVISIONAL ROSTER FOR THE 2019 CONCACAF GOLD CUP|date=20 May 2021|work=Canada Soccer}}</ref> but was excluded from the final squad. Wotherspoon scored his first goal for Canada against the [[Cayman Islands national football team|Cayman Islands]] in a [[2022 FIFA World Cup qualification (CONCACAF)|2022 FIFA World Cup qualifying match]] on 29 March 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://northerntribune.ca/canada-world-cup-cayman-islands/|first=John|last=Jacques|title=Canada Coasts Past Cayman Islands in Historic Eleven-Goal Win|date=29 March 2021}}</ref> On 18 June he was named to the 60-man provisional squad for the [[2021 CONCACAF Gold Cup]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.canadasoccer.com/concacaf-gold-cup-provisional-rosters-confirmed|title=CONCACAF GOLD CUP PROVISIONAL ROSTERS CONFIRMED|date=18 June 2021|work=Canada Soccer}}</ref> but it was decided due to his heavy club schedule, he would not be a part of the final 23-man team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wakingthered.com/2021/7/1/22559537/canada-announces-strong-roster-ahead-of-2021-concacaf-gold-cup|first=Ryan|last=Lindsay|date=1 July 2021|title=Canada announces strong roster ahead of 2021 Concacaf Gold Cup|work=Waking the Red}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://anchor.fm/northern-ftbol/episodes/Episode-18--David-Wotherspoon-on-making-history-twice---the-Gold-Cup-and-more-e13l44v|date=29 June 2021|title=Episode 18 – David Wotherspoon on making history (twice!), the Gold Cup and more!|work=Northern Fútbol Podcast}}</ref>

In November 2022, Wotherspoon was named to Canada's squad for the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://canpl.ca/article/canada-announces-26-man-squad-for-2022-fifa-world-cup-in-qatar|date=November 13, 2022|title=Canada announces 26-man squad for 2022 FIFA World Cup in Qatar|work=[[Canadian Premier League]]|first=Charlie|last=O'Connor-Clarke}}</ref> He made his only appearance at the World Cup in Canada's third match against [[Morocco national football team|Morocco]] on December 1, as a substitute for [[Junior Hoilett]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/cn3z22jyznmo|date=December 1, 2022|title=Proud moment as Wotherspoon makes World Cup debut}}</ref> This marked the first time a [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] player took the field in a World Cup match.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/st-johnstone/3940714/david-wotherspoon-st-johnstone-canada-world-cup-history/|title=David Wotherspoon makes St Johnstone history with World Cup appearance – and there was cameo for 'Spoony Chop'|date=December 1, 2022|first=Eric|last=Nicolson}}</ref>

In June 2023, Wotherspoon was named to the 23-man Canadian squad contesting the [[2023 CONCACAF Nations League Finals]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Former CPLers Loturi, Zator called up by Canada for 2023 Concacaf Nations League Finals|date=June 7, 2023|url=https://canpl.ca/article/canada-canmnt-2023-concacaf-nations-league-final-roster|first=Mitchell|last=Tierney|work=[[Canadian Premier League]]}}</ref> On June 19 he was named to the squad for the [[2023 CONCACAF Gold Cup]], his first participation at the tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://canpl.ca/article/canmnt-announces-final-23-man-squad-for-concacaf-gold-cup|date=June 19, 2023|work=[[Canadian Premier League]]|title=CanMNT announces final 23-man squad for Concacaf Gold Cup|first=Charlie|last=O'Connor-Clarke}}</ref>

==Style of play==
Although he started out as a right back for Hibs, Wotherspoon has also played as a right-sided or attacking midfielder. His primary position is as a [[Midfielder|central midfielder]] and at the start of the [[2011–12 Hibernian F.C. season|2011–12 season]] he expressed his desire to play there more often.<ref name="position"/> Although he also said that he was willing to play anywhere to be in the first team.<ref name="position">{{cite news   | url =  https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/13736136 | title =  David Wotherspoon wants central Hibs role | publisher =  BBC Sport | date = 10 June 2011 | access-date = 16 April 2012}}</ref> Manager [[Pat Fenlon]] experimented with a 4–2–3–1 formation, using Wotherspoon as a central creative player, during the 2012–13 pre-season.<ref name = "2012 tactics">{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19393623|title=David Wotherspoon eyes regular run for Hibs|first=Brian|last=McLauchlin|publisher=BBC Sport |date=27 August 2012|access-date=27 August 2012}}</ref> These tactics were abandoned after a 3–0 defeat against [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]], with Wotherspoon then being used as a right midfielder in a more orthodox 4–4–2 shape.<ref name = "2012 tactics"/>

In recent years, Wotherspoon has become known for his regular use of the "Spoony chop".<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/st-johnstone/2296354/david-wotherspoon-world-cup-canada-st-johnstone/amp/|title=The 'Spoony Chop' could be seen at the World Cup as St Johnstone cup hero continues on road to Qatar with Canada|last=Nicolson|first=Eric|date=11 June 2021|work=The Courier}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Wotherspoon, who is from [[Bridge of Earn]], was a St Johnstone supporter in his childhood.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/Hibs39-Wotherspoon-aims-to-beat.5659675.jp |title=Hibs' Wotherspoon aims to beat boyhood heroes Saints |work=[[Edinburgh Evening News]] |publisher=Johnston Press|date=18 September 2009 |access-date=3 September 2010 |last=Hardie |first=David|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110616023911/https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/Hibs39-Wotherspoon-aims-to-beat.5659675.jp|archive-date=16 June 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref> His mother was born in Canada.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Nicolson |first1=Eric |title=David Wotherspoon fighting to get back into the St Johnstone first team |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/st-johnstone/729430/david-wotherspoon-fighting-to-get-back-into-the-st-johnstone-first-team/ |website=The Courier |date=22 September 2018 |access-date=8 June 2021}}</ref>

'''Graeme Garry Shinnie''' (born 4 August 1991) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[defensive midfielder]] or [[Defender (association football)|left back]] for [[Scottish Championship]] side, [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]].

He has previously played for [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]], [[Forres Mechanics F.C.|Forres Mechanics]], [[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]] and [[Wigan Athletic F.C.|Wigan Athletic]]. Shinnie made six full international appearances for [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] between May 2018 and March 2019.

== Career ==
=== Inverness Caledonian Thistle ===
Shinnie started his career playing for Dyce Boys Club, a boy's club in Aberdeen, alongside brother [[Andrew Shinnie|Andrew]].<ref>{{cite news|title=League Cup Final: Inverness star Graeme Shinnie out to make Aberdeen pay for snubbing him as a kid|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/league-cup-final-inverness-star-3248507|publisher=Daily Record|date=16 March 2014|access-date=27 March 2014}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/inverness-caledonian-thistle/1743792/the-making-of-graeme-shinnie-from-boys-club-die-hard-to-aberdeen-talisman/|title=The making of Graeme Shinnie, from boys club die-hard to Aberdeen talisman|first=Jamie|last=Durent|date=9 May 2019}}</ref> He joined [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] in July 2009, at the age of 17.<ref name = "ICT">{{cite web|url=http://ictfc.com/stats/player.php?id=180|title=Profile|access-date=27 March 2014|publisher=Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150912044947/http://ictfc.com/stats/player.php?id=180|archive-date=12 September 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> He made his senior debut for them in the [[Scottish League Cup]] on 1 August 2009, before making his [[Scottish Football League|League debut]] on 26 September 2009.<ref name = "SB">{{soccerbase|51850}}</ref>

Shinnie went on loan to [[Forres Mechanics F.C.|Forres Mechanics]] in the [[Scottish Highland Football League]] in February 2010.<ref name = "ICT"/><ref>{{cite news|title=Home form keeps title hopes alive|url=http://www.inverness-courier.co.uk/Sport/Football/Home-form-keeps-title-hopes-alive-11724.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140328231222/http://www.inverness-courier.co.uk/Sport/Football/Home-form-keeps-title-hopes-alive-11724.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=28 March 2014|publisher=Inverness Courier|date=19 February 2010|access-date=28 March 2014}}</ref> His loan spell was extended until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Winger loan deal blocked|url=http://www.inverness-courier.co.uk/Home/Winger-loan-deal-blocked-5684371.htm|publisher=Inverness Courier|date=16 March 2010|access-date=28 March 2014|archive-date=28 March 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140328231731/http://www.inverness-courier.co.uk/Home/Winger-loan-deal-blocked-5684371.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref> Shinnie was offered a contract extension by Inverness on 30 November 2010,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/i/inverness_ct/9244713.stm|title=Nick Ross and Graeme Shinnie offered Inverness deals|access-date=30 November 2010|date=30 November 2010|publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> agreeing a 3-year deal on 13 December 2010.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/i/inverness_ct/9283522.stm|title=Graeme Shinnie extends contract with Caley Thistle|publisher=BBC Sport|date=13 December 2010|access-date=13 December 2010}}</ref> He suffered an intestinal problem that stopped him from playing between January and August 2011.<ref name = "intestinal">{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/14601610|title=Terry Butcher praises comeback by Graeme Shinnie|publisher=BBC Sport|date=20 August 2011|access-date=20 August 2011}}</ref>

In the [[2011-12 in Scottish football|2011–12 season]], Graeme's brother Andrew joined Inverness on a free transfer from [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Andrew Shinnie and Josh Meekings to join Inverness|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/14032207|publisher=BBC Sport|date=5 July 2011|access-date=26 December 2012}}</ref> Shinnie scored his first goal of his Inverness career on 27 August 2011 in a 2–1 win over [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] and after the match, manager [[Terry Butcher]] expressed delight for Shinnie on his first goal.<ref>{{cite news|title=Terry Butcher delighted for Inverness goal hero Graeme Shinnie after illness almost cut short is career|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/terry-butcher-delighted-for-inverness-goal-1110607|publisher=Daily Record|date=28 August 2011|access-date=26 December 2012}}</ref> Following a 3–1 loss against [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] on 17 September 2011, captain [[Richie Foran]] spoken out about Shinnie, stating he was worthy of pass marks.<ref>{{cite news|title=Inverness CT skipper Richie Foran: Graeme was a Shinnie example to us all |url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/inverness-ct-skipper-richie-foran-1082192|publisher=Daily Record|date=19 September 2011|access-date=26 December 2012}}</ref> After two-months spell out for the side, Shinnie made his return in a 2–1 loss against Rangers on 17 December 2011. Despite the performance, Butcher praised the returning Shinnie and [[Lee Cox (footballer)|Lee Cox]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Butcher praises young duo|url=http://www.inverness-courier.co.uk/Sport/Football/Butcher-praises-young-duo-20122011.htm|archive-url=https://archive.today/20140329004851/http://www.inverness-courier.co.uk/Sport/Football/Butcher-praises-young-duo-20122011.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=29 March 2014|publisher=Inverness Courier|date=20 December 2011|access-date=28 March 2014}}</ref> In December 2012, Shinnie signed a new contract extension, keeping him until 2015,<ref>{{cite news|title=Graeme Shinnie & Josh Meekings sign new Inverness deals|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20837926|publisher=BBC Sport|date=24 December 2012|access-date=26 December 2012}}</ref> having vowed to remain at the club.<ref>{{cite news|title=Inverness ace Graeme Shinnie vows to sign new deal after club stood by him during injury hell |url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/inverness-ace-graeme-shinnie-vows-1501267|publisher=Daily Record|date=22 December 2012|access-date=26 December 2012}}</ref>

In the [[2014 Scottish League Cup Final]], Shinnie played throughout the match until it went to a penalty shoot-out, won by opponents Aberdeen.<ref>{{cite news|title=Aberdeen 0 – 0 Inverness Caledonian Thistle|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/26502621|publisher=BBC Sport|date=16 March 2014|access-date=28 March 2014}}</ref> He was selected in the 2013–14 Premiership [[PFA Scotland Team of the Year]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/27080030|title=Celtic and Dundee United trios in SPFL Premiership team of year|date=18 April 2014|access-date=18 April 2014|publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> In April 2015, Shinnie helped Inverness to reach the [[2015 Scottish Cup Final|Scottish Cup Final]];<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32373835|title=Inverness CT: Graeme Shinnie eyes Scottish Cup-winning finale|date=19 April 2015 |publisher=BBC Sport }}</ref> ''Caley'' went on to win the trophy, beating [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] 2–1 on 30 May 2015, with Shinnie lifting the trophy as captain in his last game for the club.<ref name="cup win"/><ref>{{cite web|title=Graeme Shinnie signs off from Inverness in 'the best way'|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32949340|publisher=BBC Sport|last=Lamont|first=Alasdair|date=31 May 2015|access-date=10 June 2015}}</ref>

=== Aberdeen ===
In January 2015 it was announced that Shinnie had signed a three-year contract with [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]], despite interest from [[Football League Championship]] clubs, and would join the club when the summer transfer window opened in June 2015.<ref>{{cite web|title=Shinnie deal|url=http://www.afc.co.uk/news/5611.php#.VMUDIf1yaAg|website=www.afc.co.uk|access-date=25 January 2015}}</ref> He made his competitive debut for Aberdeen on 2 July 2015, against [[FK Shkëndija]] in the first qualifying round of the [[2015–16 UEFA Europa League#First qualifying round|Europa League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Shkendija 1–1 Aberdeen|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33350986|publisher=BBC Sport|last=Spence|first=Jim|date=2 July 2015|access-date=2 July 2015}}</ref> He scored his first goal for Aberdeen on 9 August 2015, in a 2–0 league win against [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Aberdeen 2–0 Kilmarnock|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33750474|publisher=BBC Sport|last=Davie|first=Scott|date=9 August 2015|access-date=21 September 2015}}</ref>
[[File:GraemeShinnie.jpeg|left|thumb|Shinnie at the [[2018 Scottish League Cup final]].]]
Shinnie signed a new contract with Aberdeen in January 2017, which ran until its expiry in summer 2019.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/38719893 |title=Graeme Shinnie signs Aberdeen contract until 2019 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=23 January 2017 |access-date=23 January 2017}}</ref> In May 2017 he was made team captain, after it was announced that Ryan Jack had signed a pre-contract agreement with [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/15303609.graeme-shinnie-to-replace-ryan-jack-as-aberdeen-captain-for-scottish-cup-final-clash-with-celtic/ |title=Graeme Shinnie to replace Ryan Jack as Aberdeen captain for Scottish Cup final clash with Celtic |first=Alasdair |last=Mackenzie |work=The Herald |date=23 May 2017 |access-date=13 March 2019}}</ref> During his four-year spell at [[Pittodrie Stadium|Pittodrie]], he took part in three finals (the [[2016 Scottish League Cup Final (November)|2016–17]] and [[2018 Scottish League Cup Final|2018–19]] League Cup finals, and the [[2017 Scottish Cup Final]]), losing to [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] on each occasion. In the Premiership, Aberdeen finished runners-up to Celtic three times.<ref name=precon/>

=== Derby County ===
In May 2019 it was announced that Shinnie would join English club [[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]] in July 2019 on a free transfer, signing a three-year contract.<ref name=precon>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48193256|title=Graeme Shinnie: Aberdeen captain signs pre-contract with Derby County|date=7 May 2019|access-date=7 May 2019|publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> He scored his first goal for the club, an injury time winner, against [[Wigan Athletic]] on 23 October 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50064661|title=Derby 1–0 Wigan|website=BBC Sport|date=23 October 2019|access-date=24 October 2019}}</ref>

===Wigan Athletic===
In January 2022 he signed for [[Wigan Athletic F.C.|Wigan Athletic]], for an undisclosed transfer fee, signing a two-and-a-half-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wigantoday.net/sport/football/wigan-athletic-confirm-scottish-ace-capture-3529566|title=Wigan Athletic confirm Scottish ace capture|website=www.wigantoday.net|date=16 January 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/60018092|title=Wigan sign Derby midfielder Shinnie|work=BBC Sport |date=16 January 2022}}</ref>

===Return to Aberdeen===
He returned to [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] on loan in January 2023.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64181482|title=Shinnie returns to Aberdeen on loan from Wigan|work=BBC Sport |date=5 January 2023}}</ref> In June 2023 he signed a permanent three-year contract, and was designated captain.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/66025211|title=Aberdeen re-sign Shinnie as Williams joins on loan|work=BBC Sport |date=28 March 2023}}</ref>

He made his 600th professional appearance on 8 March 2025, scoring a goal, in a Scottish Cup match against Queen's Park.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cly36jgel00o|title=Aberdeen's Graeme Shinnie 'proud' to reach 600 games amid Crohn's battle|date=7 March 2025|website=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c07z177230yt|title=Aberdeen vs Queen's Park: Scottish Cup report, reaction & stats|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

On his 300th appearance for the club in all competitions, Shinnie captained Aberdeen in the [[2025 Scottish Cup final]] which they won on [[Penalty shootout (association football)|penalties]] against Celtic (he was among the four Aberdeen players to score their penalties) for a first win in the competition for 35 years; as well as joining a small group of players to win the trophy with two clubs outside the [[Old Firm]], he became the first man to lift the cup as captain of two different teams.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c4gr652z2d5o|title=Aberdeen win Scottish Cup: 'I could retire today and be a happy man'|date=24 May 2025|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

In May 2026 it was announced that he would leave Aberdeen at the end of his contract the following month.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.afc.co.uk/en/news/captain-graeme-shinnie-to-depart|title=Captain Graeme Shinnie to Depart - Aberdeen FC|website=www.afc.co.uk}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cvgzze5n2y1o |title=Aberdeen: Captain Graeme Shinnie to leave club |website=BBC Sport |date=25 May 2026 |accessdate=25 May 2026}}</ref>

=== Return to Inverness ===
On 26 May 2026, it was announced that Shinnie had signed a pre-contract agreement to re-join Inverness Caledonian Thistle on a two-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-26 |title=Shinnie’s return to Caley Thistle confirmed |url=https://www.inverness-courier.co.uk/sport/shinnie-s-return-to-caley-thistle-confirmed-435995/ |access-date=2026-05-26 |website=Inverness Courier |language=en}}</ref>

== International career ==
Shinnie made his debut for the [[Scotland national under-21 football team]] in April 2012.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/17849719|title=Scotland U21 1–4 Italy U21 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=25 April 2012|access-date=25 April 2012}}</ref> On 29 September 2015, he was called up to the senior squad for games against [[Poland national football team|Poland]] and [[Gibraltar national football team|Gibraltar]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Scotland: Shinnie & Rhodes called up for Euro 2016 qualifiers|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34388353|access-date=29 September 2015|publisher=BBC Sport |date=29 September 2015}}</ref> He was called up again in October 2017,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/41796933|title=Scotland: Interim manager Malky Mackay calls up three new faces for friendly|date=30 October 2017|publisher=BBC Sport }}</ref> and in May 2018.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44111727 |title=Scotland pick Johnny Russell plus seven uncapped players including Lewis Stevenson & Lewis Morgan |publisher=BBC Sport |date=14 May 2018 |access-date=14 May 2018}}</ref>

Shinnie made his full Scotland debut on 29 May 2018, in a 2–0 defeat to Peru.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44219810 |title=Peru 2–0 Scotland |first=Alasdair |last=Lamont |publisher=BBC Sport |date=30 May 2018 |access-date=30 May 2018}}</ref> In March 2019 he was selected to play at left-back in a [[UEFA Euro 2020 qualifying]] match away to [[Kazakhstan national football team|Kazakhstan]], but was at fault for one of the goals as Scotland lost 3–0.<ref name = kazakh/> Afterwards, Shinnie acknowledged that he had performed poorly and would be unlikely to be selected again once [[Andy Robertson]] and [[Kieran Tierney]] were available.<ref name = kazakh>{{cite web |url=https://www.eveningtimes.co.uk/sport/other_football/17519128.graeme-shinnie-blame-me-for-sorry-kazakhstan-debacle-i-wont-get-back-in-the-scotland-team/|title=Graeme Shinnie: Blame me for sorry Kazakhstan debacle – I won't get back in the Scotland team|work=[[Evening Times]]|first=Matthew |last=Lindsay|date=21 March 2019|access-date=23 March 2019 }}</ref> That match was Shnnie's sixth and final appearance for Scotland.<ref>{{SFA Profile|id=59288}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Shinnie is the younger brother of fellow footballer [[Andrew Shinnie]], who joined him at [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness]] in 2011.<ref name = "intestinal"/> The first time that the two brothers faced each other in a competitive game was in a [[2016–17 Scottish Cup]] semi-final, between Andrew's [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] and Graeme's Aberdeen.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/39653101 |title=Hibernian v Aberdeen: Graeme and Andrew Shinnie vie for Scottish Cup final place |publisher=BBC Sport |date=20 April 2017 |access-date=22 April 2017}}</ref> The brothers grew up in [[Cove Bay]] and attended [[Kincorth Academy]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.eveningexpress.co.uk/fp/aberdeen-fc/aberdeen-graeme-andrew-shinnie-scottish-cup/ |title=Aberdeen school pride as Shinnie brothers prepare for first competitive battle |work=Evening Express|date=18 April 2017 |access-date=18 May 2018}}</ref>

Shinnie has [[Crohn's disease]].<ref name="auto"/>

== Playing style ==
Originally a left back at Inverness, Shinnie played primarily as a central midfielder at Aberdeen.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/41897811|title=Scotland call ups a 'laughing stock', says Kris Boyd|date=7 November 2017|publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref>

'''Daniel Gerard Devine''' (born 7 September 1992) is a Northern Irish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)#Centre-back|centre-back]] for {{Scottish football updater|InvernCT}} club [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]].

Devine has previously played for [[Linfield F.C.|Linfield]], [[Preston North End F.C.|Preston North End]], [[Fleetwood Town F.C.|Fleetwood Town]], [[Wrexham A.F.C.|Wrexham]], [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] and [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]].

==Career==
===Club career===
Born in [[Belfast]], Devine played youth football with Lisburn Youth FC, [[Lisburn Distillery F.C.|Lisburn Distillery]] and [[Linfield F.C.|Linfield]]. He made one senior appearance for Linfield in an [[Northern Ireland Football League Cup|Irish League Cup]] game against Portadown on 17 December 2008 <ref>{{cite web|date=17 December 2008|title=Match Report - Linfield 0-1 Portadown|url=https://www.linfieldfc.com/matchreport.aspx?id=531|access-date=18 March 2021|website=Linfield FC official website}}</ref> before moving to [[Preston North End F.C.|Preston North End]] in July 2009.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.pnefc.net/page/YouthsProfiles/0,,10362~1730302,00.html |title=Profile |access-date=30 April 2011 |date=3 February 2010 |publisher=Preston North End F.C. |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120327082447/http://www.pnefc.net/page/YouthsProfiles/0%2C%2C10362~1730302%2C00.html |archive-date=27 March 2012  }}</ref> He made his professional debut for Preston on 30 April 2011 in a 2–1 defeat against [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_div_1/13174361.stm|title=Ipswich 2 – 1 Preston|access-date=30 April 2011|date=30 April 2011|work=BBC Sport|publisher=BBC}}</ref> In June 2011, Devine signed a one-year contract with Preston.<ref>{{cite news|title=Preston North End confirm Paul Hayes departure|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/p/preston/9513442.stm|publisher=BBC |work=BBC Sport|date=15 June 2011|access-date=17 January 2013}}</ref> In May 2012, Devine was released from the club after being told his contract would not be renewed.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.pnefc.net/page/NewsDetail/0,,10362~2766952,00.html |title=Summer Change Programme Underway |publisher=Preston North End FC |work=www.pnefc.net |date=10 May 2012 |access-date=10 May 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120513021541/http://www.pnefc.net/page/NewsDetail/0%2C%2C10362~2766952%2C00.html |archive-date=13 May 2012  }}</ref>

He joined [[Fleetwood Town F.C.|Fleetwood Town]] in the summer of 2012, moving on loan to [[Wrexham A.F.C.|Wrexham]] in September 2012.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.dailypost.co.uk/sport-news/wrexham-fc/2012/09/18/wrexham-fc-sign-danny-devine-on-loan-until-christmas-55578-31855340/|title=Wrexham FC sign Danny Devine on loan until Christmas|work=Daily Post|date=18 September 2012|access-date=18 September 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121020131853/http://www.dailypost.co.uk/sport-news/wrexham-fc/2012/09/18/wrexham-fc-sign-danny-devine-on-loan-until-christmas-55578-31855340/|archive-date=20 October 2012}}</ref> Wrexham offered Devine a permanent long-term contract, but he chose to join [[Scottish Premier League]] side [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]], citing his desire to work with manager [[Terry Butcher]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20832455|title=Wrexham miss out on defender Danny Devine|work=BBC Sport|publisher=BBC|date=3 January 2013|access-date=4 January 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20907073 |first=Heather |last=Dewar |title=Inverness: Danny Devine agrees contract after Wrexham exit|work=BBC Sport|publisher=BBC|date=3 January 2013|access-date=4 January 2013}}</ref> After Butcher turned down the chance to join [[Barnsley F.C.|Barnsley]], Devine said he was relieved that Butcher chose to stay, as Butcher was one of the reasons why he turned down clubs in England.<ref>{{cite news|title=Inverness: Danny Devine happy at Terry Butcher decision |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20980465|work=BBC Sport|publisher=BBC|date=10 January 2013|access-date=17 January 2013}}</ref>

In March 2013, Devine signed a contract extension, keeping him at the club until the end of the 2014–15 season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Defender Danny Devine agrees Inverness CT contract|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/21806184|work=BBC Sport |publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation |date=15 March 2013 |access-date=15 March 2013|first=Heather |last=Dewar}}</ref> A suspension to [[Gary Warren (footballer)|Gary Warren]] meant that Devine played for Inverness in their [[2015 Scottish Cup Final]] victory.<ref name = "cup final"/> Soon afterwards, Devine signed a new one-year contract with the club.<ref name = "cup final">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33033661 |title=Inverness: Danny Devine secures new Caley Thistle contract |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=5 June 2015 |access-date=6 June 2015}}</ref>

Devine left Inverness in 2016 and was then signed by [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] on a two-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://ptfc.co.uk/news/2016-2017/june_2016/daniel_devine_signs_two_year_deal|title=Daniel Devine signs two year deal|access-date=16 June 2016|publisher=Partick Thistle F.C.|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160620083147/http://ptfc.co.uk/news/2016-2017/june_2016/daniel_devine_signs_two_year_deal|archive-date=20 June 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> Thistle were relegated via the playoffs at the end of the 2017–18 season. Following that relegation, Devine was one of many players released by Thistle.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/playing-squad-update/ |title=Playing squad update |date=25 May 2018 |access-date=25 May 2018 |website=www.ptfc.co.uk|publisher=Partick Thistle FC}}</ref>

Devine then signed with [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/article/list-of-spfl-summer-signings/ |title=List of SPFL summer signings |publisher=SPFL |date=6 June 2018 |access-date=6 June 2018 |archive-date=12 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612140006/https://spfl.co.uk/news/article/list-of-spfl-summer-signings/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> Devine was released after two seasons with Dunfermline, and subsequently re-signed for fellow Championship side Inverness Caledonian Thistle in August 2020 on a two-year deal.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ictfc.com/danny-devine-signs-for-ictfc |title=Danny Devine Signs For ICTFC |publisher=Inverness Caledonian Thistle FC |date=17 August 2020 |access-date=17 August 2020}}</ref>

===International career===
Devine represented Northern Ireland at youth international level.<ref name = "sectarian"/><ref name = "NIFG">[https://nifootball.blogspot.co.uk/2010/11/daniel-devine.html Northern Ireland profile] at NIFG</ref> In May 2011 the BBC reported that then Northern Ireland manager [[Nigel Worthington]] had been informed by Devine that he intended to switch his allegiance to the Republic of Ireland.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/13424369|title=NI poised to lose Devine and Ferguson to Republic|access-date=18 May 2011|date=18 May 2011|publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> In March 2018, the then Northern Ireland manager [[Michael O'Neill (footballer)|Michael O'Neill]] said that he would have selected Devine in his Northern Ireland squad for [[UEFA Euro 2016]], but was unable to do so because Devine had signed an international transfer form which committed him to the Republic.<ref name = "sectarian">{{cite web |url=https://www.msn.com/en-ie/sport/football/northern-irish-boss-claims-fai-use-'sectarian'-tactics/ar-BBJQyR5?ocid=st |title=Northern Irish boss claims FAI use 'sectarian' tactics |first=Philip |last=Quinn |work=Extra.ie |date=4 March 2018 |access-date=5 March 2018}}</ref>

'''Kevin Holt''' (born 25 January 1993) is a Scottish professional footballer who plays as a [[Defender (association football)#Full-back|left-back]] and also a [[Defender (association football)|centre-back]] for [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]]. Holt started his career with local side [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]] before playing for [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] and [[Cyprus|Cypriot]] side [[Pafos FC|Pafos]], then returning to ''The Doonhamers''. After another stint in Cyprus with [[Ermis Aradippou FC|Ermis Aradippou]], Holt spent two seasons with [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] before signing with [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]].

==Playing career==
===Queen of the South (First spell)===
Holt joined Queen of the South in August 2010 and began playing for their Under-19 squad.<ref name="Holt_Profile">{{cite news |title=Kevin Holt Profile |url=https://www.qosfc.com/players |work=qosfc.com |publisher=[[Queen of the South F.C.]]|accessdate=27 September 2011 }}</ref> In June 2011, Holt was awarded the Jade Moore Memorial Trophy for being Queens under-19s player of the season.<ref>{{cite news |title=Queens under 19s awards |url=http://www.dgstandard.co.uk/dumfries-sport/dumfries-football/queen-of-south-fc/2011/06/08/queens-under-19s-awards-51311-28835140/ |work=[[Dumfries & Galloway Standard]] |publisher=Scottish & Universal Newspapers Limited |date=8 June 2011 |accessdate=3 December 2011 }}</ref> Holt debuted for the first-team on 17 September 2011, appearing as a substitute in a 4–1 victory versus [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]] in a [[Scottish Football League First Division|Scottish First Division]] fixture replacing hat-trick scorer [[Kevin Smith (footballer, born 1987)|Kevin Smith]].<ref name="Holt_SFL">{{cite news|title=Holt stays on at Palmerston |url=http://www.scottishfootballleague.com/news/article/holt-stays-on-at-palmerston/ |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130202034309/http://www.scottishfootballleague.com/news/article/holt-stays-on-at-palmerston/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=2 February 2013 |work=scottishfootballleague.com |publisher=Scottish Football League |date=28 December 2011 |accessdate=4 June 2012 }}</ref>

Holt made his first senior start on 12 November 2011, versus [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] in a goalless home draw.<ref name="Holt_SFL"/> Holt was sent off versus [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] in December 2011 and this was his first ever [[Misconduct (association football)#Sending-off offences (red card)|dismissal]].<ref name="Holt_SFL"/> Holt's debut in the [[Scottish Cup]] was in a 1–0 away win versus the ''Maryhill Magyars'' on 7 January 2012 with the goal scored by [[Dan Carmichael]].<ref name="Cup_Debut"/> This was Queens first win in the competition since their 4–3 semi-final win versus [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] in 2008 at [[Hampden Park]].<ref name="Cup_Debut">{{cite news|title=Partick Thistle 0 – 1 Queen of the South |url=http://qosfc.com/new_report.aspx?fixtureid=537 |work=qosfc.com |publisher=[[Queen of the South F.C.]] |date=7 January 2012 |accessdate=8 January 2012 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120119032932/http://www.qosfc.com/new_report.aspx?fixtureid=537 |archivedate=19 January 2012 }}</ref> At the end of the [[2011–12 Scottish First Division|2011–12]] season Queens were relegated to the [[Scottish Football League Second Division|Scottish Second Division]] but despite this Holt remained with the club, having signed a new contract in December 2011.<ref>{{cite news |title=Queens' star man Robinson in no hurry to leave Palmerston |url=http://www.dgstandard.co.uk/dumfries-sport/dumfries-football/queen-of-south-fc/2012/05/11/queens-star-man-robinson-in-no-hurry-to-leave-palmerston-51311-30942104/ |work=[[Dumfries & Galloway Standard]] |publisher=Scottish & Universal Newspapers Limited |date=11 May 2012 |accessdate=4 June 2012 }} Holt signed for Steven Pressley's Cypriot First Division team, Pafos FC</ref> He scored 6 goals in 137 competitive QoS first team games.<ref name=base>{{Cite web|url=https://www.soccerbase.com/players/player.sd?player_id=58191|title=Kevin Holt | Football Stats | Dundee United | Age 32 | Soccer Base|website=www.soccerbase.com}}</ref>

===Dundee===
In May 2015, Holt signed a pre-contract with [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] and the move was completed during the summer of 2015.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dundee sign Queen of the South's Kevin Holt on a pre-contract|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32786220|publisher=BBC Sport|date=18 May 2015}}</ref> After three seasons with Dundee, Holt was released at the end of the [[2017-18 in Scottish football|2017-18]] season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/player-update/ |title=Player update |publisher=Dundee FC |date=16 May 2018 |accessdate=16 May 2018}}</ref> Holt scored 8 goals in 113 competitive first-team matches for the ''Dee''.<ref name=base/>

===Pafos===
On 9 June 2018, after being released by [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]], Holt signed for [[Cyprus|Cypriot]] club [[Pafos FC|Pafos]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.pressreader.com/uk/the-courier-advertiser-fife-edition/20180609/282565903838973 |title=Pafos move for former Dark Blues Defender |work=The Courier |date=9 June 2018 |accessdate=9 June 2018}}</ref> 
Pafos ended their 22 matches in eighth position out of twelve clubs and entered the league's relegation section.<ref name=cyp>{{Cite web|url=https://cyprus-mail.com/cyprus-football-highlights-2018-2019-2/|title=404 - Page not found | Cyprus Mail|website=cyprus-mail.com|access-date=6 May 2019|archive-date=30 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190330220122/https://cyprus-mail.com/cyprus-football-highlights-2018-2019-2/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Queen of the South (Second spell)===
On 27 May 2019, Holt signed for [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]] for a second spell on a two-year contract.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.qosfc.com/news-4577 | title=QosFC: Holt Returns to Queens }}</ref> The club announced Holt's departure from the club in September 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=11 September 2020|title=Kevin Holt Departs|url=https://www.qosfc.com/news-5208|access-date=11 September 2020|website=qosfc.com}}</ref>

===Ermis Aradippou===
On 11 September 2020, Holt returned to [[Cyprus]] to sign for [[Ermis Aradippou FC|Ermis Aradippou]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=11 September 2020|title=Transfer News LIVE: 11 September 2020|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/transfer-news-live-celtic-rangers-22664801|access-date=11 September 2020|website=Daily Record}}</ref>

===Partick Thistle===
Holt signed a two-year deal with Scottish Championship club [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] in May 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/signing-news-kevin-holt-pens-two-year-contract/|title = Signing News: Kevin Holt pens two-year contract}}</ref>
Holt scored his first goal for Thistle, heading in from a corner, in a 3-0 away win against Dunfermline.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58036534|title=Two wins from two for Partick Thistle|work=BBC Sport}}</ref>

Holt finished the 2022–23 season having scored nine goals that season for Thistle, the highest return of his career in an individual season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://twitter.com/thistlearchive/status/1662747917231308801?s=46&t=4F4JIh7SqgH4ETcXZ7u2Rg|title=x.com}}</ref>

During his second season with Thistle, Holt was part of the squad that made it to the Scottish Premiership promotion play off final, which Thistle eventually lost on penalties to Ross County, meaning the club remained in the Scottish Championship. Following this Holt left the club.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/trio-leave-partick-thistle/ | title=Trio leave Partick Thistle }}</ref>

===Dundee United===
In June 2023, Holt signed a one-year deal with [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=KEVIN HOLT PENS TANNADICE DEAL |url=https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/news/7888/KEVIN-HOLT-PENS-TANNADICE-DEAL.html |access-date=2023-06-26 |website=Dundee United Football Club |language=en}}</ref>

===Derry City===
On 22 February 2025, he signed for [[League of Ireland Premier Division]] club [[Derry City F.C.|Derry City]] on a two-year-contract, for a fee understood to be £40,000 plus add-ons, with [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] stating that he had threatened to make himself unavailable for selection for the rest of his contract should they try to block the move from taking place.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.derrycityfc.net/2025/02/deadline-deal-as-city-sign-holt/|title=Deadline Deal as City Sign Holt|date=22 February 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.derryjournal.com/sport/football/derry-city-closing-in-on-transfer-deadline-day-move-for-dundee-united-defender-kevin-holt-5003013|title=Dundee United defender set to complete deadline day move to Derry City|date=22 February 2025|website=Derry Journal}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/soccer/league-of-ireland/dundee-united-would-like-to-place-on-record-our-disappointment-after-first-choice-defender-kevin-holt-moves-to-derry-city/a476799899.html|title=Dundee United 'would like to place on record our disappointment' after first choice defender Kevin Holt moves to Derry City|date=23 February 2025|website=www.independent.ie}}</ref>

===Ayr United===
Holt returned to Scotland in July 2025, signing a two year deal with Scottish Championship club [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]] for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{Cite web | title=Archived copy | url=https://x.com/ayrunitedfc/status/1945847224291774969?s=46&t=4F4JIh7SqgH4ETcXZ7u2Rg | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251208092020/https://x.com/ayrunitedfc/status/1945847224291774969?s=46&t=4F4JIh7SqgH4ETcXZ7u2Rg | archive-date=2025-12-08}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Kevin Holt is the son of the Dumfries born footballer Gordon Holt. Gordon played for [[Kello Rovers F.C.|Kello Rovers]] in the [[Scottish Junior Football Association|Scottish Junior]] ranks before turning professional when he played for [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]] during the [[1986–87 in Scottish football|1986-87]] season and then for [[Stranraer F.C.|Stranraer]] during the [[1987–88 in Scottish football|1987-88]] season.<ref>{{Cite web| title=Gordon Holt | url=http://www.neilbrown.newcastlefans.com/player4/gordonholt.html | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304072510/http://www.neilbrown.newcastlefans.com/player4/gordonholt.html | archive-date=2016-03-04}}</ref>

In 2011, Holt was studying for a career in banking.<ref name="Holt_Profile"/>

'''Liam Dick''' (born 19 August 1995) is a Scottish professional footballer who plays for [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]].

==Career==
A member of [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]]'s Under 19 team,<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.falkirkfc.co.uk/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=4747&Itemid=473 | title=Under 19 Squad 2011–12 Season | publisher=[[Falkirk F.C.]] | work=Falkirk News | accessdate=17 October 2011}}</ref> Dick made his first team debut as a substitute in Falkirk's win over [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] on penalties in the [[Scottish League Cup]] on 25 October 2011.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/15346253 | title=Dundee Utd 2 – 2 Falkirk | publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation | work=BBC Sport | date=25 October 2011 | access-date=28 October 2011}}</ref> In the last game of the season, he made his league debut, coming on as a substitute towards the end of the 3–2 win over [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]].<ref name="soccerbase"/> In January 2013, Dick, along with [[Ryan McGeever]], signed with Falkirk until 2016.<ref>{{cite news|title=Falkirk have secured new contracts with midfielder Liam Dick and defender Ryan McGeever|url=https://www1.skysports.com/football/news/12691/8380631/Falkirk-have-secured-new-contracts-with-midfielder-Liam-Dick-and-defender-Ryan-McGeever|publisher=Sky Sports|date=4 January 2013|accessdate=21 January 2013}}</ref>

In November 2015, Dick signed a short-term loan deal with [[Scottish League One]] side [[Stranraer F.C.|Stranraer]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Dick joins Stranraer on loan |url=http://spfl.co.uk/news/article/dick-joins-stranraer-on-loan/ |publisher=SPFL |date=10 November 2015 |accessdate=10 November 2015}}</ref> After impressing in his performances for Stranrer, on 4 January 2016, he signed an extension to keep him on loan at [[Stair Park]] until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Willie Gibson Signs & Latest Squad Updates|url=http://www.stranraerfc.org/index.php/latest-news/429-squad-updates-4-01-15 |publisher=stranraerfc.org |date=4 January 2016 |accessdate=5 January 2016}}</ref> In June 2016, Dick signed for Stranraer on a permanent basis.<ref>{{cite web|title=LIAM DICK JOINS STRANRAER|url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/liam-dick-joins-stranraer|publisher=Scottish Professional Football League|date=6 June 2016|accessdate=12 August 2019}}</ref>

After two-and-a-half seasons at Stair Park, he agreed to join [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]] on 1 January 2018.<ref>{{cite web |last=Findlay |first=Alan |title=Signing news: Liam Dick agrees terms |url=http://www.dumbartonfootballclub.com/news/?mode=view&id=3375 |publisher=Dumbarton FC |date=31 December 2017 |accessdate=31 December 2017}}</ref> After the Sons relegation to League One, Dick turned down a new deal and left the club in May 2018<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.dumbartonfootballclub.com/news/?mode=view&id=3635|title=DEFENDER MOVES ON|last=Findlay|first=Alan|date=30 May 2018|website=Dumbarton Football Club}}</ref>

Dick then signed for [[Alloa Athletic F.C.|Alloa Athletic]] in July 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.alloaathletic.co.uk/BlogView.aspx?pageid=2&ItemID=1811&mid=2|title=Manager brings in three|date=12 July 2018|website=Alloa Athletic FC}}</ref> In June 2021, he joined [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.raithrovers.net/liam-dick-signs-for-raith-rovers/ |title=Liam Dick Signs For Raith Rovers |publisher=Raith Rovers F.C. |date=7 June 2021 }}</ref> In May 2023, he signed a new contract until the end of the 2023–24 season,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.raithrovers.net/liam-dick-signs-on/ |title=Liam Dick signs on |publisher=Raith Rovers F.C. |date=16 May 2023 }}</ref> and in June 2024, he extended his contract until 2025.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.raithrovers.net/liam-dick-extends-contract/ |title=Liam Dick extends contract |publisher=Raith Rovers F.C. |date=6 June 2024 }}</ref>

'''Anthony Paul Watt''' (born 29 December 1993) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[forward (association football)|forward]] for [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]].

He was a product of the [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrie United]] youth academy before joining [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] in 2011, where he scored the winning goal in a [[Celtic F.C. 2–1 FC Barcelona|2–1 win over FC Barcelona]] in the [[2012–13 UEFA Champions League]].

Watt fell out of favour at Celtic and spent the 2013–14 season on loan at [[Belgian Pro League]] club [[Lierse S.K. (1906)|Lierse]]. He signed for another Belgian club, [[Standard Liège]], in the summer of 2014. He returned to the UK in January 2015 to join [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]]. Charlton loaned Watt to [[Cardiff City F.C.|Cardiff City]], [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]] and [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]]. Watt then had another stint in Belgian football with [[Oud-Heverlee Leuven|OH Leuven]], before returning to Scotland with [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] in July 2018.

After a spell with Bulgarian club [[PFC CSKA Sofia|CSKA Sofia]], Watt signed for [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] in February 2020. He then joined Dundee United in January 2022.

Watt represented Scotland at various youth levels and has played for the [[Scotland national football team|Scotland national team]] once, in March 2016.
