===Celtic===
[[File:Tony Watt 20130421.jpg|upright|thumb|Watt at Celtic Park in 2013]]
Several clubs including [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] and [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]] showed interest in signing Watt during the 2011 [[January transfer window]]. After a trial with [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] and a week's training with Liverpool, Watt was signed by his boyhood heroes [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] on 4 January, for a reported fee of £80,000 and future payments dependent on his first-team progression.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/celtic/9221363/Airdrie-United-set-to-earn-20000-Tony-Watt-windfall.html |title=Airdrie United set to earn £20,000 Tony Watt windfall |work=[[The Daily Telegraph]] |date=23 April 2012 |access-date=24 April 2012}}</ref> He signed a three-year contract.<ref name="KelvinWilson">{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/c/celtic/9349975.stm |title=Celtic hope for early Kelvin Wilson switch from Forest |publisher=BBC Sport |date=8 January 2011 |access-date=8 April 2012}}</ref> Watt made his Celtic debut on 22 April 2012 in a 3–0 win over [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]]. He scored two goals within five minutes of coming on as a substitute.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/17718161 |title=Motherwell 0–3 Celtic |publisher=BBC Sport |date=22 April 2012 |access-date=22 April 2012}}</ref>

On 25 August 2012, Watt made his first start for Celtic scoring two goals in their 4–2 away win against [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness]]. He made his [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] debut on 7 November 2012, coming on as a second-half substitute for [[Mikael Lustig]] and scoring in the 83rd minute in a [[Celtic F.C. 2–1 FC Barcelona|2–1 home win]] against [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Alasdair |last=Lamont |title=Celtic 2–1 Barcelona |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20150451 | publisher=[[BBC]] Sport |date=7 November 2012 |access-date=8 November 2012}}</ref> Four days later, he came off the subs bench to score again, this time in a 1–1 draw against [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] in the league.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fitbastats.com/celtic/game.php?gameid=84827 |title=Celtic 1–1 Vs St Johnstone in Scottish League (11/11/2012) |publisher=FitbaStats |access-date=11 February 2015}}</ref> On 15 November 2012, Watt signed a new contract extending his stay with [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] until 2016.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20344778 |title=Tony Watt signs new Celtic contract until 2016 | publisher=[[BBC]] Sport |date=15 November 2012 |access-date=15 November 2012}}</ref> Watt made a further 14 appearances for Celtic that season, mostly coming on as a substitute, and did not score any more goals.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fitbastats.com/celtic/player_games.php?playerid=3069&page=2 |title=Games involving Watt, Tony in Season 2012/2013 |publisher=FitbaStats |access-date=11 February 2015}}</ref> He did however win his first major honour as Celtic won their 44th [[List of Scottish football champions|league championship]] title in May 2013; his 20 league appearances over the season entitling him to a league winner's medal.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fitbastats.com/celtic/player.php?playerid=3069 |publisher=FitbaStats |access-date=11 February 2015 |title=Watt, Tony}}</ref>

====Lierse (loan)====
Celtic qualified for the [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] group stage and signed two new strikers, [[Amido Baldé]] and [[Teemu Pukki]], minimising Watt's opportunities at [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]].<ref name = "lierse loan"/> On 31 August 2013, Watt moved to [[Belgian Pro League]] club [[Lierse S.K. (1906)|Lierse S.K.]] on a season long loan deal for the 2013–14 season.<ref name = "lierse loan">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23919537|title=Celtic striker Tony Watt joins Lierse SK on loan |publisher=BBC Sport |date=1 September 2013 |access-date=1 September 2013}}</ref> In September 2013, the young striker was brought on as a substitute against [[K.V. Kortrijk|Kortrijk]] in his debut for Lierse and, within 90 seconds of being on the field, he scored with his second touch of the ball.<ref>{{cite web|last=Lindsay|first=Matthew|title=Lennon says Watt will learn in Lierse|url=http://www.eveningtimes.co.uk/celtic/lennon-says-watt-will-learn-in-lierse-137225n.22231587|work=Evening Times|access-date=28 December 2013|date=24 September 2013}}</ref> Despite this, Watt was branded lazy and unfit by Lierse boss [[Stanley Menzo]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Wright|first=Angus|title=Tony Watt branded lazy and unfit by loan club boss|url=http://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/spfl/tony-watt-branded-lazy-and-unfit-by-loan-club-boss-1-3107023|publisher=Scotland on Sunday|access-date=28 December 2013|date=23 September 2013}}</ref> In response, Watt pulled off his shirt after scoring against [[Lommel United]] a few days later in the [[Belgian Cup]] resulting in a yellow card. Watt explained: "I just wanted to show that I am not fat. I knew perfectly well that if I took my top off I would get a yellow card – it happens all over the world but I just wanted to show everyone that I am in prime condition. I am not too fat and I wanted to prove this."<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/spfl/celtic-s-tony-watt-hits-back-over-lierse-fat-jibes-1-3114947 |title=Celtic's Tony Watt hits back over Lierse fat jibes |work=The Scotsman |access-date=11 February 2015 |date=27 September 2013 |last=Walker |first=Mark}}</ref>

Watt struggled to hold down a first team place thereafter, and was sent off on 2 November 2013, within a minute of coming on as a second-half substitute against [[R. Charleroi S.C.|Charleroi]], however the red card was later rescinded.<ref>{{cite web|title=Celtic's Tony Watt sent off within 40 seconds of coming on for Lierse v Sporting Charleroi|url=http://www.101greatgoals.com/blog/celtics-tony-watt-sent-off-within-40-seconds-of-coming-on-for-lierse-v-sporting-charleroi-video/|publisher=101 Great Goals|access-date=28 December 2013|date=3 November 2013}}</ref> A week later, Watt was sent home from training after a row with manager Stanley Menzo.<ref>{{cite web|last=Askew|first=Carl|title=Celtic starlet Tony Watt turfed out of training in Belgium after bust-up with coach|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/celtic-starlet-tony-watt-turfed-2790304|work=Daily Record|location=Glasgow|access-date=28 December 2013|date=14 November 2013}}</ref> He was then again publicly criticised by Menzo in December 2013, with the manager stating he would not take him back from Scotland for the second half of the season. However, Watt was recalled to the side on [[Boxing Day]] and scored twice against [[KV Mechelen|Mechelen]] in a 3–0 win. Menzo commented afterwards about Watt, "Today I am glad we have him but tomorrow I might want to murder him! That's just how it is with him."<ref>{{cite web|last=Swan|first=Craig|title=Neil Lennon brands teenage striker Tony Watt immature and warns on-loan Bhoy it's time to grow up and become a man|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/neil-lennon-brands-teenage-striker-2965413|work=Daily Record|location=Glasgow|access-date=28 December 2013|date=28 December 2013}}</ref>
Watt travelled with Lierse to Portugal in January 2014 for a mid-season friendly match against Dutch side [[SC Heerenveen|Heerenveen]], with the striker scoring both of his side's goals in a 2–3 defeat.<ref>{{cite web|title=Heerenveen klopt Lierse met 3–2 in oefenduel|url=http://www.hln.be/hln/nl/7836/Lierse/article/detail/1772052/2014/01/10/Heerenveen-klopt-Lierse-met-3-2-in-oefenduel.dhtml|publisher=HLN 24U Nieus & Sport|access-date=10 January 2014|date=10 January 2014}}</ref>

Despite manager Stanley Menzo's earlier threats, Watt remained with Lierse for the second half of the season. He started for Lierse on 18 January 2014 away against [[K.V. Kortrijk|Kortrijk]] and scored twice in a 4–3 win for his side.<ref>{{cite web|title=Kortrijk – Lierse Game Result, Statistics and Goals 25/01/2014|url=http://fussball.wettpoint.com/en/games/1392512.html|publisher=Fussball Datenbank|access-date=26 January 2014}}</ref> Watt continued his run of impressive form on 31 January, scoring with a 20-yard shot in a surprise 2–0 win for Lierse over reigning Belgian champions [[R.S.C. Anderlecht|Anderlecht]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Lierse SK 2 Anderlecht 0|url=http://m.live.sporza.be/cm/lmc.mobile/2.28512/speeldag24/1.1852772|publisher=Live Sproza|access-date=2 February 2014|date=31 January 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=McHugh|first=Joe|title=Watt scores against Anderlecht as Lierse win 2–0|url=http://videocelts.com/2014/02/blogs/loan-celts/watt-scores-against-anderlecht-as-lierse-win-2-0-video|publisher=Video Celts|access-date=2 February 2014|date=1 February 2014}}</ref> The relationship between Watt and manager Stanley Menzo remained volatile though. In February 2014 Watt stated that he loved Lierse and Belgium,<ref>{{cite web|title=Are Celtic about to lose their next big striking sensation in Tony Watt?|url=http://metro.co.uk/2014/02/13/are-celtic-about-to-lose-their-next-big-striking-sensation-in-tony-watt-4301239/|publisher=Metro|access-date=11 March 2014|date=13 February 2014}}</ref> however after losing his starting place in the team again during March 2014, he complained to the media that "Whenever we lose, Menzo blames me" and added that "Actually, it's his fault."<ref>{{cite web|title=He Always Blames Me! Celtic Striker Tony Watt Blasts Lierse Coach Stanley Menzo|url=http://www.insidefutbol.com/2014/03/11/he-always-blames-me-celtic-striker-tony-watt-blasts-lierse-coach-stanley-menzo/131211/|publisher=Inside Futbol|access-date=11 March 2014|date=11 March 2014}}</ref> Lierse responded to Watt's comments by demoting him from the first-team squad to their 'B' squad.<ref>{{cite web|last=McPartlin|first=Patrick|title=Tony Watt demoted to Lierse 'B team'|url=http://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/latest/tony-watt-demoted-to-lierse-b-team-1-3339785|work=The Scotsman|access-date=14 March 2014|date=13 March 2014}}</ref> Watt did not play for Lierse again, and returned to Celtic at the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Belgians await a decision from Celtic as new bid comes in for striker Tony Watt|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-transfer-news/belgians-await-decision-celtic-new-3516609|work=Daily Record|location=Glasgow|access-date=14 May 2014|date=9 May 2014}}</ref>

===Standard Liège===
After his loan spell in the country, a number of top Belgian clubs were reported to be showing an interest in signing Watt permanently.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://hereisthecity.com/en-gb/2014/05/09/celtics-barcelona-hero-edges-ever-closer-to-parkhead-exit/ |access-date=4 March 2015 |publisher=Here Is The City |title=Celtic's Barcelona hero edges ever closer to Parkhead exit |date=9 May 2014 |first=Jack |last=Beresford}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11781/9354345/transfer-news-celtic-striker-tony-watt-aware-of-interest-in-his-services |title=Transfer news: Celtic striker Tony Watt aware of interest in his services |publisher=Sky Sports |date=19 June 2014 |access-date=4 March 2015}}</ref> Watt left Celtic in July 2014 for a reported fee of £1.2 million, signing a five-year contract with Belgian club [[Standard Liège]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11095/9398349/transfer-news-tony-watt-has-joined-standard-liege-on-a-five-year-deal |title=Transfer news: Tony Watt has joined Standard Liège on a five-year deal |publisher=Sky Sports |date=28 July 2014 |access-date=28 July 2014}}</ref> He made his debut on 2 August 2014, coming on as a second-half substitute in a 3–2 league win away against [[K.V. Kortrijk|Kortrijk]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Kortrijk vs. Standard Liège 2 – 3|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2014/08/02/belgium/pro-league/kv-kortrijk/standard-de-liege/1696901/|work=Soccerway|access-date=7 August 2014}}</ref> Watt made his next appearance three days later, again as a second-half substitute, this time in a 2–1 away win against [[Panathinaikos F.C.|Panathinaikos]] in the [[2014–15 UEFA Champions League qualifying phase and play-off round|Champions League]] qualifying rounds.<ref>{{cite web|title=Panathinaikos vs. Standard Liège 1 – 2|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2014/08/05/europe/uefa-champions-league/panathinaikos-fc/standard-de-liege/1802631/|work=Soccerway|access-date=7 August 2014}}</ref> However, Watt failed to make much impact and by the end of December 2014 had scored only three goals with most of his appearances being as a substitute.<ref name="SOC" />

===Charlton Athletic===
The Addicks confirmed the signing of Watt on 6 January 2015. "He's a guy who can score goals, he has a lot of pace, especially round the back of the defence, and although he's only 21 he has a lot of experience already and has played in the Champions League" manager [[Bob Peeters]] said.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Kyle|first1=Gregor|title=Former Celtic striker Tony Watt signs for Charlton Athletic|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-transfer-news/former-celtic-striker-tony-watt-4928833|work=Daily Record|location=Glasgow|access-date=6 January 2015|date=6 January 2014}}</ref> Watt scored his first goal for Charlton in a 3–2 loss at home against [[Norwich F.C.|Norwich]] on 10 February 2015.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jerome earns Norwich a late 3–2 win at battling Charlton|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/live/match/314122/report|publisher=Sky Sports|access-date=11 February 2015|date=10 February 2015}}</ref> Four days later, Watt helped Charlton end a 13-game winless run in the league with a 3–0 victory over [[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]]. Watt did not score but turned in an outstanding performance which included an assist for Charlton's second goal, earning him the man of the match award.<ref>{{cite web|title=Charlton 3 – 0 Brentford|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31423238|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=27 February 2015|date=14 February 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Virtue|first=Rob|title=Charlton 3 Brentford 0 – Watt leads charge as Addicks end winless run|url=http://www.wharf.co.uk/2015/02/charlton-brentford.html|publisher=Wharf|access-date=27 February 2015|date=14 February 2015}}</ref> On 28 February, Watt scored a [[2 (number)#In sports|brace]] in a 3–0 win against [[Huddersfield Town A.F.C.|Huddersfield]] at [[The Valley (London)|The Valley]] in an impressive performance by both Charlton and Watt.<ref>{{cite web|last=Wright|first=Nick|title=Charlton turn on the style for sell-out crowd as Tony Watt downs Chris Powell's Huddersfield|url=http://www.london24.com/sport/football/clubs/charlton/charlton_turn_on_the_style_for_sell_out_crowd_as_tony_watt_downs_chris_powell_s_huddersfield_1_3974399|publisher=London 24|access-date=2 March 2015|date=28 February 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402184404/http://www.london24.com/sport/football/clubs/charlton/charlton_turn_on_the_style_for_sell_out_crowd_as_tony_watt_downs_chris_powell_s_huddersfield_1_3974399|archive-date=2 April 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> For the remainder of the season he formed a formidable partnership with fellow striker [[Igor Vetokele]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Mendez|first=Louis|title=Addicks midfielder full of admiration for strike partnership|url=http://www.newsshopper.co.uk/sport/11826921.Addicks_midfielder_full_of_admiration_for_strike_partnership/|work=News Shopper|access-date=2 March 2015|date=2 March 2015}}</ref>

Watt scored three goals for Charlton during the first month of [[2015–16 Charlton Athletic F.C. season|2015–16]],<ref name="wonline">{{cite news|last=Gaskell|first=Simon|title=Cardiff City signing Tony Watt hits out at 'false reasons' for Charlton exit as he admits nerves over Bluebirds move|url=http://www.walesonline.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/cardiff-city-signing-tony-watt-10500264|access-date=24 October 2017|work=Wales Onlinw|date=25 November 2015}}</ref> but as the season progressed and amidst a combination of injuries and rumours of a row at training, he became a more peripheral figure at the club.<ref name="wonline" /><ref>{{cite news|last=O'Keefe|first=Chris|title=Team News: Tony Watt, Igor Vetokele return for Rotherham clash|url=https://www.sportsmole.co.uk/football/charlton-athletic/team-news/team-news-watt-vetokele-return-for-rotherham-clash_245584.html|access-date=24 October 2017|work=Sports Mole|date=12 September 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Langshaw|first=Mark|title=Team News: Gary Hooper handed first Sheffield Wednesday start at Charlton Athletic|url=https://www.sportsmole.co.uk/football/charlton-athletic/team-news/team-news-gary-hooper-handed-first-sheff-weds-start_256299.html|access-date=24 October 2017|work=Sports Mole|date=7 November 2015}}</ref>

====Cardiff City (loan)====
On 23 November 2015, Watt was loaned to [[Cardiff City F.C.|Cardiff City]], until 16 January 2016,<ref>{{Cite news |title=Tony Watt joins Cardiff City on loan until January |url=http://www.cafc.co.uk/news/article/charlton-athletic-tony-watt-cardiff-city-2814200.aspx |publisher=Charlton Athletic FC |date=23 November 2015 |access-date=23 November 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151124011302/http://www.cafc.co.uk/news/article/charlton-athletic-tony-watt-cardiff-city-2814200.aspx |archive-date=24 November 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref> he later made his debut during a 2–2 draw with [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]] and scored his first goal the following game against [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Bolton 2–3 Cardiff |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34951378 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=5 December 2015 |access-date=5 December 2015}}</ref> Cardiff were hit with a transfer embargo for the January transfer window, following a breach of financial fair play rules, meaning they could not sign Watt on a permanent deal. He returned to Charlton after they rejected an extension to the loan deal, making nine appearances and scoring twice in the Welsh capital.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Tony Watt: Cardiff City fail to extend Charlton striker loan |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35333530 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=16 January 2016 |access-date=16 January 2016}}</ref>

====Blackburn Rovers (loan)====
On 29 January 2016, Watt was loaned to [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]], until the end of the 2015–16 season, with a fee already agreed for a permanent move in the Summer of 2016. Watt scored his first goal for Rovers on his debut in an FA Cup match away to Oxford United on 30 January.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Tony Watt joins Blackburn Rovers on loan |url=http://www.cafc.co.uk/news/article/charlton-blackburn-rovers-tony-watt-loan-transfer-2927139.aspx |publisher=Charlton Athletic FC |date=29 January 2016 |access-date=29 January 2016 }}{{Dead link|date=November 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> Watt scored his first league goal for Rovers against [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]] at Ewood Park.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Blackburn Rovers 2 Birmingham City 0 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35693658 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=8 March 2016}}</ref>
On 7 April 2016, Watt returned to [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]] due to an injury.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.rovers.co.uk/news/article/blackburn-rovers-charlton-athletic-tony-watt-3047238.aspx|title = Watt returns to Charlton}}</ref>

====Hearts (loan)====
Watt was loaned to [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]] for the 2016–17 season.<ref>{{cite web |first=Brian |last=McLauchlin |publisher=BBC Sport |date=20 July 2016 |access-date=20 July 2016 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36848275 |title=Tony Watt: Hearts sign former Celtic striker on season-long loan}}</ref> On 1 January 2017, the loan deal was cut short and he returned to Charlton, having only scored once in 17 games for Hearts.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Anderson|first1=Barry|title=Hearts to cut short Charlton striker Tony Watt's loan deal|url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/hearts-to-cut-short-charlton-striker-tony-watt-s-loan-deal-1-4329121|access-date=14 February 2018|work=Edinburgh Evening News|date=30 December 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Tony Watt to return to the club |url=https://cafc.co.uk/news/view/595526a71ad42/news-tony-watt-to-return-to-the-club |publisher=Charlton Athletic FC |date=1 January 2017 |access-date=2 January 2017}}</ref>

===OH Leuven===
On 13 August 2017, Watt returned to Belgium, signing for [[Belgian First Division B]] team [[Oud-Heverlee Leuven]] a one-year contract with the option for another season.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://ohl.be/nl/heren/nieuws/bericht/10177/schotse-cultvoetballer-tekent-bij-ohl |title=Schotse cultvoetballer tekent big OHL |trans-title=Scottish cultfootballer signs with OHL |language=nl |date=13 August 2017 |publisher=ohl.be |access-date=13 August 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180709215656/http://ohl.be/nl/heren/nieuws/bericht/10177/schotse-cultvoetballer-tekent-bij-ohl |archive-date=9 July 2018 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===St Johnstone===
Having left Leuven in February 2018, Watt was unable to sign for another club during the 2017–18 season. After training with [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] due to a mutual connection with their manager [[Derek McInnes]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44751575 |title=Tony Watt 'not far away' from return to UK football |publisher=BBC Sport |date=7 July 2018 |access-date=22 July 2018}}</ref> he signed a one-year contract with [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] in July 2018.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44771122 |title=Tony Watt: St Johnstone sign Scotland striker on one-year deal |publisher=BBC Sport |date=9 July 2018 |access-date=9 July 2018}}</ref> On 21 July he scored for the first time since the previous August, netting the only goal of a 1–0 victory over [[Montrose F.C.|Montrose]] in the [[2018–19 Scottish League Cup group stage#Group F|group stage]] of the [[2018–19 Scottish League Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44912280 |title=Scottish League Cup: Watt & Dobbie secure wins for St Johnstone and Queen of the South |publisher=BBC Sport |date=21 July 2018 |access-date=22 July 2018}}</ref> He went on to score six goals in the opening nine games of the season, seeing him winning the [[List of Scottish Professional Football League monthly award winners|Scottish Premiership Player of the Month]] award for August 2018.<ref name="sjpom" /> Watt then suffered a goal drought for four months, until scoring the only goal in the 89th minute of St Johnstone's 1–0 win over [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] on 26 December 2018.<ref>{{cite news |last=Roache |first=Ian |title=St Mirren 0 St Johnstone 1: Late drama as Tony Watt grabs winner to take points home to Perth |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/st-johnstone/791931/st-mirren-0-st-johnstone-1-late-drama-as-tony-watt-grabs-winner-to-take-points-home-to-perth/ |access-date=22 October 2019 |work=The Courier |date=26 December 2018}}</ref> Manager [[Tommy Wright (footballer, born 1963)|Tommy Wright]] commented after the game: "We're trying to get Tony in the box more often and it's a great header from him that wins the game. That should do him a world of good."<ref>{{cite news |last=Lamont |first=Alasdair |title=St Mirren 0 – 1 St Johnstone |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46614949 |access-date=22 October 2019 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=26 December 2019}}</ref> However, Watt only scored one more goal for St Johnstone, in a 2–0 win over [[Hamilton Accies]] in January 2019.<ref name="SOC" /> In April 2019, it was announced that Watt had turned down the offer of a new contract with St Johnstone, and would leave at the end of the season.<ref>{{cite news |title=St Johnsone: Striker Tony Watt turns down new deal and will leave in summer |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47861667 |access-date=22 October 2019 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=8 April 2019}}</ref>

===CSKA Sofia===
On 27 May 2019, Watt signed a three-year contract with Bulgarian club [[PFC CSKA Sofia|CSKA Sofia]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://cska.bg/index.php?main_page=document_general_info&products_id=8101 |title=Нападателят Тони Уот е първото лятно попълнение на ЦСКА |work=cska.bg |date=27 May 2019|language=bg}}</ref> He scored his first goal for the "redmen" in a competitive match on 20 July 2019, in the 3–1 league loss against [[PFC Cherno More Varna|Cherno More]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2019/07/20/bulgaria/a-pfg/pfc-cska-sofia/pfc-cherno-more-varna/3032719/ |title=CSKA Sofia vs. Cherno More Varna 1:3 |work=soccerway.com |date=20 July 2019| access-date=30 January 2020|language=en}}</ref> Watt parted ways with the team by mutual consent in January 2020 for personal reasons.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://topsport.bg/cska/tsska-se-razdeli-s-napadatelya-toni-uot.html |title=ЦСКА се раздели с нападателя Тони Уот |work=topsport.bg |date=28 January 2020| access-date=31 January 2020|language=bg}}</ref>

===Motherwell===
In February 2020, Watt started training with [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51372626 |title=Motherwell: Free agent striker Tony Watt trains with Fir Park club |publisher=BBC Sport |date=4 February 2020 |access-date=4 February 2020}}</ref> and he subsequently signed a short-term contract with the club on 7 February 2020<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51412594 |title=Tony Watt: Striker joins Motherwell as free agent until end of season |publisher=BBC Sport |date=7 February 2020 |access-date=7 February 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=TONY WATT SIGNS FOR MOTHERWELL |url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2020/02/07/tony-watt-signs-for-motherwell/ |website=motherwellfc.co.uk |publisher=Motherwell F.C. |access-date=7 February 2020 |date=7 February 2020}}</ref>

After extending his contract with Motherwell until the summer of 2021 on 29 May 2020,<ref>{{cite web |title=TONY WATT SIGNS NEW DEAL |url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2020/05/29/tony-watt-signs-new-deal/ |website=motherwellfc.co.uk |publisher=Motherwell F.C. |access-date=29 May 2020 |date=29 May 2020}}</ref> Watt then extended his contract with again on 9 November 2020, until the summer of 2022.<ref>{{cite web |title=TONY WATT SIGNS NEW DEAL |url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2020/11/09/tony-watt-signs-new-deal-2/ |website=motherwellfc.co.uk |publisher=Motherwell F.C. |access-date=9 November 2020 |date=9 November 2020}}</ref>

During the [[2020–21 Motherwell F.C. season|2020–21 season]], Watt was rewarded for his performances, by being voted as the Motherwell fans Player of the Month for four successive months from October to January.<ref>{{cite web | title = TONY WATT IS PAYCARE PLAYER OF THE MONTH FOR JANUARY |url = https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2021/02/08/tony-watt-is-paycare-player-of-the-month-for-january/ |website=motherwellfc.co.uk |publisher=Motherwell F.C. |access-date=9 March 2021 |date=8 February 2021}}</ref> On 20 February 2021, he was named as [[Captain (association football)|captain]] for Motherwell's home match versus [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]].<ref>{{cite web | title=Motherwell 0-3 St Johnstone | url= https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2021/02/20/motherwell-0-3-st-johnstone-2/|website=motherwellfc.co.uk |publisher=Motherwell F.C. |access-date=9 March 2021 |date=20 February 2021}}</ref>

===Dundee United===
On 27 December 2021, signed a pre-contract deal with fellow Scottish Premiership club [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]], agreeing a three-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/59796062|title=Tony Watt: Motherwell striker to sign for Dundee United next season|website=bbc.co.uk|first=Jane|last=Lewis|date=27 December 2021|access-date=27 December 2021}}</ref> Three weeks later, the clubs came to an agreement for Watt to join United immediately for an undisclosed transfer fee.<ref>{{cite news |title=Tony Watt: Dundee United sign striker from Motherwell on deal until 2025 |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11794/12518392/tony-watt-dundee-united-sign-striker-from-motherwell-on-deal-until-2025 |access-date=20 January 2022 |publisher=Sky Sports |date=17 January 2022}}</ref> He made his debut for United on 18 January 2022, as a substitute in a 2–1 home defeat against St Mirren.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Smith |first1=Ewan |title=Tam Courts explains why he benched new boy Tony Watt as Dundee United boss remains 'calm and focused' |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-united/2922441/tam-courts-new-boy-tony-watt-debut/ |access-date=20 January 2022 |work=The Courier |date=19 January 2022 |location=Dundee}}</ref>

Watt was loaned to St Mirren in January 2023.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/64471842 |title=St Mirren sign Dundee Utd forward Tony Watt & Southampton teenager Thierry Small |publisher=BBC Sport |date=31 January 2023 |accessdate=31 January 2023}}</ref>

On 29 December 2023, his 30th birthday, Watt scored a hattrick in a 3–0 win over [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] at [[Tannadice Park|Tannadice]].<ref name="Dundee United 3-0 Partick Thistle">[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/67798658 Dundee United 3-0 Partick Thistle: Watt celebrates birthday with hat-trick] [[BBC]] (29 December 2023) {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231229105702/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/67798658 |date=29 December 2023 }}</ref>

===Partick Thistle===
In July 2025 Watt joined [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web | title=Tony Watt arrives in Maryhill {{!}} Partick Thistle FC | url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/tony-watt-arrives-in-maryhill/ | access-date=2025-08-17 | website=ptfc.co.uk}}</ref> Watt made his Thistle debut off the bench in a 4–1 away victory over Edinburgh City in the Scottish League Cup group stages.<ref>{{Cite web | title=Edinburgh City vs Partick Thistle: League Cup stats & head-to-head – BBC Sport | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cx24yx2krgnt | access-date=2025-08-17 | website=www.bbc.co.uk}}</ref>

Watt scored his first goal for Thistle on 15 July 2025, in a 2–0 home win over Stranraer in the Scottish League Cup group stages.<ref>{{Cite web | title=Partick 2-0 Stranraer (Jul 15, 2025) Final Score – ESPN | url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/match/_/gameId/736197 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250722213436/https://www.espn.com/soccer/match/_/gameId/736197 | access-date=2025-08-17 | archive-date=2025-07-22}}</ref> Watt scored his first league goal for Thistle, opening the scoring in a 3–2 home win over Raith Rovers.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c3r40qq4vlrt bbc.co.uk]</ref>

==International career==
Watt has played for [[Scotland national under-19 football team|Scotland U19s]], his debut came on 12 May 2011, in a 1–0 loss to [[Denmark national under-19 football team|Denmark]].<ref name="U19">{{cite web |url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/football_player_profile.cfm?page=2492&playerID=80870&squadID=9 |title=Anthony Watt |publisher=[[Scottish Football Association]] |access-date=22 April 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/international_fixture_details.cfm?page=1921&matchID=105983 |title=Denmark 1–0 Scotland |publisher=Scottish Football Association |date=12 May 2011 |access-date=25 April 2012}}</ref> He scored his first goal on 23 September 2011, in a 3–1 victory over [[Wales national under-19 football team|Wales]]<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/international_fixture_details.cfm?page=1921&matchID=114073 |title=Wales 1–3 Scotland |publisher=Scottish Football Association |date=23 September 2011 |access-date=25 April 2012}}</ref> After his Celtic debut, [[Scotland national under-20 football team|Scotland U20s]] manager [[Billy Stark]] said that he wanted to move Watt up from the U19 squad to the under 20s,<ref name="U20">{{cite web |url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/football_player_profile.cfm?page=1921&playerID=80870&squadID=7 |title=Anthony Watt |publisher=[[Scottish Football Association]] |work=www.scottishfa.co.uk |access-date=22 April 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/football/scotland/2012/04/24/celtic-young-star-tony-watt-set-for-scotland-under-20-call-after-hitting-debut-double-86908-23835447/ |title=Celtic young star Tony Watt set for Scotland Under-20 call after hitting debut double |work=Daily Record |date=24 April 2012 |access-date=25 April 2012}}</ref> Watt made his debut for [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland U21s]] in August 2012 in a friendly match against [[Belgium national under-19 football team|Belgium]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19250608|title=Scotland U21 0–1 Belgium U21|publisher=BBC Sport|date=14 August 2012|access-date=14 August 2012}}</ref> He went on to make a total of nine appearances for the U21 side, scoring five times.<ref>{{cite web|title=U21 Profile – Anthony Watt|url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/football_player_profile.cfm?page=2492&playerID=80870&squadID=5|publisher=Scottish Football Association|access-date=13 March 2014}}</ref>

On 21 May 2013, Watt was called up by [[Gordon Strachan]] to the [[Scotland national football team|senior Scotland]] squad for the World Cup qualifier in Zagreb against Croatia on 7 June 2013.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/22607488 |publisher=BBC Sport |title=Scotland: Leigh Griffiths & Tony Watt called up for Croatia match |date=21 May 2013 |access-date=11 February 2014}}</ref> He did not play, and was subsequently dropped from the Under 21 side by manager [[Billy Stark]], with Stark citing issues with Watt's fitness as the main reason for not selecting him.<ref>{{cite web|last=Haggerty|first=Anthony|title=No place in Scotland Under-21 squad for Tony Watt as manager Billy Stark tells the striker to show some 'personal responsibility'|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/no-place-scotland-under-21-squad-2330492|work=Daily Record|location=Glasgow|access-date=13 March 2014|date=2 October 2013}}</ref>

Watt was called up to the senior [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] squad again in March 2016 for a friendly against [[Czech Republic national football team|Czech Republic]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35770855|title=Scotland: Six new call-ups for Czech Republic and Denmark friendlies|date=10 March 2016|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=10 March 2016}}</ref> and made his debut in the match on 24 March, a 1–0 win for Scotland, when he came on as a 78th-minute substitute for [[Ross McCormack]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Lamont|first=Alasdair|title=Czech Republic 0 – 1 Scotland|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35308793|access-date=29 March 2016|publisher=BBC Sport|date=24 March 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Ruthven|first=Graham|title=How did Scotland's fringe players fare in win over Czech Republic?|url=http://stv.tv/sport/football/1347800-how-did-scotlands-debutants-perform-in-win-over-czech-republic/|access-date=29 March 2016|work=STV Sport|date=25 March 2016}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Watt grew up in [[Coatbridge]] and attended St Andrew's High School.<ref name=helped>{{cite web |url=http://stv.tv/news/west-central/203603-celtic-star-tony-watt-shows-it-is-never-too-late-says-pe-teacher/ |title=Meet the man who helped make Celtic's Tony Watt a star |publisher=[[Scottish Television|STV]] |date=3 December 2012 | access-date=26 September 2016}}</ref>

'''Christopher Kane''' (born 5 September 1994) is a [[Scottish people|Scottish]] professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|striker]] for {{Scottish football updater|DunfermA}} club [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]].

==Career==
Kane made his debut for [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] against [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] on 9 November 2013.<ref>{{cite web|title=Nigel & Stevie the marksmen in win over Killie|url=http://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/matchdaydetail.php?param=648|publisher=St Johnstone F.C.|date=9 November 2013|accessdate=29 August 2014|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140903070946/http://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/matchdaydetail.php?param=648|archivedate=3 September 2014|df=dmy-all}}</ref> In January 2014, Kane signed for [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]] on a one-month loan deal,<ref>{{cite web |title=St Johnstone challenge Kane to follow in May's footsteps |url=http://www.thecourier.co.uk/sport/football/st-johnstone/st-johnstone-challenge-kane-to-follow-in-may-s-footsteps-1.171742 |publisher=The Courier |last=Roache |first=Ian |date=3 January 2014 |accessdate=29 August 2014}}</ref> scoring on his debut as the ''Sons'' defeated [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]] 2–0 on 4 January 2014.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dumbarton 2–0 Morton |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/25533112 |website=BBC Sport |date=4 January 2014 |access-date=29 August 2014}}</ref> On 31 January 2014, his loan was extended until the end of that season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chris Kane extends Dumbarton loan deal|url=https://www.dumbartonreporter.co.uk/sport/football/articles/2014/01/31/487055-chris-kane-extends-dumbarton-loan-deal/ |publisher=Dumbarton and Vale of Leven Reporter |date=31 January 2014 |accessdate=29 August 2014}}</ref> On 29 August 2014, Kane returned to Dumbarton on loan once again, agreeing a deal until January 2015.<ref>{{cite web |title=Striker returns |url=http://www.dumbartonfootballclub.com/news/?mode=view&id=1498 |publisher=Dumbarton FC |last=Findlay |first=Alan |date=29 August 2014 |accessdate=29 August 2014}}</ref> Kane scored the winner on his second debut for the ''Sons'' versus [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.livingstonfc.co.uk//news/news_20140830_2.php |title=Dumbarton 1 – 0 Livingston |publisher=Livingston FC |date=30 August 2014 |accessdate=10 August 2017}}</ref> On 24 May 2015, Kane scored his first ever goal for St Johnstone, the winner in a 1–0 win over [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] which secured a fourth-placed finish for the [[Perth, Scotland|Perth]] club.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32664504 |title=Aberdeen 0–1 St Johnstone |work=BBC Sport |date=24 May 2015 | access-date=24 May 2015}}</ref>

On 10 August 2017, Kane along with his teammate [[Jason Kerr (footballer)|Jason Kerr]] joined Scottish Championship club [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]] on loan until 31 January 2018.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.qosfc.com/news-3659 |title=Two players join |publisher=Queen of the South FC |date=10 August 2017 |accessdate=10 August 2017}}</ref> On 14 January 2018, Kane was recalled to the [[Perth, Scotland|Perth]] club when his loan spell in [[Dumfries]] with the ''Doonhamers'' ended.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/st-johnstone/576586/chris-kane-will-return-st-johnstone-better-player/|title=Chris Kane will return to St Johnstone a better player|work=The Courier}}</ref> On 29 January 2018, Kane scored a [[hat-trick]] in a 4–0 away win versus [[Albion Rovers F.C.|Albion Rovers]] in the [[Scottish Cup]] fourth round at [[Cliftonhill]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/42672293|title=Albion Rovers 0-4 St Johnstone|date=18 April 2018|website=BBC Sport|accessdate=28 August 2019}}</ref>

Kane was one of three St Johnstone players to sign a short term six-month contract extension in May 2020, as the club formulated plans amid the ongoing coronavirus pandemic.<ref>{{cite web |title=Liam Craig turns spotlight away from himself after signing new St Johnstone deal |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/liam-craig-turns-spotlight-away-22085393 |website=dailyrecord.co.uk |date=25 May 2020 |accessdate=29 May 2020}}</ref> He was a regular player as St Johnstone won both cup competitions during the 2020–21 season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cn057mgn1gvo |title=Saints should 'strive' for more glory days in cup - Kane |website=BBC Sport |date=19 January 2024 |accessdate=13 February 2024}}</ref>

He missed most of the 2022–23 season due to injury, but made a comeback near the end of the season and signed a new one-year contract with St Johnstone in June 2023.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/news/article/chris-kane-signs-contract-extension |title=Chris Kane Signs Contract Extension |publisher=St Johnstone FC |website=perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk |date=15 June 2023 |accessdate=13 February 2024}}</ref>

He moved on loan to [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] in February 2024 and then joined the club on permanent contract after leaving St Johnstone in May 2024 at the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chris Kane joins on loan |url=https://dafc.co.uk/chris-kane-joins-on-loan/ |publisher=Dunfermline Athletic FC |date=13 February 2024 |accessdate=13 February 2024}}</ref>

'''Callumn Morrison''' (born 5 July 1999) is a Scottish footballer who plays as a [[forward (association football)|forward]] for [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]]. He has also played for [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]], [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] and Linfield, and had loan spells with [[Stirling Albion F.C.|Stirling Albion]], [[Brechin City F.C.|Brechin City]] and [[East Fife F.C.|East Fife]].

Morrison grew up in the [[Alva, Clackmannanshire|Alva]] area and attended [[Alva Academy]].

==Career==
Morrison made his league debut for [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]] on 22 August 2015, in a 3–0 win against [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]]. He was loaned to [[Stirling Albion F.C.|Stirling Albion]] in the 2016–17 and 2017–18 seasons.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://spfl.co.uk/news/article/morrison-returns-to-stirling-on-loan/ |title=Morrison returns to Stirling on loan |publisher=SPFL |date=13 July 2017 |accessdate=13 July 2017}}</ref>

On 26 January 2018, Morrison extended his contract at Hearts until 2020.<ref>{{cite web|title=YOUNGSTERS COMMIT THEIR FUTURE TO HEARTS|url=http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/news/6478|publisher=Heart of Midlothian F.C.|date=26 January 2018|accessdate=30 January 2018}}</ref> That same day, he moved on loan to [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Brechin City F.C.|Brechin City]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Brechin hope to have Hearts midfielder in squad|url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/scottish-championship/588040/brechin-hope-hearts-midfielder-squad/|publisher=TheCourier|last=Nicolson|first=Eric|date=27 January 2018|accessdate=30 January 2018}}</ref> He made his debut the following day in a 3–1 defeat against [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Queen of the South 3 Brechin City 1|url=http://www.brechincity.com/bcfc/servlet/BCFCFrontControllerServlet?action=match&page_id=702&category=2|publisher=Brechin City F.C.|last=Mew|first=Steven|date=27 January 2018|accessdate=30 January 2018}}</ref>

On 10 August 2020, Morrison signed for [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]], on a one-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.falkirkfc.co.uk/2020/08/10/bairns-sign-callumn-morrison/|title=BAIRNS SIGN CALLUMN MORRISON|publisher=Falkirk FC|date=10 August 2020|access-date=19 August 2021}}</ref> 
He signed a further year extension on 20 November 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/former-hearts-winger-pens-new-deal-after-explosive-start-season-falkirk-3042392/|title= Former Hearts winger pens new deal after explosive start to season with Falkirk|work=www.edinburghnews.com|date=20 November 2020|access-date=19 August 2021}}</ref>
In his first season at [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]], he finished as the club's top goalscorer scoring nine goals in twenty-six games in competitive competitions.<ref name="CM20">{{soccerbase season|87614|2020|accessdate=19 August 2021}}</ref>

On 19 August 2021, Morrison signed a new two-year deal with [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.falkirkfc.co.uk/2021/08/19/callumn-morrison-signs-two-year-deal/|title=CALLUMN MORRISON SIGNS TWO-YEAR DEAL|publisher=Falkirk FC|date=19 August 2021|access-date=19 August 2021}}</ref> In the 2023-2024 season Morrison finished as league one top goal scorer.<ref>{{cite web |title=Callumn Morrison Wins League 1 Player of the Season |url=https://www.falkirkfc.co.uk/2024/05/24/callumn-morrison-wins-league-1-player-of-the-season/ |website=[[Falkirk F.C.]] |date=2024-05-24 |access-date=2024-07-11}}</ref>

In February 2025 Morrison moved to [[Northern Irish Premier League]] side [[Linfield F.C.|Linfield]] on a two and a half year deal, Scoring 12 goals in 33 appearances.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/cvg8352l93eo |title=Linfield sign winger Morrison from Falkirk |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=19 January 2026 |archive-date=3 February 2025 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20260119170334/https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/cvg8352l93eo |url-status=live }}</ref> Morrison failed to settle in [[Northern Ireland]] with a young family at home in Scotland and less than a year later he signed for [[Scottish Championship]] side and former rivals [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]]. He made his debut for the Pars in a victory over [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] in the [[Scottish Cup]], one day after signing.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c4gwvev72yzo |title=Morrison leaves Linfield for Dunfermline |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=19 January 2026 |archive-date=16 January 2026 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20260119162747/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c4gwvev72yzo |url-status=live }}</ref>

==International career==
Morrison played for the [[Scotland national under-17 football team|Scotland under-17]] during the 2015–16 season.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/football_player_profile.cfm?page=2492&playerID=205247&squadID=13 |title=Callumn Morrison |work=www.scottishfa.co.uk |publisher=Scottish Football Association |date= |accessdate=8 November 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/under17/teams/players/250091567--callumn-morrison/ |title=Callumn Morrison |work=[[UEFA]] |publisher=UEFA |date= |access-date=8 November 2015}}</ref>

'''Oliver Glen Shaw''' (born 12 March 1998) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)#Striker|striker]] for [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]].

He has previously played for [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]], [[Stenhousemuir F.C.|Stenhousemuir]], [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]], [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]], [[Barnsley F.C.|Barnsley]], [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] and [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]]. Shaw represented Scotland at [[Scotland national under-19 football team|under-19]] and [[Scotland national under-21 football team|under-21]] levels.

==Early life==
Shaw is from the [[Barnton, Edinburgh|Barnton]] area of [[Edinburgh]], and although a Hibernian fan, he initially joined local rivals [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] as a youth player before signing for Hibernian.<ref name=driven/> His father is retired footballer [[Greg Shaw (footballer)|Greg Shaw]], who played for [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]], [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]], [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]], [[Airdrieonians F.C. (1878)|Airdrieonians]], [[Clydebank F.C. (1965)|Clydebank]] and [[Berwick Rangers F.C.|Berwick Rangers]].<ref name=driven/>

==Club career==
===Hibernian===
After establishing himself in the Hibernian [[Hibernian F.C. Under-20s and Academy|youth team squad]], he made his first team debut for the club in a [[Scottish League Cup]] match against [[Montrose F.C.|Montrose]] on 1 August 2015, which Hibernian won 3–0.<ref name=driven>{{cite news|title=Driven Hibs kid Oli Shaw passes two tests in one day|url=http://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/driven-hibs-kid-oli-shaw-passes-two-tests-in-one-day-1-3848292 |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News |date=4 August 2015 |access-date=26 February 2017}}</ref> Having passed his [[United Kingdom driving test|driving test]] the same day, he was included as a substitute by then-manager [[Alan Stubbs]], and replaced Alex Harris in the 75th minute.<ref>{{cite web|title=Hibernian 3–0 Montrose |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33662386 |publisher=BBC |website=BBC Sport |date=1 August 2015 |access-date=26 February 2017}}</ref>

Shaw was sent to [[Scottish League One]] side [[Stenhousemuir F.C.|Stenhousemuir]] on a development loan for the 2016–17 season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Oliver Shaw Player Profile |url=http://www.stenhousemuirfc.com/club/squad/244/Oliver-Shaw/ |publisher=Stenhousemuir F.C. |date=12 August 2016 |access-date=26 February 2017 |archive-date=27 February 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170227235450/http://www.stenhousemuirfc.com/club/squad/244/Oliver-Shaw/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> He also continued to play for the Hibs development team and was the top goalscorer in the [[2016–17 SPFL Development League]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://spfl.co.uk/news/article/shaw-tops-u20-scoring-charts/ |title=Shaw tops U20 scoring charts |publisher=SPFL |date=27 April 2017 |access-date=27 April 2017 |archive-date=4 May 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170504183034/http://spfl.co.uk/news/article/shaw-tops-u20-scoring-charts/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Shaw scored his first goal for the Hibs first team on 22 October 2017, in a 4–2 defeat against [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] in the [[2017–18 Scottish League Cup]] semi-final.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/41683715 |title=Hibernian 2–4 Celtic |first=Tom |last=English |website=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=21 October 2017 |access-date=22 October 2017}}</ref> He scored his first league game for Hibs on 10 December, also against Celtic.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/42212528 |title=Hibernian 2–2 Celtic |first=Tom |last=English |website=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=10 December 2017 |access-date=11 December 2017}}</ref> In January 2018, Shaw signed a contract with Hibs that was due to run until the end of the 2020–21 season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/42581467 |title=Hibernian: Oli Shaw signs contract extension to stay at Easter Road |website=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=5 January 2018 |access-date=5 January 2018}}</ref> He continued to play for the Hibs under-20 team, and was again the top goalscorer in the Development League in [[2017–18 SPFL Development League|2017–18]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/article/shaw-tops-u20-scoring-charts-37/ |title=Shaw tops U20 scoring charts |publisher=Scottish Professional Football League |date=8 May 2018 |access-date=8 May 2018 |archive-date=9 May 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180509012625/https://spfl.co.uk/news/article/shaw-tops-u20-scoring-charts-37/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Shaw struggled to get playing time during 2019, with his last start for Hibs coming in February 2019.<ref name = "county"/> He was sold to [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] in January 2020 for an undisclosed fee.<ref name = "county">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51213809 |title=Oli Shaw: Ross County sign striker from Hibernian |website=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=22 January 2020 |access-date=22 January 2020}}</ref>

===Kilmarnock===
On 31 August 2021, Shaw joined [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] on a two-year deal, signing for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://kilmarnockfc.co.uk/news/oli-shaw-joins-killie-on-two-year-deal/|title=Oli Shaw joins Killie on two-year deal|website=kilmarnockfc.co.uk|date=31 August 2021}}</ref>

After a good start in front of goal for [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]], he won the [[2021–22 Scottish Championship#Awards|Scottish Championship player of the Month]] award for October 2021 having scored five goals in five games in the league that month.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/ayrshire/oli-shaw-thriving-kilmarnock-leading-25358706|title=Oli Shaw thriving in Kilmarnock leading role as star striker discovers prolific touch|website=dailyrecord.co.uk|first=Colin|last=Paterson|date=2 November 2021|access-date=6 November 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/ayrshire/kilmarnock-v-partick-thistle-match-25393922|title=Kilmarnock v Partick Thistle match preview as Oli Shaw named Championship player of the month|website=dailyrecord.co.uk|first=Colin|last=Paterson|date=6 November 2021|access-date=6 November 2021}}</ref>

===Barnsley===
On 31 January 2023, Shaw joined [[Barnsley F.C.|Barnsley]] on a two-and-a-half-year deal for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.barnsleyfc.co.uk/news/20232/january/oli-shaw-joins-the-reds/|title=OLI SHAW SIGNS FOR THE REDS|website=barnsleyfc.co.uk|date=31 January 2023}}</ref>. On 31 August 2023, Shaw joined [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] on loan until the end of the 23/24 season <ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.barnsleyfc.co.uk/news/20232/august/shaw-makes-loan-move/|title=OLI SHAW MAKES LOAN SWITCH|website=barnsleyfc.co.uk|date=31 August 2023}}</ref>.

===Hamilton Academical===
On 1 July 2024, Shaw joined Scottish Championship side [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]] on a three-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://hamiltonacciesfc.co.uk/oli-shaw-makes-it-five-summer-signings/|title=OLI SHAW MAKES IT FIVE SUMMER SIGNINGS|website=hamiltonacciesfc.co.uk|date=1 July 2024|accessdate=2 July 2024}}</ref>

==International career==
Shaw scored for the [[Scotland national under-19 football team|Scotland under-19s]] against [[Sweden men's national under-19 football team|Sweden]] on 4 October 2016 in a warm-up game ahead of [[2017 UEFA European Under-19 Championship qualification|qualification]] for the [[2017 UEFA European Under-19 Championship]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Scotland 2 Sweden 0: Hibs hitman Oli Shaw and Celtic ace Mark Hill on the mark as Sbragia's U19s smash young Swedes |url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-match-reports/scotland-2-sweden-0-hibs-8980223 |publisher=Daily Record|date=4 October 2016 |access-date=26 February 2017}}</ref> Scotland were drawn against [[Israel national under-19 football team|Israel]], [[Andorra national under-19 football team|Andorra]] and [[Liechtenstein national under-19 football team|Liechtenstein]] in Group C of the qualification tournament, and progressed to the Elite qualifying stage after finishing second in the group. With all three matches being played in Andorra over 6 days from 25 October 2016, Shaw scored the only goal of the game against Liechtenstein and also featured in the matches against Andorra and Israel.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/scottish_fa_news.cfm?page=1961&newsCategoryID=6&newsID=16609 |title=Skipper McCrorie satisfied as Under-19s progress |publisher=Scottish Football Association |date=31 October 2016 |access-date=22 April 2017}}</ref> Shaw was added to the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland under-21]] squad in August 2018.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/oli-shaw-heads-up-hibs-trio-handed-scotland-under-21-call-ups-1-4787187 |title=Oli Shaw heads up Hibs trio handed Scotland Under-21 call-ups |first=Peter |last=Wales |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News |date=21 August 2018 |access-date=9 March 2019}}</ref>

'''Daniel MacKay''' (born 19 April 2001) is a Scottish [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Midfielder#Winger|left winger]] for [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]].

He has previously played for [[Elgin City F.C.|Elgin City]], [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]], [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] and [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]]. MacKay has also represented Scotland at youth levels up to and including the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|under-21]] team.

He is the older brother to Calum MacKay, who most recently played for [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-07-11 |title=Three Academy Graduates sign professional contracts |url=https://ictfc.com/three-academy-graduates-sign-professional-contracts |access-date=2022-07-11 |website=ICTFC |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==Career==

=== Inverness Caledonian Thistle ===
He made his first team debut in a friendly vs [[Nairn County F.C.|Nairn County]], scoring from 20 yards past the keeper. MacKay made his professional first team debut and scored his first professional goal against [[Peterhead F.C.|Peterhead]] on 7 October 2017 in the [[Scottish Challenge Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.skysports.com/football/inverness-vs-peterhead/384555 |title=Inverness 3–0 Peterhead |work=Sky Sports |publisher=Sky |date=7 October 2017 |accessdate=28 January 2018}}</ref> He scored his first [[Scottish Championship|league]] goal in a 3–1 away loss to [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/42756925 |title=Falkirk 3–1 Inverness Caledonian Thistle |date=27 January 2018 |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |access-date=28 January 2018}}</ref> He was assisted by fellow league debutant, [[Jack Brown (footballer, born 2001)|Jack Brown]]. MacKay is the youngest player and goalscorer in the club's history,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44082233 |title=Daniel MacKay: Inverness CT's youngest scorer joins Aaron Doran in signing new deal |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=11 May 2018 |accessdate=11 May 2018}}</ref> at just 16 years and 174 days.

He was one of 10 youth players to turn professional with the club in May 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/inverness-caledonian-thistle/1474956/caley-thistle-sign-up-10-youth-players-on-professional-contracts/|title=Caley Thistle sign up 10 youth players on professional contracts|date=14 May 2018|accessdate=20 February 2019|author=Stuart Findley|publisher=The Press and Journal}}</ref>

On 9 August 2019, MacKay and goalkeeper [[Daniel Hoban]] were loaned by Inverness to [[Scottish League Two|League Two]] club [[Elgin City F.C.|Elgin City]]. However a little over a week later, MacKay injured his ankle in a 1–0 home loss to [[Stenhousemuir F.C.|Stenhousemuir]] in the 43rd minute. MacKay's loan was extended to the end of the season in the January Transfer Window.{{citation needed|date=December 2020}}

In his first full playing season with Inverness, MacKay scored seven goals and won the club's goal of the season award for his effort against [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] in a Scottish Cup tie.{{citation needed|date=June 2021}}

On 7 August 2026, MacKay returned to Inverness Caledonian Thistle on a short term deal.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.inverness-courier.co.uk/sport/midfielder-returns-to-inverness-caledonian-thistle-after-agr-442013/|title=Midfielder returns to Inverness Caledonian Thistle after signing for Hibernian five years ago|first=Will|last=Clark|date=7 August 2026|accessdate=7 August 2026}}</ref>

=== Hibernian ===
MacKay signed for [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] for an undisclosed amount in May 2021.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/a-massive-club-in-a-massive-city-daniel-mackay-eager-to-repay-hibs-after-signing-four-year-deal-3235073?itm_source=parsely-api |title='A massive club in a massive city' - Daniel Mackay eager to repay Hibs after signing four-year deal |first=Patrick |last=McPartlin |date=12 May 2021 |accessdate=12 May 2021 |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News}}</ref>
On 29 July 2021, MacKay scored his first goal for [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] in a competitive game against [[FC Santa Coloma]] in a 2–1 win in the [[2021–22 UEFA Europa Conference League qualifying phase and play-off round#Second qualifying round|UEFA Conference League qualifiers]] second-leg.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57972238|title=FC Santa Coloma 1–2 Hibernian|website=bbc.co.uk|first=Matthew|last=Reed|date=29 July 2021|access-date=30 July 2021}}</ref>

On 13 January 2022, MacKay joined [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] on loan for the remainder of the [[2021-22 Scottish Championship|2021–22]] season.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/article/dan-mackay-joins-kilmarnock-on-loan|title=Dan Mackay Joins Kilmarnock On Loan|website=hibernianfc.co.uk|date=13 January 2022|access-date=13 January 2022}}</ref>

In July 2022, MacKay was loaned back to [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] for the 2022–23 season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.msn.com/en-gb/sport/football/hibs-winger-daniel-mackay-returns-to-inverness-caledonian-thistle-on-season-long-loan/ar-AAZmK4J  |title=Hibs winger Daniel MacKay returns to Inverness Caledonian Thistle on season-long loan |website=msn.com |first=Patrick |last=McPartlin |date=8 July 2022 |accessdate=8 July 2022}}</ref> He scored for Inverness in the [[2023 Scottish Cup final]], which they lost 3–1 to [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/65730831 |title=Celtic 3-1 Inverness CT: Ange Postecoglou's side win Scottish Cup to claim treble |website=BBC Sport |date=3 June 2023 |accessdate=4 June 2023 |first=Thomas |last=Duncan}}</ref>

MacKay moved on loan to [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] in August 2023.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cw5rw90re0xo |title=Livi sign Hibs forward Mackay on loan |website=BBC Sport |date=4 August 2023 |accessdate=4 August 2023}}</ref>

=== Partick Thistle ===
In June 2024, he joined [[Partick Thistle F.C|Partick Thistle]] on a two-year deal following his departure from [[Easter Road]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/daniel-mackay-joins-the-jags-on-two-year-deal/|title=Daniel MacKay joins the Jags on two-year deal|website=ptfc.co.uk|date=25 June 2024}}</ref>

Following an injury in training in August 2024, it was confirmed that MacKay would be out injured for a significant period of the 2024–25 season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/injury-update-daniel-mackay-8th-august-2024/|title=Injury Update: Daniel Mackay – 8th August 2024|website=Partick Thistle FC}}</ref>

== International career ==
In 2017, MacKay played for the [[Scotland national under-16 football team|Scotland Schoolboys]] team, along with fellow [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] team-mate, Kieran Chalmers. He scored in a match against England a day before he featured in the [[2018 Scottish Challenge Cup Final]], where he provided the assist to the winning goal from [[Carl Tremarco]].{{citation needed|date=December 2020}}

MacKay was called up into the [[Scotland national under-19 football team|Scotland under-19]] squad on 28 January 2019 ahead of friendlies vs [[Spain national under-19 football team|Spain]] and [[Azerbaijan national under-19 football team|Azerbaijan]]. He made his under-19 debut against Spain, substituting in the 72nd minute for [[Stephen Kelly (Scottish footballer)|Stephen Kelly]].{{citation needed|date=December 2020}}

On 25 May 2021, MacKay was called into the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland under-21]] squad for two friendlies against [[Northern Ireland national under-21 football team|Northern Ireland]].<ref name = selection/> Three other Inverness players ([[Robbie Deas]], [[Roddy MacGregor]] and [[Cameron Harper (footballer)|Cameron Harper]]) were also selected.<ref name = selection>{{Cite web|title=Scot Gemmill names Under-21 squad for friendly double header {{!}} News {{!}} Scottish FA|url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/news/scot-gemmill-names-under-21-squad-for-friendly-double-header/?rid=14258|access-date=2021-05-25|website=www.scottishfa.co.uk}}</ref> MacKay featured prominently in the second game, missing three good chances but winning a [[penalty kick]] that led to the match-winning goal.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/new-hibs-winger-daniel-mackay-has-eventful-afternoon-in-scotland-under-21-debut-3262564 |title=New Hibs winger Daniel Mackay has eventful afternoon in Scotland Under-21 debut |first=Mark |last=Atkinson |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News |date=5 June 2021 |accessdate=5 June 2021}}</ref>

'''Ross Alexander Munro''' (born 1 April 2000) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]], who plays as a [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] for Scottish League One club, Inverness Caledonian Thistle.

==Club career==
Born in [[Inverness]],<ref name="sw" /> Munro grew up in [[Nairn]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Skinner |first=Andy |date=13 September 2018 |title=Ross County goalkeeper Ross Munro on Scotland under-19s radar |url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/1561394/staggies-goalkeeper-munro-on-scotland-under-19s-radar/ |access-date=27 March 2022 |website=Press and Journal |language=en-GB}}</ref> He signed for [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] at under-15 level after playing for [[Nairn County F.C.|Nairn County]].<ref name="Nairn goalkeeper">{{Cite web |last=Clark |first=WIll |date=20 June 2021 |title=Nairn goalkeeper grateful to remain professional footballer at Ross County |url=https://www.ross-shirejournal.co.uk/sport/nairn-goalkeeper-grateful-to-remain-professional-footballer-242165/ |access-date=27 March 2022 |website=Ross-shire Journal |language=en}}</ref> In January 2017, Munro signed a one month development loan with [[Highland Football League|Highland League]] side [[Brora Rangers F.C.|Brora Rangers]]. On 2 February 2017, it was announced that Munro had extended his loan until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.rosscountyfootballclub.co.uk/news/archive/ross-munro-joins-brora-rangers-on-short-term-development-loan/|title=Ross Munro extends Development Loan at Brora Rangers|publisher= Ross County FC|date=3 February 2018|access-date=16 August 2018}}</ref>

On 17 May 2018, it was announced that Munro and three other youth players had signed their first senior professional contracts with [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=17 May 2018 |title=SIGNING NEWS Four Development Squad regulars sign professional contracts with the Staggies |url=http://www.rosscountyfootballclub.co.uk/news/archive/four-development-players-sign-contracts/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180817023128/http://www.rosscountyfootballclub.co.uk/news/archive/four-development-players-sign-contracts/ |archive-date=17 August 2018 |publisher=Ross County FC |access-date=16 August 2018}}</ref> Munro made his debut for Ross County in the [[Scottish Challenge Cup]] against [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian Colts]] in August 2018 which County won 2-1.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/1541440/holders-caley-thistle-out-but-staggies-progress-in-irn-bru-cup/|title=Holders Caley Thistle out, but Staggies progress in IRN-BRU Cup|publisher= Press and Journal|date=17 August 2018|access-date=17 August 2018}}</ref> He went on to play in every round of the Challenge Cup, including the final as Ross County lifted the trophy beating [[Connah's Quay Nomads F.C.|Connah's Quay Nomads]] 3–1.<ref name=raith>{{cite web|title=Munro leaves Ross County on loan|url=https://www.ross-shirejournal.co.uk/sport/munro-seals-raith-loan-deal-179592/|publisher=Ross-shire Journal|last=Henderson|first=Andrew|date=24 June 2019|access-date=10 September 2019}}</ref><ref name=challenge/>

In June 2019, Munro moved on loan to [[Scottish League One]] club [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] until January 2020.<ref name=raith/>

Munro joined [[Scottish League Two]] club [[Cowdenbeath F.C.|Cowdenbeath]] on a 7-day emergency loan on 11 December 2020,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Clark |first=Will |date=11 December 2020 |title=Ross County goalkeeper answers emergency call from Cowdenbeath |url=https://www.ross-shirejournal.co.uk/sport/ross-county-goalkeeper-answers-emergency-call-from-cowdenbeath-221338/ |access-date=27 March 2022 |website=Ross-shire Journal |language=en}}</ref> and had a loan spell at [[Annan Athletic F.C.|Annan Athletic]] later that season.<ref name="Nairn goalkeeper"/> He signed a new one-year contract at the club in June 2021.<ref name="Nairn goalkeeper"/>

In March 2022, Munro signed a new one-year contract with the club.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Skinner |first=Andy |date=8 March 2022 |title=Ross Munro signs new one-year deal with Ross County |url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/ross-county/4032875/ross-munro-signs-new-one-year-deal-with-ross-county/ |access-date=27 March 2022 |website=Press and Journal |language=en-GB}}</ref>

In January 2024, Munro joined [[League of Ireland Premier Division]] club [[Dundalk F.C.|Dundalk]] on a permanent deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dundalkfc.com/new-signing-ross-munro/|title=NEW SIGNING: ROSS MUNRO|website=www.dundalkfc.com|date=24 January 2024|accessdate=24 January 2024}}</ref>

In December 2024, Munro agreed join [[Scottish Championship]] club, [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] until the end of the season on a permanent deal.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-12-19 |title=Former Ross County goalkeeper signs for Championship league leaders |url=https://www.ross-shirejournal.co.uk/sport/former-ross-county-goalkeeper-signs-for-championship-league-369521/ |access-date=2025-01-04 |website=RossShire Journal |language=en}}</ref>

==International career==
In October 2018, Munro was called up to the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland national under-21 side]] for a fixture against [[Ukraine national under-21 football team|Ukraine]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/ross-county/1612755/ross-county-youngster-ross-munro-targets-more-scotland-under-21-experiences-after-maiden-call-up/|title=Ross County youngster Ross Munro targets more Scotland under-21 experiences after maiden call-up|first=Jamie|last=Durent|date=20 November 2018|access-date=27 March 2022}}</ref>
