'''Zak Andrew Rudden''' (born 6 February 2000) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|striker]] for {{Scottish football updater|DunfermA}} club [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]]. He has previously been a player for [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]], [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]], [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] and [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]], and has had loan spells at [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]], [[Plymouth Argyle F.C.|Plymouth Argyle]], Dundee, [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]], [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] and [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].

==Club career==

===Rangers===
Born in [[Edinburgh]],<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://queensparkfc.co.uk/zak-rudden-to-leave-queens-park/|title=Zak Rudden To Leave Queen's Park|first=David|last=Oliver|date=12 June 2025}}</ref> Rudden began his career with [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/16284660.rangers-kid-zak-rudden-putting-in-the-hours-to-catch-steven-gerrards-eye-at-ibrox/|title=Rangers kid Zak Rudden putting in the hours to catch Steven Gerrard's eye at Ibrox|date=13 June 2018|access-date=17 September 2018|first=Christopher|last=Jack|newspaper=The Herald}}</ref> and joined the first-team for pre-season before the start of the [[2018–19 in Scottish football|2018–19]] season for the first time.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://rangers.co.uk/news/headlines/zaks-best-week/|title=Zak's best Week|date=26 June 2018|access-date=17 September 2018|publisher=Rangers F.C.}}</ref>

===Loans===
In August 2018, Rudden moved out on loan to [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45376379|title=Morton 'saddened' by Ray McKinnon's departure for Falkirk|date=31 August 2018|access-date=17 September 2018|publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> On 15 September 2018, Rudden scored on his debut for Falkirk.<ref name = "18-19"/>

On 23 August 2019 Rudden moved on loan to [[EFL League Two]] side [[Plymouth Argyle F.C.|Plymouth Argyle]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pafc.co.uk/news/2019/august/zak-attack/|title=Zak Attack|date=23 August 2019|access-date=23 August 2019|publisher=PAFC.co.uk}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49449315|title=Zak Rudden: Plymouth Argyle sign Rangers striker on loan|date=23 August 2019|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=28 August 2019}}</ref> He made his debut for the club the next day, as a first half substitute in a 3–0 win over [[Walsall F.C.|Walsall]], and scored his first goal for the club in an [[EFL Trophy]] tie against [[Swindon Town]] on 8 October 2019.<ref name = "19-20"/> The loan ended in January 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pafc.co.uk/news/2020/january/rudden-returns-to-rangers/|title=Zak Going Back|website=www.pafc.co.uk}}</ref>

===Partick Thistle===
On 15 January 2020 Rudden signed for [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] on a two-and-a-half-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/signing-news-zak-rudden-joins-the-club/|title=Signing News: Zak Rudden Joins the Club|date=15 January 2020|publisher=Partick Thistle F.C.}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51123284 |title=Zak Rudden: Rangers striker signs for Partick Thistle |website=BBC Sport |date=15 January 2020 |access-date=15 January 2020}}</ref>

After multiple injury problems and the shutdown of football due to COVID-19, Rudden scored his first Thistle goal on 23 March 2021 in a 3–0 win at home over Cowdenbeath in the Scottish Cup.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-fixture/partick-thistle-v-cowdenbeath-23rd-march-2021/|title=Partick Thistle v Cowdenbeath – 23rd March 2021|website=Partick Thistle FC}}</ref>

In April 2021, Rudden scored his first and second league goals for Thistle in a 2–0 home win against Clyde.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/56740532|title=Lower league round-up: Partick Thistle maintain League One title hopes|work=BBC Sport |date=13 April 2021}}</ref>

===Dundee===
In January 2022 he signed a pre-contract agreement with [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] on a three-year deal, starting in summer 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-fc/2933124/dundee-sign-zak-rudden/|title=Zak Rudden: Dundee confirm pre-contract agreement with Partick Thistle top scorer|first=Scott|last=Lorimer|date=21 January 2022 }}</ref> On 31 January 2022, Rudden joined Dundee on loan until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|date=31 January 2022|title=Zak joins on loan|url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/zak-joins-on-loan/|access-date=31 January 2022|website=Dundee Football Club – Official Website|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/60206893|title=Dundee sign Thistle's Rudden on loan|work=BBC Sport }}</ref> He made his debut the following day as a substitute in the [[Dundee derby]], and scored his first goal for the club four days later against [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]].<ref name = "21-22"/>

After officially joining Dundee permanently the following season, Rudden scored his first goal of the season in a home league win over [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Dundee end Arbroath run in six-goal thriller |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62431314 |access-date=12 August 2022}}</ref>

On 31 January 2023, Rudden joined [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] on loan until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=31 January 2023 |title=Zak joins St. Johnstone |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/zak-joins-st-johnstone/ |access-date=31 January 2023 |website=Dundee Football Club – Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64471150|title=St Johnstone sign Dundee striker Rudden on loan|work=BBC Sport }}</ref> On 25 February Rudden scored his first goal for the ''Saintees'' in a draw against [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=St Johnstone 1–1 St Mirren: Alex Gogic scores late on as Buddies salvage a point against 10-man Saints |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/st-johnstone-vs-st-mirren/report/465180 |access-date=25 February 2023 |website=Sky Sports |language=en}}</ref>

Following his return from loan at St Johnstone, Rudden scored the winner in Dundee's first competitive game of the 2023–24 season, coming in the [[Scottish League Cup|League Cup]] against [[Bonnyrigg Rose F.C.|Bonnyrigg Rose]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Bonnyrigg Rose v Dundee |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66191435 |access-date=18 July 2023}}</ref> On 23 September, Rudden came off the bench on for 10-man Dundee and scored a late equaliser against [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Ten-man Dundee stun Kilmarnock with late leveller |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66828957 |access-date=23 September 2023}}</ref>

On 26 January 2024, Rudden joined [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] on loan until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Zak Rudden signs {{!}} Raith Rovers FC |url=https://www.raithrovers.net/67002/zak-rudden-signs.htm |access-date=26 January 2024 |website=www.raithrovers.net|date=26 January 2024 }}</ref> He made his debut the following day in a league game at home against [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Nine-minute Samuel hat-trick dents Raith's title bid |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68039855 |access-date=27 January 2024 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> Rudden scored his first goal for the ''Fifers'' in the following league game, in a sold-out title-chasing win over his parent club's rivals [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Stunner revives Raith's title hopes as Dundee Utd falter |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68144329 |access-date=17 February 2024 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

On 12 July 2024, Dundee announced that Rudden had departed the club after both parties mutually agreed to terminate his contract.<ref>{{Cite web |date=12 July 2024 |title=Rudden departs |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/rudden-departs/ |access-date=12 July 2024 |website=Dundee Football Club – Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Queen's Park===

The day after departing Dundee, Rudden signed for [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |date=13 July 2024 |title=Zak Rudden Signs for Queen's Park |url=https://queensparkfc.co.uk/zac-rudden-signs-for-queens-park/ |access-date=13 July 2024 |website=Queen's Park Football Club: Home |language=en-US}}</ref> Rudden made his debut for the ''Spiders'' on the same day, and scored his first goal for the club in a 0–5 away victory over [[Peterhead F.C.|Peterhead]] in the [[Scottish League Cup]] group stage.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Peterhead vs. Queen's Park – 13 July 2024 – Soccerway |url=https://uk.soccerway.com/matches/2024/07/13/scotland/league-cup/peterhead-fc/queens-park-fc/4360400/ |access-date=13 July 2024 |website=uk.soccerway.com}}</ref>

===Livingston===
On 12 June 2025, it was announced that Rudden had signed for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].<ref name="auto"/>

===Dunfermline Athletic===
On 28 August 2025, less than three months after signing for Livingston, Rudden signed for [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://dafc.co.uk/welcome-to-dunfermline-zak-rudden/ |title=Welcome to Dunfermline, Zak Rudden |date=28 August 2025 |publisher=DAFC.co.uk |access-date=28 August 2025 |archive-date=28 August 2025 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250828121525/https://dafc.co.uk/welcome-to-dunfermline-zak-rudden/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Rudden made his debut on 30 August and scored his first goal for the club in a draw against [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dunfermline Athletic vs Ross County: Scottish Championship updates & report |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cpv0wnn0lz9t |access-date=30 August 2025 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> After suffering an injury in February 2026, Rudden returned for the final game of the season as a substitute for the ''Pars'' in the [[2026 Scottish Cup final]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Duncan |first=Live ReportingThomas |title=Celtic vs Dunfermline Athletic LIVE: Scottish Cup final TV, radio, text, team news, reaction, stats |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cn4pd19zv9dt |access-date=1 June 2026 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

'''Reece Lyon''' (born 13 March 2000) is a [[Scottish people|Scottish]] [[association football|footballer]] who plays for {{Scottish football updater|QueenOTS}} club [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]]. Lyon has had spells with [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]], [[Annan Athletic F.C.|Annan Athletic]] (loan) and [[Kelty Hearts F.C.|Kelty Hearts]].

==Club career==
Lyon came through the [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]] youth academy after signing from [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] in 2013.<ref name="OS profile"/> He made his debut in the [[Scottish Challenge Cup]] against [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]] in August 2018.<ref name="OS profile">{{cite news|url=https://gmfc.net/player/reece-lyon/|title=Reece Lyon|publisher=Greenock Morton F.C.|accessdate=30 September 2018|website=gmfc.net}}</ref> Lyon scored on his first start for the club: scoring the winning goal against [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45948214|title=Queen of the South 1-2 Greenock Morton|publisher=BBC|website=BBC Sport|date=30 October 2018|accessdate=31 October 2018}}</ref>

Lyon was loaned to [[Annan Athletic F.C.|Annan Athletic]] in September 2022.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.gmfc.net/reece-lyon-joins-annan-athletic-on-loan-until-january/ |title=Reece Lyon joins Annan Athletic on loan until January |publisher=Greenock Morton FC |website=gmfc.net |date=2 September 2022 |accessdate=4 September 2022}}</ref>

On 28 June 2023, [[Kelty Hearts F.C.|Kelty Hearts]] announced Lyon had signed for the club.<ref>{{Cite web |date=29 June 2023 |title=Michael Tidser signs ex-Greenock Morton man Reece Lyon |url=https://www.dunfermlinepress.com/news/23622548.kelty-hearts-michael-tidser-signs-ex-greenock-morton-man-reece-lyon/ |access-date=30 April 2024 |website=www.dunfermlinepress.com}}</ref>

'''Charlie Ian Gilmour''' (born 11 February 1999) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Midfielder#Defensive midfielder|defensive midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|DunfermA}} club [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]].

==Club career==

===Arsenal===
Born in [[Brighton]], Gilmour was spotted by [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] scouts at the age of 6.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.football.london/arsenal-fc/news/charlie-gilmour-arsenal-bate-borisov-13683390|title=Charlie Gilmour on his journey to the Arsenal first-team – and why he worships Santi Cazorla|website=football.london|date=27 September 2017|accessdate=30 November 2018}}</ref> On 29 November 2018, he made his first team debut, playing the last 14 minutes in a 3–0 win over [[FC Vorskla Poltava|Vorskla Poltava]] in the [[UEFA Europa League|Europa League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2018/11/29/europe/uefa-cup/fc-vorskla-poltava/arsenal-fc/2909571/|title=VORSKLA VS. ARSENAL 0 – 3|website=uk.soccerway.com|date=29 November 2018|accessdate=30 November 2018}}</ref> Gilmour was released by Arsenal on 7 June 2019, after spending 14 years at the club.

===Norwich City===
A day later, on 8 July 2019, Gilmour signed with [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{cite web |title=Charlie Gilmour signs for Norwich City |url=https://www.canaries.co.uk/News/2019/july/charlie-gilmour-signs-for-norwich-city/ |publisher=[[Norwich City F.C.]] |accessdate=8 July 2019}}</ref> On 18 July 2019, he signed for Dutch side [[SC Telstar|Telstar]] on a season-long loan.<ref>{{cite web |title=Former Arsenal midfielder seals swift Holland loan switch following City arrival |date=18 July 2019 |url=https://www.edp24.co.uk/sport/norwich-city/city-u23-midfielder-seals-holland-loan-switch-1-6167020 |publisher=[[Eastern Daily Press]] |accessdate=18 July 2019}}</ref>

===St Johnstone===
On 1 February 2021, Gilmour signed a short-term deal with [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=1 February 2021|title=Former Arsenal youngster Charlie Gilmour signs for Saints|url=https://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/news/post/former-arsenal-youngster-charlie-gilmour-signs-saints|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210201175821/https://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/news/post/former-arsenal-youngster-charlie-gilmour-signs-saints |archive-date=1 February 2021 |access-date=1 February 2021|website=perthstjohnstone.co.uk}}</ref> On 21 May 2021, he signed a new two-year contract with St Johnstone.<ref>{{cite web|title=Gilmour Signs New 2 Year Contract|url=https://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/news/article/gilmour-signs-new-2-year-contract|website=perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk|date=21 May 2021|access-date=26 May 2021}}</ref>

===Inverness Caledonian Thistle===
On 1 July 2023, Gilmour joined [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]], making his debut on 15 July in a 2–1 home win over [[Bonnyrigg Rose F.C.|Bonnyrigg Rose]] in the [[Scottish League Cup|League Cup]], before scoring his first goal for the club ten days later in a 3–2 loss to [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]], also in the League Cup. Gilmour made his league debut for Inverness in a 2–1 home loss to [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]], before scoring his first league goal a season later in a 1–0 home win over [[Alloa Athletic F.C.|Alloa Athletic]] in League One.

=== Dunfermline Athletic ===
On 2 June 2025, Gilmour joined Scottish Championship club [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] on a three-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brown |first=Craig |date=2025-06-02 |title=Charlie Gilmour signs {{!}} Dunfermline Athletic Football Club - |url=https://dafc.co.uk/charlie-gilmour-signs/ |access-date=2025-06-02 |website=Dunfermline Athletic Football Club |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==International career==
Gilmour has represented both England and Scotland at youth international level. In 2013 and 2014, he represented Scotland at [[Scotland national under-15 football team|under-15]] and [[Scotland national under-16 football team|under-16]] level<ref name = 'Scotland FA'>{{cite web|url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/players/?pid=286274&lid=9|title=Charlie Gilmour at Scottish FA|publisher=[[Scottish Football Association]]|accessdate=30 November 2018}}</ref> but then in 2015, he represented [[England national under-17 football team|England Under-17]] in the FA International Tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uBSoneNKinY|title=England U17 3–7 Portugal U17 Goals and Highlights|publisher=[[The FA]]|date=30 August 2015|accessdate=30 November 2018}}</ref> He later returned to action for Scotland, playing at [[Scotland national under-17 football team|under-17]] and [[Scotland national under-19 football team|under-19]] level.<ref name = 'Scotland FA'/>

'''Roddy MacGregor''' (born 21 December 2001) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]]

==Club career==

===Inverness Caledonian Thistle===
MacGregor began his career with [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]], and was one of 10 youth players to turn professional with the club in May 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/inverness-caledonian-thistle/1474956/caley-thistle-sign-up-10-youth-players-on-professional-contracts/|title=Caley Thistle sign up 10 youth players on professional contracts|date=14 May 2018|accessdate=20 February 2019|author=Stuart Findley|publisher=The Press and Journal}}</ref> He made his senior debut on 17 November 2018, in a 3–3 league draw away at [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]].<ref name = "2018-19"/>

He made a "breakthrough" with the Inverness first team in the 2019–20 season,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/inverness-caledonian-thistle/2526241/roddy-macgregor-knows-adding-goals-to-game-could-bag-him-caley-thistle-starting-spot/|title=Roddy MacGregor knows adding goals to game could bag him Caley Thistle starting spot |date=29 September 2020 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.inverness-courier.co.uk/sport/macgregor-targets-more-goals-for-caley-thistle-213562/|title=Roddy MacGregor targets more goals for Inverness Caley Thistle |date=29 September 2020 }}</ref> making 20 appearances in all competitions.<ref name = "2019-20"/>

He scored his first goal for Inverness on 10 November 2020, in the [[Scottish League Cup]], in a 3–3 draw with [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]].<ref name = "2020-21"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/inverness-caledonian-thistle/2647927/goal-will-take-a-huge-weight-off-roddy-macgregors-shoulders-caley-thistle-boss-john-robertson/|title=Goal will take a huge weight off Roddy MacGregor's shoulders – Caley Thistle boss John Robertson |date=14 November 2020 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.inverness-courier.co.uk/sport/caley-thistle-can-compete-against-the-best-in-league-says-roddy-macgregor-218229/|title=Inverness Caledonian Thistle can compete against the best in league says Roddy MacGregor |date=13 November 2020 }}</ref> He scored his first league goal on 4 December 2020, in a 3–0 victory against [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]].<ref name = "2020-21"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/inverness-caledonian-thistle/2713168/caley-thistles-roddy-macgregor-up-for-starting-challenge-after-goal-against-queen-of-the-south/|title=Caley Thistle's Roddy MacGregor up for starting challenge after goal against Queen of the South |date=7 December 2020 }}</ref>

===Queen's Park===
Roddy joined Scottish Championship Queen's Park on 2 July 2024, signing a two-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.inverness-courier.co.uk/sport/former-ict-star-signs-for-championship-club-354531/|title=CInverness Caley Thistle academy graduate Roddy MacGregor signs for Scottish Championship outfit Queen's Park|date=2 July 2024|website=The Inverness Courier}}</ref>

===Return to Inverness Caledonian Thistle===
MacGregor announced his return to [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] on 29 July 2026.<ref>{{Cite news |date=29 July 2026 |title=Inverness Caledonian Thistle FC (@ICTFC) on X |url=https://x.com/ICTFC/status/2082539160485695854 |access-date=29 July 2026 |work=X (formerly Twitter) |language=en-US}}</ref>

==International career==
On 25 May 2021, he received his first international call up, for the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland under-21]] team for two friendlies against [[Northern Ireland national under-21 football team|Northern Ireland]] alongside Inverness team-mates, [[Robbie Deas]], [[Cameron Harper (footballer)|Cameron Harper]] and [[Daniel MacKay]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Scot Gemmill names Under-21 squad for friendly double header {{!}} News {{!}} Scottish FA|url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/news/scot-gemmill-names-under-21-squad-for-friendly-double-header/?rid=14258|access-date=25 May 2021|website=www.scottishfa.co.uk}}</ref> MacGregor made his under-21 debut in the second game, coming on as a substitute for [[Josh McPake]] in the 72nd minute.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/news/scotland-under-21s-edge-northern-ireland-in-five-goal-friendly-clash/?rid=13925 |title=Scotland Under-21s edge Northern Ireland in five goal friendly clash |website=www.scottishfa.co.uk |date=5 June 2021 |accessdate=5 June 2021}}</ref>

'''Alfons Antonio Chico Amade''' (born 12 November 1999) is a professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[right-back]] for [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]].<ref name="worldfootball"/> Born in Germany, he represents the [[Mozambique national football team|Mozambique national team]].

==Club career==
Amade made his professional debut for [[TSG 1899 Hoffenheim|TSG Hoffenheim]] in the [[Bundesliga]] on 2 March 2019, coming on as a substitute in the 82nd minute for [[Nadiem Amiri]] in the match against [[Eintracht Frankfurt]], which finished as a 2–3 away loss.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.kicker.de/frankfurt-gegen-hoffenheim-2019-bundesliga-4243475/analyse |title=Adams' Platzverweis eröffnet Frankfurter Finale furioso |trans-title=Adams' dismissal launches furious Frankfurt finale |website=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |date=2 March 2019 |access-date=2 March 2019 |language=German}}</ref>

In July 2025, Amade signed for [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://dafc.co.uk/alfons-arrives-in-dunfermline/ |title=Alfons Arrives in Dunfermline |publisher=Dunfermline Athletic |access-date=8 August 2025 |archive-date=8 August 2025 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250808121759/https://dafc.co.uk/alfons-arrives-in-dunfermline/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He was the first signing to move to the Scottish club from their affiliate team [[PFC Septemvri Sofia|Septemvri Sofia]] in [[Bulgaria]].

==International career==
Born in Germany, Amade is of Mozambican descent. He is a former youth international for Germany.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://regionalsport.de/eintracht-braunschweig-leiht-defensivjuwel-alfons-amade/|title=Eintracht Braunschweig leiht Defensivjuwel Alfons Amadé|website=regionalSport.de}}</ref>

In December 2023, Amade was called up by the [[Mozambique national football team|Mozambique national team]] for the [[2023 Africa Cup of Nations]].<ref>{{cite web |title=AFCON 2023 – PROVISIONAL SQUADS LIST|url=https://www.cafonline.com/media/szzh20fx/afcon-2023-provisional-squads-list.pdf|page=28}}</ref>

'''Luis James Longstaff''' (born 24 February 2001) is an English [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[right winger]] for {{Scottish football updater|InvernCT}} side [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]].

== Career ==
Longstaff made his professional debut for [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] on 17 December 2019, starting in the away match against [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] in the [[2019–20 EFL Cup#Quarter-finals|quarter-finals]] of the [[EFL Cup]].<ref name="SW">{{Soccerway}}</ref>

On 31 August 2021, he joined Scottish third tier side [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]] on loan until 30 June 2022.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Shaw |first1=Chris |title=Luis Longstaff joins Queen's Park on loan |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/academy/442310-luis-longstaff-joins-queen-s-park-on-loan |publisher=Liverpool FC |access-date=31 August 2021}}</ref>

In June 2022 it was announced by Liverpool that he would leave the club at the end of the month when his contract expired.<ref>{{cite news |title=Liverpool: Divock Origi and Loris Karius among seven to leave Reds |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/61742711 |access-date=9 June 2022 |work=BBC Sport |date=9 June 2022}}</ref>

On 4 August 2022, he joined [[Scottish Championship]] side Cove Rangers. After one season with Cove, Longstaff signed a two-year contract with [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] in July 2023.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/inverness-caledonian-thistle/5969236/caley-thistle-sign-winger-luis-longstaff/ |title=Caley Thistle sign former Cove Rangers winger Luis Longstaff |newspaper=Press and Journal |first=Danny |last=Law |date=21 July 2023 |accessdate=22 July 2023}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Although of a similar age and originating from the north-east of England, he is not related to fellow players [[Sean Longstaff|Sean]] and [[Matty Longstaff]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hunter |first1=Steve |title=Meet the Academy: Luis Longstaff |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/academy/394591-meet-the-academy-luis-longstaff |access-date=13 May 2022 |publisher=Liverpool F.C. |date=8 May 2020}}</ref>

The secondary school he went to was [[Greenfield Academy]].<ref>{{Citation |title=Greenfield Academy |date=2026-05-08 |work=Wikipedia |url=https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Greenfield_Academy&oldid=1353203837 |access-date=2026-05-08 |language=en}}</ref>

'''Paul Allan''' (born 7 February 2000) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[defensive midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|InvernCT}} side [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]]. Allan previously played for [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]], with loan spells with [[Stenhousemuir F.C.|Stenhousemuir]], [[Hill of Beath Hawthorn F.C.|Hill of Beath Hawthorn]], [[Brechin City F.C.|Brechin City]] and [[Albion Rovers F.C.|Albion Rovers]].

==Career==
Allan started his youth career at Inverkeithing Boys Club, before joining [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] at the age of 10.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://dafc.co.uk/people.php?SID=U20s&ID=93|title=Dunfermline Athletic Football Club|website=dafc.co.uk}}</ref> He signed a two-year contract with the club in May 2017,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dunfermlinepress.com/sport/15274118.dunfermline-athletics-paul-allan-signs-two-year-contract-with-the-club/|title=Talented teen Paul commits future to the Pars|website=Dunfermline Press |date=9 May 2017 }}</ref> and had spells on loan at [[Stenhousemuir F.C.|Stenhousemuir]] – for whom he made three appearances<ref name="soccerway" /> – and [[Hill of Beath Hawthorn F.C.|Hill of Beath Hawthorn]] during the 2017–18 season.<ref name="auto"/>

He made his debut for Dunfermline Athletic on 14 August 2018 in a 2–1 victory over [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] in the [[Scottish Challenge Cup]].<ref name="soccerway">{{soccerway|paul-allan/515301|accessdate=17 October 2020}}</ref>

In September 2019, he joined [[Brechin City F.C.|Brechin City]] on loan until January 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.brechincity.com/bcfc/p/n/2198|title=Brechin City Football Club|website=www.brechincity.com}}</ref> In January 2020, the loan was extended until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://dafc.co.uk/story.php?t=The_future_is_bright_as_three_extend_contracts_&ID=11709|title=The future is bright as three extend contracts | Dunfermline Athletic Football Club|website=dafc.co.uk}}</ref> He appeared in 19 league matches for the club, scoring once.<ref name="soccerway" />

In October 2020, Allan joined [[Scottish League Two]] side [[Albion Rovers F.C.|Albion Rovers]] on a season-long loan,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://dafc.co.uk/story.php?t=Paul_Allan_goes_out_on_loan&ID=12626 |title=Paul Allan goes out on loan |publisher=Dunfermline Athletic FC |date=21 October 2020 |accessdate=21 October 2020}}</ref> with the loan being ended by his parent club in January.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://albionroversfc.com/paul-allan-departs/ |title=Paul Allan departs. |publisher=Albion Rovers FC |date=12 January 2021 |accessdate=12 January 2021}}</ref>

In August 2024, Allan left Dunfermline and joined Scottish League One side, Inverness Caledonian Thistle.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-08-24 |title=Inverness Caledonian Thistle have reportedly signed former Dunfermline Athletic midfielder |url=https://www.inverness-courier.co.uk/sport/inverness-caledonian-thistle-have-reportedly-signed-former-d-359334/ |access-date=2025-05-16 |website=Inverness Courier |language=en}}</ref>

'''Luke James Robinson''' (born 20 November 2001) is a professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|left-back]] for {{Scottish football updater|DunfermA}} side [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]].

==Club career==
Born in [[Birkenhead]],<ref name="sw" /> Robinson played youth football for AC Hoylake, [[Wrexham A.F.C.|Wrexham]] and [[Wigan Athletic F.C.|Wigan Athletic]] before starting a two-year scholarship deal with Wigan in summer 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Roberts |first=Les |date=6 November 2017 |title=AC Hoylake star signs scholarship with Wigan |url=https://www.achoylake.com/news/ac-hoylake-star-signs-scholarship-with-wigan-2061653.html |access-date=17 November 2021 |publisher=AC Hoylake}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=21 December 2017 |title=10 youngsters offered scholarships for next season |url=https://wiganathletic.com/news/2017/december/10-youngsters-offered-scholarships-for-next-season/ |access-date=17 November 2021 |publisher=Wigan Athletic F.C.}}</ref> He signed a two-and-a-half-year contract in March 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wylie |first=Jack |date=7 March 2020 |title=Latics Hand Pro To Robinson |url=https://www.lfe.org.uk/news/latics-hand-pro-to-robinson/ |access-date=25 December 2020 |website=lfe.org.uk |publisher=League Football Education}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=6 March 2020 |title=U18 defender Luke Robinson signs professional contract |url=https://wiganathletic.com/news/2020/march/U18-Defender-Luke-Robinson-Signs-Professional-Contract/ |access-date=25 December 2020 |website=wiganathletic.com |publisher=Wigan Athletic F.C.}}</ref> He made his debut for Wigan as a late substitute in a [[EFL League One|League One]] victory over [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]] in December 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kendrick |first=Paul |date=5 December 2020 |title=LIVE BLOG: Sunderland 0 Wigan Athletic 1 |url=https://www.wigantoday.net/sport/football/live-blog-sunderland-0-wigan-athletic-1-3058848 |access-date=25 December 2020 |website=Wigan Today|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221104090253/https://www.wigantoday.net/sport/football/live-blog-sunderland-0-wigan-athletic-1-3058848|archive-date=4 November 2022}}</ref>

In July 2022, Robinson signed a new two-year contract with Wigan.<ref>{{cite web |title=Wigan Athletic defender extends his contract |url=https://www.wigantoday.net/sport/football/wigan-athletic-defender-extends-his-contract-3776375 |website=Wigan Today |access-date=21 July 2022 |date=20 July 2022}}</ref> He proceeded to sign a season-long loan contract at [[Tranmere Rovers F.C.|Tranmere Rovers]], his hometown club.<ref>{{cite web |title=Luke Robinson joins Rovers on loan from Wigan |url=https://www.birkenhead.news/luke-robinson-joins-rovers-on-loan-from-wigan/ |publisher=Birkenhead News |access-date=21 July 2022 |date=21 July 2022}}</ref> He made three appearances for the club, but suffered an ankle injury in training, and did not play again for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web |title=St Johnstone new boy Luke Robinson ready to turn adversity into success |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/st-johnstone/4666339/st-johnstone-fc-luke-robinson-injury/ |website=The Courier |access-date=2 September 2023 |date=25 August 2023}}</ref>

On 22 August 2023, Robinson joined [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] on a season-long loan.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Luke Robinson Signs On A Season Loan |url=https://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/ |access-date=2023-08-22 |website=St Johnstone Football Club |language=en}}</ref> Having been recalled from his loan on 31 December 2023,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://wiganathletic.com/news/2024/january/01/luke-robinson-recalled-from-loan-spell-at-st-johnstone/|title=Luke Robinson recalled from loan spell at St Johnstone|website=wiganathletic.com|date=1 January 2024|accessdate=23 October 2024}}</ref> he returned to the club on loan until the end of the season on 19 January 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk/news/article/luke-robinson-returns-to-saints-on-loan|title=LUKE ROBINSON RETURNS TO SAINTS ON LOAN|website=www.perthstjohnstonefc.co.uk|date=19 January 2024|accessdate=23 October 2024}}</ref>

On 9 May 2025, Wigan announced it had triggered a one year extension of his contract.<ref>{{Cite web   |date=2025-05-09 |title=Wigan Athletic confirms retained list following the 2024/25 season |url=https://wiganathletic.com/news/2025/may/09/wigan-athletic-confirms-retained-list-following-the-2024-25-season/ |access-date=2025-05-14 |publisher=Wigan Athletic FC}}</ref> He was released at the end of the 2025–26 season.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kendrick |first1=Paul |title=Latics Academy product pens emotional farewell at end of 'journey' |url=https://www.wigantoday.net/sport/football/wigan-athletic-academy-product-pens-emotional-farewell-at-end-of-journey-8505862 |website=Wigan Today |access-date=4 August 2026 |date=6 May 2026}}</ref>

On 6 July 2026, Robinson signed a two-year contract with Scottish club [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Dunfermline add fourth summer signing in former Wigan defender |url=https://www.dunfermlinepress.com/sport/26256125.luke-robinson-joins-dunfermline-leaving-wigan/ |website=Dunfermline Press |access-date=4 August 2026 |date=6 July 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
He has played for Scotland internationally at [[Scotland national under-18 football team|under-18]] and [[Scotland national under-19 football team|under-19]] levels.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Luke Robinson | Scotland | Scottish FA |url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/players/?pid=507707 |access-date=25 December 2020 |website=www.scottishfa.co.uk |publisher=Scottish Football Association}}</ref>

'''Kerr David Smith''' (born 12 December 2004) is a Scottish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[centre-back]] for {{Scottish football updater|InvernCT}} club [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]].

He is a product of the [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] academy, and made his [[Scottish Premiership]] debut there in 2021 aged 16, before joining Aston Villa in January 2022.

== Early life ==
Smith was born in [[Dundee]] on 12 December 2004 and grew up in [[Montrose, Angus]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Kerr Smith |url=https://www.arabarchive.co.uk/player.php?id=1980 |access-date=21 March 2021 |work=Arab Archive}}</ref> Smith attended Lochside Primary School in Montrose, Angus and [[St John's Roman Catholic High School|St John's RC High School]] in Dundee. Smith played for the [[Brechin City F.C.|Brechin City]] Boys Club as a child before starting an association with the Dundee United academy at seven years old.<ref>{{Cite web |title=KERR SMITH MAKES PREMIER LEAGUE SWITCH |url=https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/news/7157/KERR-SMITH-MAKES-PREMIER-LEAGUE-SWITCH.html |access-date=2023-08-29 |website=Dundee United Football Club |language=en}}</ref>

== Club career ==

=== Dundee United ===
Smith was developed through [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]]'s academy. At the age of 15, he appeared for a youthful Dundee United team in a friendly match against [[Premier League]] club [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]] in August 2020, which was abandoned after 45 minutes.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Woodger |first1=Calum |title=Dundee United A-A Sheffield United: Friendly called to a halt as Blades led through Sharp at sodden Tannadice |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-united/1533736/dundee-united-sheffield-united-friendly-abandoned/ |access-date=21 March 2021 |work=The Courier |date=25 August 2020 |location=Dundee}}</ref> In the next few weeks, he had trials with Premier League clubs [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]], [[Everton F.C.]] and [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Nicolson |first1=Eric |title=EXCLUSIVE: Highly-rated young Dundee United defender Kerr Smith goes down south with Aston Villa |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-united/1616119/exclusive-highly-rated-young-dundee-united-defender-kerr-smith-to-join-aston-villa/ |access-date=21 March 2021 |work=The Courier |date=30 September 2020 |location=Dundee}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Nicolson |first1=Eric |title=EXCLUSIVE: Dundee United hot prospect Kerr Smith has spent a week training with Manchester United |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-united/1679737/dundee-united-kerr-smith-manchester-united-transfer-news/ |access-date=21 March 2021 |work=The Courier |date=27 October 2020 |location=Dundee}}</ref> Despite interest from those clubs and others in England, Smith decided to sign his first professional contract with Dundee United upon reaching his 16th birthday in December 2020, under contract until 2023.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Banks |first1=Ben |title=Kerr Smith signs first Dundee United deal amid Manchester United interest |url=https://www.nottheoldfirm.com/news/kerr-smith-signs-first-dundee-united-deal-amid-manchester-united-interest/ |access-date=21 March 2021 |work=Not The Old Firm |date=18 December 2020}}</ref> He was immediately allocated a first team squad number of 43<ref>{{cite news |title=Kerr Smith signs first professional contract at Tannadice |url=https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/news/6703/KERR-SMITH-SIGNS-FIRST-PROFESSIONAL-CONTRACT-AT-TANNADICE.html |access-date=21 March 2021 |publisher=Dundee United F.C. |date=12 December 2020}}</ref> and was an unused substitute in United's [[Scottish Premiership]] match against [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] the following day.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Pirie |first1=Mark |title=Dundee United vs Rangers - Live updates |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/dundee-united-vs-rangers-live-23159707 |access-date=21 March 2021 |work=Daily Record |date=13 December 2020}}</ref>

He made his competitive senior debut for Dundee United as a late substitute in their 4–1 Premiership defeat against Rangers at [[Ibrox Stadium]] on 21 February 2021.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Cairney |first1=James |title=Rangers 4-1 Dundee United: How the visitors rated in Premiership loss |url=https://www.glasgowtimes.co.uk/sport/19107132.rangers-4-1-dundee-united-visitors-rated-premiership-loss/ |access-date=21 March 2021 |work=Glasgow Times |date=21 February 2021}}</ref> He then made his first starting appearance in a 3–0 defeat against [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] at [[Rugby Park]] on 21 April 2021.<ref>{{cite news |title=Job not done after Killie win - Wright |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56564074 |access-date=23 April 2021 |work=BBC Sport |date=22 April 2021}}</ref>

=== Aston Villa ===
On 14 January 2022, English [[Premier League]] club [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] announced Smith as a new signing for their [[Aston Villa F.C. Under-23s and Academy|Academy]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=14 January 2022|title=Smith joins Villa Academy|url=https://www.avfc.co.uk/news/2022/january/14/smith-joins-villa-academy/|access-date=2022-01-14|website=Aston Villa Football Club}}</ref> The transfer fee was undisclosed, but was reported to be worth up to £2 million.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Hamilton|first=Sean|title=Kerr Smith seals move from Dundee United to Aston Villa|url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-united/2911062/kerr-smith-seals-move-from-dundee-united-to-aston-villa/|access-date=2022-01-14|website=The Courier|date=14 January 2022 |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==== St Johnstone loan ====
On 2 January 2024, Smith signed a professional contract with Aston Villa. The same day he joined Scottish Premiership club [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] on loan until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2024-01-02 |title=Kerr Smith pens pro deal and seals loan |url=https://www.avfc.co.uk/news/2024/january/02/smith-pens-pro-deal-and-seals-loan/ |access-date=2024-01-02 |website=Aston Villa Football Club}}</ref> Smith made his debut as a late substitute in a 1–0 victory over [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] on 3 February.<ref>{{Cite news |date=3 February 2024 |title=St Johnstone sink County in long-awaited away win |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68115004 |access-date=2024-02-05 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> Smith returned to Aston Villa in March 2024, after suffering a season ending injury.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Nicolson |first=Eric |date=2024-03-15 |title=Kerr Smith injury ends St Johnstone loan spell |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/st-johnstone/4923006/st-johnstone-kerr-smith-hamstring-injury/ |access-date=2025-05-06 |website=The Courier |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==== Barrow loan ====
On 15 August 2025, Smith signed for [[EFL League Two]] club [[Barrow A.F.C.|Barrow]] on a season-long loan.<ref>{{Cite web |date=15 August 2025 |title=Kerr Smith: Barrow sign Aston Villa U21 defender on loan |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cz0yx00vg7no |access-date=15 August 2025 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

On 10 June 2026, the Premier League released list showed that Smith's Aston Villa contract was set to expire on 30 June.<ref>{{Cite web |date=10 June 2026 |title=Premier League clubs' released lists - who's set for free transfer? |url=https://www.premierleague.com/en/news/4672506/premier-league-clubs-202526-released-lists-whos-set-for-free-transfer |access-date=15 June 2026 |website=Premier League |language=en}}</ref>

=== Inverness Caledonian Thistle ===
On 17 July 2026, Smith signed for [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] on a one-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2026-07-17 |title=Kerr Smith signs for ICTFC |url=https://ictfc.com/kerr-smith-signs-for-ictfc/ |access-date=2026-07-20 |website=Inverness Caledonian Thistle FC |language=en-GB}}</ref> He made his debut on 21 August 2026, as a late substitute in a 1–1 league draw against [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=21 August 2026 |title=Inverness CT vs Partick Thistle: Scottish Championship - BBC Scotland TV stream |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cj75gg2nd67pt |access-date=27 August 2026 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

== International career ==
Smith made his debut for the [[Scotland national under-19 football team|Scotland U19]] team in a 3–0 victory over [[Gibraltar national under-19 football team|Gibraltar]] in a [[2022 UEFA European Under-19 Championship qualification]] match on 13 November 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-11-13|title=Four Rangers teens involved as Scotland under-19s win 3-0 in Croatia|url=https://www.rangersnews.uk/international/four-rangers-teens-involved-as-scotland-under-19s-win-3-0-in-croatia/|access-date=2022-01-14|website=Rangers News|language=en-GB|archive-date=15 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220115062650/https://www.rangersnews.uk/international/four-rangers-teens-involved-as-scotland-under-19s-win-3-0-in-croatia/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

He was selected for the Scotland under-21 squad in Oct 2023 but was not capped.

King joined [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] in his early years,<ref>{{Cite web|date=10 March 2020|title=Introducing... Leon King|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W6G7IBkYd7M|access-date=3 May 2021|website=[[Rangers F.C.]]|publisher=Youtube}}</ref> soon appearing to be one of the club's brightest prospects.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Campbell|first=Jordan|date=Nov 9, 2019|title=Chelsea and Liverpool among those looking at Rangers' 15-year-old defender King|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1285129/2019/11/09/chelsea-and-liverpool-among-those-looking-rangers-15-year-old-defender-king/|access-date=2021-05-23|website=[[The Athletic]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Wright|first=Angus|date=9 November 2019|title=Rangers face fight to keep hold of 15-year-old defender as English and European giants circle|url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/rangers/latest-rangers-news/rangers-face-fight-keep-hold-15-year-old-defender-english-and-european-giants-circle-1402839|access-date=2021-05-23|website=[[The Scotsman]]|language=en}}</ref> He made his [[Rangers F.C. Under-20s and Academy|Rangers Under-20s]] debut aged only 14 under the management of [[Graeme Murty]] in November 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2018-11-26|title=Rangers Academy continues to go from strength to strength|url=https://www.rangersnews.uk/news/rangers-academy-continues-to-go-from-strength-to-strength/|access-date=2021-05-23|website=Rangers News|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=27 November 2018|title=Rangers U20s 6-1 Partick Thistle U20s|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7ekWg_ah-Mg|access-date=3 May 2021|website=[[Rangers F.C.]]|publisher=Youtube}}</ref> At the end of the [[2018–19 Rangers F.C. season|2018–19]] season, he was also part of the squad that won the [[Scottish Youth Cup]] against [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]].<ref>{{cite web|date=25 April 2019|title=Rangers crowned Scottish Youth Cup winners|url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/news/rangers-crowned-scottish-youth-cup-winners/?rid=2112|access-date=23 May 2021|publisher=[[Scottish Football Association|SFA]]}}</ref>

King made his Rangers debut on 29 November 2020 in a [[Scottish League Cup|League Cup]] match against [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Falkirk 0–4 Rangers |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55031996|website=BBC Sport|last=Elgott|first=Jordan |date=29 November 2020}}</ref> He made his [[Scottish Premiership]] debut for on 12 May 2021, replacing [[Joe Aribo]] in the 86th minute of a 3–0 away win against [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=McDougall|first=Mark|date=2021-05-12|title=Livingston 0 Rangers 3 as Steven Gerrard's men edge closer to 100 point mark|url=https://www.glasgowlive.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/livingston-v-rangers-live-score-20581889|access-date=2021-05-12|website=Glasgow Live|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last=Campbell|first=Andy|date=2021-05-12|title=Rangers win to stay unbeaten in league|language=en-GB|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56990121|access-date=2021-05-12}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Black|first=James|date=2021-05-13|title=Rangers veteran delighted after landmark appearance for Ibrox prodigy in Livi win|url=https://www.hitc.com/en-gb/2021/05/13/rangers-mclaughlin-leon-king/|access-date=2021-05-23|website=HITC|language=en-GB}}</ref>

On 5 January 2022, King signed a contract extension until the summer of 2024 and was subsequently promoted to the first-team squad on a full time basis.<ref>{{ Cite news | url=https://www.rangers.co.uk/article/leon-king-signs-new-rangers-contract/61x8l6r15jXye1NvVNPIH5| work=Rangers.co.uk | publisher=Rangers Football Club| date=5 January 2022| title=LEON KING SIGNS NEW RANGERS CONTRACT }}</ref>

On 7 September 2022, King made his debut for Rangers in the [[UEFA Champions League]] group stage, coming on as a half time substitute vs [[AFC Ajax |Ajax]]. He made his full starting debut in the competition on 4 October 2022 against [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] at [[Anfield]]. Due to injuries to other defenders, King would feature in all Rangers Champions League fixtures that campaign.

On 7 September 2025, King joined [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]] on loan until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c20z6z9132vo|title=Rangers defender King joins Ayr United on loan|publisher=BBC|date=7 September 2025|accessdate=8 September 2025}}</ref> Whilst with the club he won multiple of their end of season awards including Men's Player of the Year.<ref name="POTY">{{cite web|url=https://ayrunitedfc.co.uk/player-of-the-year-winners|title=Player of the Year Winners|publisher=[[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]]|date=27 April 2026|accessdate=16 July 2026}}</ref>

===Ayr United===
On 16 July 2026, it was confirmed that King had signed a two year deal to join Ayr United permanently.<ref name="AyrSign"/>

== International career ==
King was selected for the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland under-21]] squad in May 2022.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/61507036 |title=Rangers' Alex Lowry one of five new call-ups by Scotland Under-21s |website=BBC Sport |date=19 May 2022 |access-date=19 May 2022}}</ref>

'''Rory MacLeod''' (born 3 February 2006) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[forward (association football)|forward]] or [[right winger]] for [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]].

==Club career==
In December 2021, aged only 15, MacLeod signed his first professional deal with [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/news/7140/RORY-MACLEOD-SIGNS-PRO-DEAL.html|title=Rory MacLeod Signs Pro-Deal|publisher=[[Dundee United F.C.]]|date=23 December 2021|accessdate=10 February 2022}}</ref> On 9 February 2022, he became Dundee United's youngest player ever at the age of 16 years and 6 days when he came on as a late substitute in a 2–0 win over [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-united/2996958/rory-mcleod-becomes-youngest-ever-dundee-united-player-as-tam-courts-hails-goal-hero-tony-watt/|title=Rory MacLeod becomes youngest ever Dundee United player as Tam Courts hails goal hero Tony Watt|website=thecourier.co.uk|date=9 February 2022|accessdate=10 February 2022}}</ref> On 14 September 2023, MacLeod joined [[Scottish League Two]] side [[Forfar Athletic F.C.|Forfar Athletic]] on loan until January 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/news/8023/RORY-MACLEOD-JOINS-FORFAR-ATHLETIC-ON-SHORT-TERM-LOAN-.html|title=Rory Macleod Joins Forfar Athletic on Short-Term Loan |publisher=[[Dundee United F.C.]]|date=14 September 2023|accessdate=15 September 2023}}</ref>

On 30 August 2024, he joined [[Premier League]] side [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] on a season-long loan, joining the [[Southampton F.C. Under-21s and Academy|Under-21 squad]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=31 August 2024 |title=Academy seal four deadline day signings |url=https://www.southamptonfc.com/en/news/article/academy-seal-four-deadline-day-signings |access-date=31 August 2024 |website=Southampton FC}}</ref>

On 11 July 2025, Macleod joined [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] on a permanent deal for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/news/8985/RORY-MACLEOD-JOINS-DUNFERMLINE-ATHLETIC-FOR-AN-UNDISCLOSED-FEE.html|title=RORY MACLEOD JOINS DUNFERMLINE ATHLETIC FOR AN UNDISCLOSED FEE|publisher=[[Dundee United F.C.]]|date=11 July 2025|accessdate=1 September 2025}}</ref> His start with the club was interrupted by a spell in hospital to treat a throat abscess.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://dafc.co.uk/rory-macleod-back-from-hospital-ordeal/|title=Rory Macleod – Back from Hospital Ordeal|publisher=[[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.]]|date=18 August 2025|accessdate=1 September 2025}}</ref>

==International career==
In October 2021, MacLeod was called up the [[Scotland national under-16 football team|Scotland under-16]] squad for their [[Victory Shield]] matches.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/news/mclaren-names-squad-for-victory-shield/|title=McLaren names squad for Victory Shield|publisher=[[Scottish FA]]|date=1 October 2021|accessdate=10 February 2022}}</ref> He scored in victory over [[Wales national under-16 football team|Wales U16]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-united/2676684/dundee-united-rory-macleod-goal-as-scotland-victory-shield/|title=Dundee United kid notches crucial goal as Scotland share Victory Shield glory in Belfast|website=thecourier.co.uk|date=22 October 2021|accessdate=10 February 2022}}</ref> In February 2022, he received his first call-up to the [[Scotland national under-17 football team|Scotland under-17]] squad.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/news/7204/YOUNG-TERRORS-MOORE-ODONNELL--MACLEOD-TO-REPRESENT-SCOTLAND.html|title=Young Terrors Moore, O'Donnell & MacLeod to Represent Scotland|publisher=[[Dundee United F.C.]]|date=8 February 2022|accessdate=10 February 2022}}</ref> In August 2023, he was called up to the [[Scotland national under-19 football team|under–19]] squad for the first time.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/news/scotland-under-19-squad-confirmed-for-friendlies-in-belgium/|title=Scotland Under-19 squad confirmed for friendlies in Belgium|website=scottishfa.co.uk|date=22 August 2023|accessdate=15 September 2023}}</ref>

'''Cale Loughrey''' ({{IPAc-en|l|ɒ|k|'|r|iː|}} {{respell|LOCK|ree}}, born August 4, 2001) is a Canadian Scottish [[association football|professional soccer]] player who plays as a [[centre-back]] for [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]]

== Early life ==
Loughrey was born in [[Toronto]], Ontario, Canada<ref name=":0" /> to a [[Scotland|Scottish]] father (originally from Clydebank, West Dunbartonshire) and a Canadian mother;<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Thomson |first=Paul |date=August 4, 2025 |title=Accies' Canadian signing Loughrey says his dad is 'pumped' to see him make move |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/hamilton-accies-canadian-signing-cale-35669161 |access-date=September 17, 2025 |website=[[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]]}}</ref> he also holds a [[British passport]].<ref name=":1" />

==College career==
In 2019, he attended [[Seneca College]], playing for the men's soccer team.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=https://www.senecasting.ca/sports/msoc/2019-20/bios/loughrey_cale_y8or|title=Cale Loughrey Seneca Sting profile|work=[[Seneca College]]}}</ref> In his only season with Seneca, he was named team captain and MVP.<ref name=UAB>{{cite web|url=https://uabsports.com/sports/mens-soccer/roster/cale-loughrey/8807|title=Cale Loughrey UAB profile|work=[[UAB Blazers]]}}</ref> He was also named an OCAA East Division First-Team All-Star.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.league1ontario.com/news_article/show/1061681|title=League1 Men's Players Sweep Up At OUA/ OCAA Awards With 11 Individual And 55 All-Star Awards|date=November 5, 2019|work=[[League1 Ontario]]}}</ref>

In 2020, he moved to the [[University of Alabama at Birmingham]], playing for the [[UAB Blazers men's soccer|men's soccer team]].<ref name=newplayer>{{Cite web|url=https://uabsports.com/news/2020/8/18/uab-mens-soccer-new-player-profiles-linares-loughrey-and-robicheaux.aspx?fbclid=IwAR3dTwQTY2WBhtWXRuu6mnx8sDeqCE05zP5RRqZMcilLW5-jy1s6anyDlpc|title=UAB Men's Soccer New Player Profiles: Linares, Loughrey and Robicheaux|date=August 18, 2020|work=[[UAB Blazers]]}}</ref> He scored his first goal on September 26, 2020, against the [[Georgia Southern Eagles men's soccer|Georgia Southern Eagles]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://uabsports.com/news/2020/9/26/late-rally-comes-up-short-as-uab-mens-soccer-drops-3-2-decision-to-georgia-southern.aspx|title=Late Rally Comes Up Short as UAB Men's Soccer Drops 3-2 Decision to Georgia Southern|work=[[UAB Blazers]]|date=September 26, 2020}}</ref> He was named a Conference USA Third Team All Star for the 2020–21 season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://uabsports.com/news/2021/4/20/mens-soccer-four-blazers-tabbed-all-conference-team-honors|title=Four Blazers Tabbed All-Conference Team Honors|date=April 20, 2021|work=[[UAB Blazers]]}}</ref>

==Club career==

===League1 Ontario===
In 2018, Loughrey played for [[Darby FC]] in [[League1 Ontario]].<ref name=2018stats>{{cite web|url=https://league1ontario.sportngin.com/roster_players/24797004|title=Cale Loughrey 2018 L1O Stats|work=[[League1 Ontario]]}}</ref>

In early 2019, he trained with [[Canadian Premier League]] club [[York9 FC]].<ref name=running>{{cite web|url=https://northerntribune.ca/forge-fc-2022-roster-update/|title=Running Through The Six: A Look At Forge's New Signings|date=February 15, 2022|work=Northern Tribune|first=John|last=Jacques}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://northerntribune.ca/neighbour-cale-loughrey-fraser-aird/|title=Once Neighbours, Cale And Fraser Now Stand On Opposite Al Classico Battle Lines|date=May 6, 2022|work=Northern Tribune|first=John|last=Jacques}}</ref> In 2019, he played for [[Unionville Milliken SC]] in League1 Ontario,<ref name=2019stats>{{cite web|url=https://league1ontario.sportngin.com/roster_players/32720262|title=Cale Loughrey 2019 L1O Stats|work=[[League1 Ontario]]}}</ref> scoring his first goal on June 22 against [[Aurora FC (Canada)|Aurora FC]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.league1ontario.com/news_article/show/1030508|title=Darby's Sears Sinks Masters And Determined Durham Get Win In Ottawa|date=June 23, 2019|work=[[League1 Ontario]]}}</ref> He played in the CPL U21 showcase match for Team Ontario being named MVP.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://canpl.ca/article/ontario-quebec-rosters-revealed-for-cpl-u-21-showcase-match|work=[[Canadian Premier League]]|date=November 8, 2019|title=Ontario, Quebec rosters revealed for CPL U-21 Showcase Match}}</ref><ref name=newplayer />

===Canadian Premier League===
In February 2022, he signed a contract with [[Forge FC]] of the [[Canadian Premier League]].<ref name=running /> He made his debut on February 16 in a [[CONCACAF Champions League]] match against Mexican side [[Cruz Azul]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://canpl.ca/article/match-analysis-forge-fc-0-1-cruz-azul-concacaf-champions-league|title=Match Analysis: Forge FC 0-1 Cruz Azul — Concacaf Champions League|first=Charlie|last=O'Connor-Clarke|date=February 16, 2022|work=[[Canadian Premier League]]}}</ref> 

[[File:Cale Loughrey, FC Edmonton.jpg|thumb|Loughrey with [[FC Edmonton]] in 2022|left]]
On March 30, 2022, he was loaned to fellow CPL club [[FC Edmonton]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jacques |first=John |date=5 April 2022 |title=Two In, Two Out: Forge Signs Players, Makes Loans To Edmonton |url=https://northerntribune.ca/forge-fc-edmonton-loan-bontis/ |website=Northern Tribune}}</ref> He made 25 appearances for Edmonton across all competitions, becoming a free agent at the end of the season, upon the expiry of his contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://hfxfootballpost.ca/after-stints-with-fc-edmonton-and-forge-cale-loughrey-is-embracing-role-with-hfx-wanderers-if-theres-anybody-i-could-trust-its-patrice/|title=After stints with FC Edmonton and Forge, Cale Loughrey is embracing role with HFX Wanderers: 'If there's anybody I could trust, it's Patrice'|first=Josh|last=Healey|date=June 7, 2023|work=HFX Football Post}}</ref>

web|url=https://hfxwanderersfc.canpl.ca/article/incredible-grit-and-desire-wanderers-sign-canadian-defender-cale-loughrey|title='Incredible grit and desire': Wanderers sign Canadian defender Cale ===Romania===
On January 27, 2025, Loughrey signed with Romanian [[Liga II]] club [[CS Corvinul Hunedoara|Corvinul Hunedoara]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sport.ro/fotbal-intern/un-canadian-in-romania-corvinul-hunedoara-anunta-un-transfer-exotic-de-peste-ocean.html|title=Un canadian în România: Corvinul Hunedoara anunță un transfer exotic de peste ocean|trans-title=A Canadian in Romania: Corvinul Hunedoara announces an exotic transfer from overseas|language=ro|date=January 27, 2025|work=Sport.ro}}</ref>

===Scotland===
On August 2, 2025, he joined [[Scottish League One]] club [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]], following a successful trial period; he signed a one-year amateur contract,<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=August 2, 2025 |title=Welcome To Hamilton, Cale Loughrey |url=https://hamiltonacciesfc.co.uk/welcome-to-hamilton-cale-loughrey/ |access-date=September 17, 2025 |website=Hamilton Accies}}</ref> due to the [[transfer embargo]] imposed to the club by the [[SPFL]] for repeatedly failing to settle their tax obligations.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{cite web |date=July 25, 2025 |title=SPFL statement – Hamilton Academical |url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/spfl-statement-hamilton-academical |accessdate=September 17, 2025 |work=[[SPFL]]}}</ref> He made his debut for Hamilton later the same day, starting in a 2–0 [[2025–26 Scottish League One|league]] win over [[Montrose F.C.|Montrose]].<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=August 2, 2025 |title=Hamilton Academical vs Montrose: Scottish League One stats & head-to-head |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cn47ynj032yt |access-date=September 17, 2025 |website=[[BBC Sport]]}}</ref>

On January 13, 2026, Loughrey signed an 18 month contract with [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/cale-loughrey-joins-the-jags-from-hamilton-accies/|title=Cale Loughrey joins the Jags from Hamilton Accies|date=January 13, 2026|work=[[Partick Thistle F.C.]]}}</ref> On the same day, Loughrey made his Thistle debut and scored his first goal for the club in a [[Scottish Challenge Cup]] tie with [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-match-report/partick-thistle-v-inverness-c-t-13th-january-2026/|title=Partick Thistle v Inverness C.T. – 13th January 2026|date=January 14, 2026|work=[[Partick Thistle F.C.]]}}</ref>

'''Adam Mackinnon''' (born 30 April 2003) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[central midfielder]] for [[Scottish League One]] side [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]].

==Career==
===Ross County===
Mackinnon made his he made his debut for County on 14 November 2020 in the [[Scottish League Cup]] against [[Stirling Albion F.C.|Stirling Albion]].<ref name=":0">{{cite web |date=14 November 2020 |title=Ross County 3-0 Stirling Albion |url=https://spfl.co.uk/league/league-cup/results/2127695 |website=spfl.co.uk |accessdate=14 November 2020}}</ref> After returning from a loan spell with Brora, Mackinnon made his league debut for County on 26 February 2022 in a 3–1 win against [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] coming on for [[Harry Paton (soccer)|Harry Paton]] in the 90th minute.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ross County 3-1 St Johnstone|url= https://spfl.co.uk/league/premiership/results/2209236 |publisher=Hebrides news|date=26 February 2022|accessdate=26 February 2022}}</ref>

==== Loans ====
On 20 November 2020 Mackinnon joined [[Highland Football League]] side [[Brora Rangers F.C.|Brora Rangers]] ahead of the new season.<ref>{{cite news |title= Loan spells for Graduates |url= https://www.northern-times.co.uk/sport/ross-county-midfielder-goes-on-loan-to-brora-rangers-218932/|publisher=Northern Times|date=20 November 2020|access-date= 20 November 2020}}</ref> Mackinnon rejoined Brora on 30 August 2021 on a six-month loan from County.<ref>{{cite news |title= Loan spells for Graduates |url= https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/highland-league/3430645/brora-sign-adam-mackinnon-on-loan-while-clachs-shaun-sutherland-signs-extension/|publisher=Press and Journal|date=30 August 2021|access-date=30 August 2021}}</ref>

Mackinnon was loaned to [[Scottish League One]] club [[Montrose F.C.|Montrose]] in the summer of 2022. He was recalled from loan on 27 December 2022 to be assessed by County manager [[Malky Mackay]].<ref>{{cite web|title= Ross County to assess next steps for Matthew Wright and Adam Mackinnon following recall from Montrose|url= https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/ross-county/5216404/ross-county-to-assess-next-steps-for-matthew-wright-and-adam-mackinnon-following-recall-from-montrose/|publisher=Press and Journal|date=29 December 2022|accessdate=29 December 2022}}</ref> On 27 January 2023, Mackinnon would return on loan for the ''Gable Endies'' until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mackinnon returns to Montrose on loan |url=https://www.rosscountyfootballclub.co.uk/news-items/mackinnon-returns-to-montrose-on-loan |access-date=2023-01-27 |website=RCFC |language=en}}</ref>

On 7 October 2023 Mackinnon was loaned to [[Highland Football League|Highland League]] side [[Brora Rangers F.C.|Brora Rangers]] till the end of the 23/24 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adam Mackinnon joins the Cattachs on loan! |url=https://www.rosscountyfootballclub.co.uk/news-items/adam-mackinnon-joins-the-cattachs-on-loan |access-date=2023-12-20 |website=RCFC |language=en}}</ref>

In January 2024, Mackinnon joined [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]] on loan until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-01-12 |title=Adam MacKinnon |url=https://www.arbroathfc.co.uk/adam-mackinnon/ |access-date=2024-01-15 |website=Arbroath FC |language=en}}</ref>

===Inverness Caledonian Thistle===
In August 2024, Mackinnon joined [[Scottish League One]] club [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] on a 2 Year Contract.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-02-08 |title=Adam Mackinnon Signs For ICTFC|url=https://ictfc.com/adam-mackinnon-signs-for-ictfc/|access-date=2024-02-08 |website=Inverness CT |language=en}}</ref>

He spent the second half of the 2022–23 season on [[Loan (sports)|loan]] at [[Port Vale F.C.|Port Vale]] and was loaned out to Dundee for the 2023–24 season. He joined [[Colchester United F.C.|Colchester United]] on loan ahead of the 2024–25 season before joining Dundee permanently in January 2025. ==Early and personal life== Aaron Martin Donnelly was born on 8 June 2003 in [[Magherafelt]] to Noel and Martina.{{cite news |last1=Baggaley |first1=Michael |title=Port Vale defender Aaron Donnelly confirms unlikely Ant & Dec connection |url=https://www.stokesentinel.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/aaron-donnelly-port-vale-dec-8314356 |access-date=1 April 2023 |work=StokeonTrentLive |date=1 April 2023 |language=en}} He has family from [[Newcastle upon Tyne]] and is related to [[Dec Donnelly]]. '''Layton Rhys Stewart''' (born 3 September 2002) is an English professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Striker (association football)|striker]] for [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Layton Stewart {{!}} Football Stats {{!}} Thun {{!}} Age 24 {{!}} Soccer Base |url=https://www.soccerbase.com/players/player.sd?player_id=125534 |access-date=2026-09-18 |website=www.soccerbase.com}}</ref>

==Career==
Stewart was named in the Liverpool first team squad for the first time in December 2019, for an [[2019–20 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]] tie with [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]]. Liverpool had named a squad of Academy players due to the first team competing in the [[2019 FIFA Club World Cup]] in [[Qatar]] in the same week.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/liverpool-aston-villa-longstaff-kane-17430446|title=Three Liverpool youngsters to watch out for against Aston Villa|last=Addison|first=Matt|date=17 December 2019|website=Liverpool Echo|access-date=10 November 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Aston Villa 5:0 Liverpool |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50723225 |website=[[BBC Sport]] |access-date=10 November 2022 |date=17 December 2019}}</ref>

From [[Huyton]], Stewart signed his first professional contract with Liverpool in February 2020. Despite suffering an anterior cruciate injury to his knee the club gave him a new contract in May 2021 as he was undergoing rehabilitation.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/liverpool-striker-contract-injury-rehab-20571931|title=Liverpool striker signs new long-term contract as injury rehab continues|website=Liverpool Echo}}</ref>

On 9 November 2022, Stewart made his senior debut when he started for
Liverpool in a win against [[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]] in the third round of the [[2022–23 EFL Cup]] at [[Anfield]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2022/nov/09/liverpool-derby-county-carabao-cup-match-report|title=Kelleher's shootout saves see Liverpool scrape past Derby in Carabao Cup|date=9 November 2022|work=[[The Guardian]]|accessdate=10 November 2022}}</ref>

===Preston North End===
On 22 July 2023, Stewart joined [[Preston North End F.C.|Preston North End]] on a three-year deal for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{cite news |title=Layton Stewart Joins PNE From Liverpool In Permanent Deal |url=https://www.pnefc.net/news/2023/july/layton-stewart-joins-pne-from-liverpool-in-permanent-deal/ |access-date=22 July 2023 |publisher=Preston North End |date=22 July 2023 |language=en-gb}}</ref> On 23 September 2023, Stewart made his debut for Preston in a 1–1 draw with [[Rotherham United F.C.|Rotherham United]], coming off the bench in the 88th minute.

On 3 January 2025, Stewart joined [[Swiss Challenge League]] leaders [[FC Thun]] on loan until the end of the season with an option to buy.<ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.fcthun.ch/de/news/2024/layton-stewart-zum-fc-thun|trans-title=Layton Stewart joins FC Thun from Preston North End|title=Layton Stewart stösst von Preston North End zum FC Thun|language=German|website=www.fcthun.ch|date=3 January 2025|accessdate=3 January 2025}}</ref>

=== Inverness Caledonian Thistle ===
On 18 September 2026, Stewart signed for [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-09-18 |title=Inverness snap up former Liverpool youth striker |url=https://www.inverness-courier.co.uk/sport/inverness-snap-up-former-liverpool-youth-striker-445372/ |access-date=2026-09-18 |website=Inverness Courier |language=en}}</ref> Stewart made his debut, and scored his first goal for the club, the following day against [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] in a 2–2 away draw.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-09-19 |title=Debut goal helps ICT to result at Livingston |url=https://www.inverness-courier.co.uk/sport/debut-goal-helps-ict-to-result-at-livingston-445425/ |access-date=2026-09-19 |website=Inverness Courier |language=en}}</ref>

'''Oliver Charlie Thomas''' (born 18 April 2005) is an English professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a striker for [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]].

==Early life==
Born in [[Bristol]], Thomas grew up in the district of [[Bradley Stoke]]. He played for Mangotsfield and represented South Gloucestershire before joining Bristol City at the Under-16 level.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bcfc.co.uk/news/thomas-heads-to-yeovil-town-on-loan/|date=20 July 2023|website=bcfc.co.uk|title= THOMAS HEADS TO YEOVIL TOWN ON LOAN}}</ref>

==Career==
In January 2023 Thomas joined [[Bath City F.C.|Bath City]] on loan from [[Bristol City F.C.|Bristol City]] for the remainder of the 2022–23 season. He played for Bath on 7 January 2023 against [[Eastbourne Borough F.C.|Eastbourne Borough]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bathcityfc.com/player/callum-ebanks/|title=Olly Thomas|website=Bathcityfc}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bcfc.co.uk/news/academy-trio-head-out-on-loan/|title=ACADEMY TRIO HEAD OUT ON LOAN|website=bcfc.co.uk}}</ref> However, by the end of the month he was recalled by Bristol City following the sale of [[Antoine Semenyo]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bristolpost.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/bristol-city-west-brom-live-8085081|title=Bristol City 3–0 West Brom live: Reaction as Bell's double and Scott send Robins through|website=Bristol Post}}</ref> Thomas had a senior Bristol City first team match day experience being named as a substitute in the [[FA Cup]] against [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Brom]] on 28 January 2023.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://uk.soccerway.com/matches/2023/01/28/england/fa-cup/bristol-city-fc/west-bromwich-albion-football-club/4015420/|title=BRISTOL CITY VS. WEST BROM|website=Soccerway}}</ref> He continued to train with the first team.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bristolpost.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/nigel-pearson-bristol-city-academy-8207472|title= Marlee Francois and the 11 Bristol City academy players Nigel Pearson has handed debuts to|first=Richard|last=Forrester|date=March 2, 2023|accessdate=March 23, 2023}}</ref> In March 2023, it was revealed that Thomas had signed a professional contract with Bristol City, agreeing a two-year contract until the summer of 2025.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bcfc.co.uk/news/new-pro-deals-for-academy-six|website=bcfc.co.uk|title=NEW PRO DEALS FOR ACADEMY SIX|date=March 24, 2023|accessdate=March 24, 2023}}</ref>

In July 2023, Thomas joined [[Yeovil Town F.C.|Yeovil Town]] of the [[National League South]], on a six-month loan.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gloverscast.co.uk/teenage-striker-arrives-from-city/|website=Gloverscast|accessdate=21 July 2023|title=Teenage Striker arrives from Bristol City|date=20 July 2023}}</ref> He made his debut for Yeovil against [[Hemel Hempstead F.C.|Hemel Hempstead]] on 5 August 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gloverscast.co.uk/match-report-hemel-hempstead-town-1-yeovil-town-0/|access-date=6 August 2023|website=Gloverscast|title= MATCH REPORT: HEMEL HEMPSTEAD TOWN 1 YEOVIL TOWN 0|first=David|last=Coates|date=August 5, 2023}}</ref> On 15 August 2023, he scored his first goal for Yeovil against [[Truro City F.C.|Truro City]]. He was recalled by Bristol City from the loan on 31 August 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gloverscast.co.uk/olly-thomas-returns-to-bristol-city/|website=Gloverscast.co.uk|title= OLLY THOMAS RETURNS TO BRISTOL CITY |first=David|last=Coates|date=August 31, 2023|accessdate=August 31, 2023}}</ref> The following day he joined [[EFL League Two]] side [[Newport County F.C.|Newport County]] on a season-long loan.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.bcfc.co.uk/academy-news/thomas-joins-newport-county-on-loan/|website=bcfc.co.uk|date=1 September 2023|accessdate=1 September 2023|title= Thomas joins Newport County on loan}}</ref> He made his debut for Newport on 2 September 2023, at home against [[AFC Wimbledon]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://uk.soccerway.com/matches/2023/09/02/england/league-two/newport-county-afc/afc-wimbledon/4088090/|title=NEWPORT VS. WIMBLEDON 2–2|date=2 September 2023|accessdate=2 September 2023|website=Soccerway}}</ref> On 24 November 2023, Thomas was recalled by Bristol City.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.newport-county.co.uk/news/20232/november/olly-thomas-returns-to-bristol-city/ |title=Olly Thomas Returns to Bristol City |work=newport-county.co.uk |date=24 November 2023 |access-date=24 November 2023 }}</ref> On 29 January 2024, Thomas re-joined Yeovil Town in the National League South on loan until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 29, 2024 |title=Olly Thomas returns to Huish Park |url=https://www.ytfc.net/signing-olly-thomas-returns-to-huish-park/ |access-date=2024-01-29 |website=Yeovil Town Football Club}}</ref>

Thomas made his senior league debut for Bristol City in a 1–0 win in the [[EFL Championship]] at home against [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]] on 25 October 2025.<ref> {{cite web|website=Bristol World |accessdate=25 October 2025|date=25 October 2025|url=https://www.bristolworld.com/sport/football/bristol-city/bristol-city-armstrong-birmingham-championship-5375143#|title= Bristol City player ratings as 'hero' 8/10 and six 7.5/10s send Robins jubilant in 1–0 Birmingham win|first=Harvey|last= Maggs}}</ref>

On 7 January 2026, Thomas signed a two-and-a-half-year contract extension with Bristol City until the summer of 2028, and subsequently joined [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] on loan until the end of the 2025–26 season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bcfc.co.uk/news/thomas-signs-new-deal/ |title=New deal and loan for Thomas |website=Bristol City F.C. |date=7 January 2026 |access-date=7 January 2026 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c8rmkleg466o|title=Olly Thomas: Bristol City striker signs new deal and agrees Dunfermline loan|date=8 January 2026|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> On 7 March, Thomas scored twice as Dunfermline defeated defending champions [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] 3-0 to reach the semi-finals of the [[2025–26 Scottish Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|website=Daily Record|url= https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/apoplectic-aberdeen-fans-rip-meek-36833300.amp|accessdate=8 March 2026|date=7 March 2026|title= Apoplectic Aberdeen fans let rip at meek Scottish Cup surrender as Dunfermline blow away crisis club - 5 talking points|first=Fraser|last=Wilson}}</ref> That September, he signed for Dunfermline on a permanent basis.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.bcfc.co.uk/academy-news/thomas-joins-dunfermline/|website=bcfc.co.uk|accessdate=4 September 2026|title= Thomas joins Dunfermline
|date=4 September 2026}}</ref>
