'''Detlef Esapa Osong''' (born 21 September 2004) is an English professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for [[Scottish Championship]] club, [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]].

==Club career==
Osong joined [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] as a youth in 2017 from grassroots football in [[Leicestershire]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nottinghamforest.co.uk/news/2022/january/06/esapa-osong-signs-professional-contract/|title=Esapa Osong signs professional contract|first=Nottingham Forest Football|last=Club|website=Nottingham Forest Football Club|date=6 January 2022 }}</ref> and worked his way up their youth sides. He had a prolific start with the club's U18s in the 2022–23 season, scoring 12 goals in 20 appearances.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.foresttilidie.com/news/nottingham-forest-steve-cooper-detlef-esapa-osong-championship-latest-news-opinion-update-youth-team-nffc|title=Nottingham Forest: Cooper can save millions by unleashing Esapa Osong|website=www.foresttilidie.com}}</ref> He signed his first professional contract with the club on 6 January 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nottinghampost.com/sport/football/transfer-news/nottingham-forest-transfers-esapa-osong-6451404|title=Esapa Osong tipped for 'bright future' after signing Reds contract|first=Sarah|last=Clapson|date=6 January 2022|website=NottinghamshireLive}}</ref>

On 1 February 2023, Osong made his professional and senior debut with Nottingham Forest in a 2–0 [[EFL Cup]] loss to [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/live-blogs/man-utd-nottingham/iNnYIFZrmcQk/|title=Manchester United vs Nottingham Forest live updates|first=The|last=Athletic|website=The Athletic|date=February 2023 }}</ref>

On 18 July 2024, Osong was loaned to [[EFL League One]] side [[Rotherham United F.C.|Rotherham United]] for the [[2024–25 Rotherham United F.C. season|2024–25 season]].<ref>https://www.themillers.co.uk/news/2024/july/18/signing---forest-forward-osong-arrives-on-loan-/</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nottinghamforest.co.uk/news/2024/july/18/osong-makes-rotherham-loan-move/|title=Osong makes Rotherham loan move|first=Nottingham Forest Football|last=Club|date=18 July 2024|website=Nottingham Forest Football Club}}</ref> He was recalled on 2 January 2025, having played 10 times in all competitions.<ref>{{cite web |title=Osong returns to Nottingham Forest|url=https://www.themillers.co.uk/news/2025/january/02/read---osong-returns-to-nottingham-forest/|publisher=Rotherham United F.C. |date=2 January 2025}}</ref> Later that month he signed on loan for [[Cambridge United F.C.|Cambridge United]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c4g352nynydo|title=Esapa Osong: Nottingham Forest forward joins Cambridge United on loan|date=27 January 2025|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

On 15 August 2025, Osong moved on loan to [[Scottish Premier League]] side [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] for their 2025–26 season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nottinghamforest.co.uk/news/2025/august/15/osong-joins-motherwell-on-loan/|title=Osong joins Motherwell on loan|first=Nottingham Forest Football|last=Club|date=15 August 2025|website=Nottingham Forest Football Club}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2025/08/15/esapa-osong-arrives-on-loan/|title=Esapa Osong arrives on loan|first1=Motherwell Football|last1=Club|first2=Scott|last2=Gibson|date=15 August 2025}}</ref> On 19 January 2026, Motherwell announced that Osong had returned to [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] after his loan deal was ended early.<ref>{{cite web |title=Esapa Osong returns to Nottingham Forest |url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2026/01/19/esapa-osong-returns-to-nottingham-forest/ |website=motherwellfc.co.uk |publisher=Motherwell F.C. |access-date=20 January 2026 |date=19 January 2026}}</ref>

On 2 February 2026, Osong joined [[EFL League Two|League Two]] club [[Fleetwood Town F.C.|Fleetwood Town]] on loan for the remainder of the [[2025–26 Fleetwood Town F.C. season|2025–26 season]].<ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.fleetwoodtownfc.com/esapa-osong-joins-town-on-short-term-loan/|title=Esapa Osong joins Town on short-term loan|website=www.fleetwoodtownfc.com|date=2 February 2026|accessdate=2 February 2026}}</ref>

On 17 September 2026, Osong joined [[Scottish Championship]] side, [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-09-17 |title=Caley Thistle sign former Nottingham Forest striker who debuted against Manchester United |url=https://www.inverness-courier.co.uk/sport/caley-thistle-sign-striker-former-nottingham-forest-striker-445233/ |access-date=2026-09-18 |website=Inverness Courier |language=en}}</ref>

'''Alfie Bavidge''' (born 11 April 2006) is a Scottish [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Striker (association football)|striker]] for {{Scottish football updater|InvernCT}} side [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]], on loan from {{Scottish football updater|Aberdeen}} side [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]].

==Career==
Bavidge started his career with [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]].<ref name="who22">{{Cite web|archive-url=https://archive.today/20230221161946/https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/aberdeen-fc/4491141/alfie-bavidge-the-16-year-old-aberdeen-striker-great-potential/|archive-date=21 February 2023|url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/aberdeen-fc/4491141/alfie-bavidge-the-16-year-old-aberdeen-striker-great-potential/|title=Who is Alfie Bavidge? The 16-year-old Aberdeen striker with great potential|author=Danny Law|date=4 July 2022|publisher=pressandjournal.co.uk (Archived)}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aberdeenlive.news/sport/football/aberdeen-academy-sensation-alfie-bavidge-7895869|title=Aberdeen academy sensation Alfie Bavidge talks about influence of his dad and season targets amid astonishing campaign|publisher=aberdeenlive.news|date=5 December 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/ckr7y3nn00eo|title=Meet the next Miovski...|publisher=bbc.com|date=1 December 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/aberdeen-fc/5046976/aberdeen-teen-goal-sensation-alfie-bavidge-has-earned-his-chance-in-atlanta-says-boss-jim-goodwin/|title=Aberdeen teen goal sensation Alfie Bavidge has earned his chance in Atlanta, says boss Jim Goodwin|publisher=pressandjournal.co.uk|date=16 November 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aberdeenlive.news/sport/football/alfie-bavidge-next-aberdeen-academy-7685975|title=Alfie Bavidge - The next Aberdeen academy star in waiting|publisher=aberdeenlive.news|date=10 October 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/aberdeen-fc/5106358/alfie-bavidge-aberdeen-goals/|title=Alfie Bavidge strives for more after Aberdeen youngster hits goal trail at youth level|publisher=pressandjournal.co.uk|date=30 November 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.afc.co.uk/2022/11/30/young-dons-alfie-bavidge-feature/|title=Aberdeen FC - Young Dons | Alfie Bavidge feature|website=Aberdeen FC|date=30 November 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/aberdeen-v-hearts-reaction-goodwins-bavidge-reward-hurt-of-midlothian-hats-off-to-hearts-fans-albert-kidd-at-65-3882569|title=Aberdeen v Hearts Reaction: Goodwin's Bavidge reward; "Hurt of Midlothian"; hats off to Hearts fans; Albert Kidd at 65|publisher=scotsman.com|date=17 October 2022}}</ref> After impressing in the academy, scoring plenty of goals along the way, he made his League debut on 4 February 2023, coming on as a second-half substitute in a 3–1 win against [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/64436052|title = Hosts end run of five defeats with convincing win|website=BBC Sport|date=4 February 2023}}</ref><ref>[https://uk.soccerway.com/players/alfie-bavidge/757075/ A. Bavidge], Soccerway</ref>

In September 2023, Bavidge joined [[Scottish League One]] club [[Kelty Hearts F.C.|Kelty Hearts]] on loan until January 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.afc.co.uk/2023/09/23/alfie-heads-out-on-loan/|title=Alfie heads out on loan|website=www.afc.co.uk|date=23 September 2023|accessdate=25 September 2023}}</ref>

On 3 February 2024, Bavidge scored his first career hat-trick in a 3-0 away win over [[Edinburgh City F.C.|Edinburgh City]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=5 February 2024 |title=Alfie Bavidge hat-trick earns Kelty a win at Edinburgh City |url=https://www.dunfermlinepress.com/sport/24098110.alfie-bavidge-hat-trick-earns-kelty-win-edinburgh-city/ |access-date= |website=www.dunfermlinepress.com}}</ref>  He followed this up just 13 days later with another hat-trick, this time for [[Scotland national under-19 football team|Scotland U-19]] in a 4-0 win against Latvia.<ref>{{Cite web |date=19 February 2024 |title=Kelty Hearts' Alfie Bavidge nets Scotland U-19 treble in Latvia win |url=https://www.dunfermlinepress.com/sport/24127879.kelty-hearts-alfie-bavidge-nets-scotland-u-19-treble-latvia-win/ |access-date= |website=www.dunfermlinepress.com}}</ref>

In August 2024, Bavidge joined [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]] on loan for the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ayrunitedfc.co.uk/alfie-bavidge-joins-the-honest-men|title=Alfie Bavidge Joins the Honest Men|website=Ayr United FC|date=31 August 2024|accessdate=7 September 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.afc.co.uk/2024/08/31/young-striker-heads-out-on-loan/|title=Young striker heads out on loan|website=Aberdeen FC|date=30 August 2024|accessdate=7 September 2024}}</ref>

In January 2025, Bavidge was recalled from his loan at Ayr United and immediately joined [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] (for whom his father had also played), scoring on his debut.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.afc.co.uk/2025/01/04/young-dons-heading-to-inverness-ct/ |title=Young Dons head to Inverness CT|website=Aberdeen FC|date=4 January 2025|accessdate=5 January 2025}}</ref>

On 1 August 2025, Bavidge returned to Inverness on a season long loan.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.afc.co.uk/2025/08/01/alfie-bavidge-heads-north-on-loan/|title=Alfie Bavidge Heads North On Loan/ |website=Aberdeen FC |date=1 August 2025 | accessdate=7 August 2025}}</ref>

On 26 June 2026, Bavidge returned to Inverness for the third consecutive season, on a season long loan.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-06-26 |title=Top scorer returns to Caley Thistle for another loan spell |url=https://www.inverness-courier.co.uk/sport/top-scorer-returns-to-caley-jags-for-another-loan-spell-438635/ |access-date=2026-06-27 |website=Inverness Courier |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Alfie is the son of former professional footballer [[Martin Bavidge]]; his grandfather Mitch Bavidge also played at a high level, mainly in the [[Highland Football League]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Britton |first=Ruaraidh |date=5 December 2022 |title=Aberdeen youngster Alfie Bavidge on influence of family as scoring run continues |url=https://www.aberdeenlive.news/sport/football/aberdeen-academy-sensation-alfie-bavidge-7895869 |access-date=18 April 2023 |website=AberdeenLive}}</ref> His brother, Sam, is also a footballer, currently playing at [[Banks o' Dee F.C.|Banks o' Dee]] in the Highland League.

'''Ben Robert Gordon Stanway''' (born 20 September 2004) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|PartickT}} club [[Partick Thistle]].

==Career==

===Partick Thistle===
Aged 17, Stanway graduated as a modern apprentice from the Thistle Weir Youth academy and joined the clubs first team in January 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ben Stanway graduates from the Thistle Weir Youth Academy |url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/ben-stanway-graduates-from-the-thistle-weir-youth-academy/ |access-date=5 January 2023 |website=Partick Thistle FC |language=en}}</ref> Stanway made his professional debut, coming on a substitute in a 2–0 away win over Stranraer in the Scottish Challenge Cup.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.skysports.com/football/stranraer-vs-partick-thistle/teams/453232 | title=Scottish Challenge Cup (Sky Sports) }}</ref>

After making a handful of appearances for Thistle's first team, Stanway joined [[Scottish League One]] side [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]] on loan in January 2023, until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ben Stanway joins Airdrieonians on loan |url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/ben-stanway-joins-airdrieonians-on-loan/ |access-date=5 January 2023|website=Partick Thistle FC |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Thomson |first=Paul |date=2023-01-01 |title=Partick Thistle midfielder joins Airdrie on loan |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/partick-thistle-midfielder-joins-airdrie-28852622 |access-date=2025-01-30 |website=Daily Record |language=en}}</ref> Stanway made his debut for Airdrie, in which he won a penalty, in a 3–0 away win against Peterhead.<ref>{{cite web | title=Peterhead v Airdrieonians | website=BBC Sport | date=2023-01-07 | url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64132774 | access-date=2023-07-29}}</ref> Stanway scored his first professional goal, opening the scoring for Airdrie in a 1–1 draw away to league leaders Dunfermline.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/64607442 | title=Dunfermline Athletic v Airdrieonians | work=BBC Sport }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/dunfermline-1-airdrie-1-sub-29249643.amp | title=Dunfermline 1 Airdrie 1: Sub keeper Hutton saves 10-man Diamonds late on | date=18 February 2023 }}</ref>

After returning to Thistle following his loan spell, Stanway made his first start for Thistle, playing the full 90 minutes in a cup tie away to Peterhead.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/66148747 | title=Peterhead v Partick Thistle | work=BBC Sport }}</ref> Stanway scored his first goal for Partick Thistle, with a header in a challenge cup game against Queen of the South.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2023-09-09 |title=Partick Thistle v Queen of the South |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/66764041 |access-date=2025-01-30 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Wilson |first=Fraser |date=2023-09-15 |title=Ben Stanway says first goal and new contract made it a great week at Partick |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/ben-stanway-reveals-partick-thistle-30943360 |access-date=2025-01-30 |website=Daily Record |language=en}}</ref> Following breaking into the Partick Thistle first team at the beginning of the 2023–24 season,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-08-15 |title=Kris Doolan outlines loan intentions for Partick Thistle youngsters |url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/23721508.doolan-outlines-intentions-partick-thistle-youngsters/ |access-date=2025-01-30 |website=The Herald |language=en}}</ref> Stanway signed a new three year professional contract with Partick Thistle until the end of the 2025–26 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ben Stanway signs contract extension with the Jags |url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/ben-stanway-signs-contract-extension-with-the-jags/ |access-date=2025-01-30 |website=Partick Thistle FC |language=en}}</ref>

Stanway scored his first league goal for Thistle away to champions Dundee United, on the final day of the league season in May 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dundee United beat Partick Thistle and celebrate Scottish Championship title |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cz96gm6rplgt |access-date=2025-01-30 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

Stanway scored his first goal of the 2024–25 season, scoring the winner with a curling strike from 20 yards, in a 2–1 away win at Hamilton Academical.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brian Graham and Ben Stanway help Partick Thistle come rally to beat Hamilton Accies |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cn8gwpegxn2t |access-date=2025-01-30 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

Stanway scored his first goal of the 2025–26 season in a 3–1 away victory against Ross County, in the Scottish League Cup group stages.<ref>https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c5y7nx2rrx1t</ref>

Stanway signed a new one year extension with Thistle on 30th July 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ben Stanway signs new deal at Firhill |url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/ben-stanway-signs-new-deal-at-firhill/ |access-date=2026-07-30 |website=Partick Thistle FC |language=en}}</ref>

'''Logan Ross''' (born 24 April 2004) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] for [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness CT]].

==Personal life==
Ross has alopecia.

==Career==
===Ross County===
Logan Ross signed his first professional contract with [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] on 6 October 2020 aged 16 after coming up the ranks with the club youth, on 8 March 2022 Himself, [[Matthew Wright (Scottish footballer)|Matthew Wright]] and [[Adam Mackinnon]] signed an extension until the end of 2023/24.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New Contracts for Academy Graduates |url=https://www.rosscountyfootballclub.co.uk/news-items/new-contracts-for-academy-graduates |access-date=2023-12-29 |website=RCFC |language=en}}</ref>

===Loans===

On 26 November 2020 Ross joined [[Highland Football League]] club [[Lossiemouth F.C.|Lossiemouth]] on a short loan until January.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-11-26 |title=Ross County keeper arrives on loan at Lossiemouth |url=https://www.northern-scot.co.uk/sport/ross-county-keeper-arrives-on-loan-at-lossiemouth-219535/ |access-date=2023-12-20 |website=Northern Scot |language=en}}</ref>

On 24 July 2021 Logan Ross and [[Lossiemouth F.C.|Lossiemouth]] extended the loan deal before another extension until the end of the 22/23 season was cut short after being recalled in January 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Academy Graduates head out on loan |url=https://www.rosscountyfootballclub.co.uk/news-items/academy-graduates-head-out-on-loan |access-date=2023-12-29 |website=RCFC |language=en}}</ref>

On 6 January 2023 Ross joined [[Highland Football League]] club [[Brora Rangers]] on a loan deal until the end of the season after being recalled mid-season from a loan in Lossiemouth.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Academy Graduates head out on loan |url=https://www.rosscountyfootballclub.co.uk/news-items/academy-graduates-head-out-on-loan |access-date=2023-12-29 |website=RCFC |language=en}}</ref>

On 14 August 2023 Ross headed back to [[Highland Football League]] club [[Brora Rangers]] on loan deal until the end of the 23/24 campaign,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Logan Ross joins Brora Rangers on loan |url=https://www.rosscountyfootballclub.co.uk/news-items/logan-ross-joins-brora-rangers-on-loan |access-date=2023-12-29 |website=RCFC |language=en}}</ref> Ross played a crucial role in the [[Highland League Cup]] reaching the final,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-12-02 |title=Ross County loanee desperate to take trophy chance |url=https://www.inverness-courier.co.uk/sport/ross-county-loanee-desperate-to-take-trophy-chance-334494/ |access-date=2024-06-08 |website=Inverness Courier |language=en}}</ref> beating Fraserburgh 5-4 (on [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|pens]].).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Law |first=Callum |date=2024-03-30 |title=Highland League results: Brora Rangers beat Fraserburgh on penalties to lift Highland League Cup |url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/highland-league/6416425/highland-league-results-brora-win-league-cup-on-penalties/ |access-date=2024-06-08 |website=Press and Journal |language=en-GB}}</ref>

On 2 February 2024 Ross returned to [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] on an emergency basis to cover for [[Ross Laidlaw]] who picked up a calf injury,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ross returns to club on emergency basis |url=https://www.rosscountyfootballclub.co.uk/news-items/ross-returns-to-club-on-emergency-basis |access-date=2024-02-06 |website=RCFC |language=en}}</ref> He was still eligible to switch between [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] and [[Brora Rangers F.C.|Brora Rangers]] when needed.

Between 27 July 2024 and 12 December 2024, Ross joined [[Highland Football League|Highland League]] clubs, [[Huntly F.C.|Huntly]], [[Forres Mechanics F.C.|Forres Mechanics]], [[Nairn County F.C.|Nairn County]] and [[Clachnacuddin F.C.|Clachnacuddin]] along with [[Scottish League Two|League Two]] club, [[Elgin City F.C.|Elgin City]] on emergency agreement.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Huntly Football Club, TRANSFER NEWS 2024/25: Huntly Loan in Ross County Keeper |url=https://huntlyfc.co.uk/news/transfer-new-2024-25--huntly-loan-in-ross-county-keeper?fbclid=IwZXh0bgNhZW0CMTEAAR0Kp2hWFBye85nRzztjgQk5Sfs1yHD6NWUGh9s0owmm-kQvN86xz2VQfW0_aem_vAW415QTti3j1UBuUHNnNA |access-date=2024-08-04 |website=huntlyfc.co.uk |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-09-05 |title=Elgin City bring in emergency loan goalkeeper for big cup clash |url=https://www.northern-scot.co.uk/sport/elgin-city-bring-in-emergency-loan-goalkeeper-for-big-cup-cl-360439/ |access-date=2024-12-23 |website=Northern Scot |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Logan Ross – Forres Mechanics – The Mighty Cans |url=https://www.forresmechanics.net/player/logan-ross/ |access-date=2024-12-23 |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-12-12 |title=Ross County goalkeeper heads out on emergency loan deal to Highland League club |url=https://www.ross-shirejournal.co.uk/sport/clachnacuddin-sign-goalkeeper-on-emergency-loan-deal-from-ro-368823/ |access-date=2024-12-23 |website=RossShire Journal |language=en}}</ref>

On 14 February 2025 Ross joined [[Clachnacuddin F.C.|Clachnacuddin]] for a second time in the season on a loan until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-02-14 |title=Ross County goalkeeper joins Clach in fresh loan move |url=https://www.inverness-courier.co.uk/sport/ross-county-goalkeeper-joins-clach-in-fresh-loan-move-374503/ |access-date=2025-02-14 |website=Inverness Courier |language=en}}</ref>

===Inverness CT===
On 16 June 2025 Ross signed for [[Scottish League One]] club [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness CT]] on a one year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-06-16 |title=Caley Thistle sign new goalkeeper |url=https://www.inverness-courier.co.uk/sport/caley-thistle-sign-new-goalkeeper-384861/ |access-date=2025-06-16 |website=Inverness Courier |language=en}}</ref>

'''Tsoanelo Letsosa''', also stylized as '''Ts'oanelo Lets'osa''' (born 6 June 2004) is a professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]]. Born in Lesotho, he represented Scotland at youth international level.

==Club career==

===Celtic===
Lets'osa began his career in the youth teams of [[Glasgow]]-based club [[Pollok F.C.|Pollok]],<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Davidson |first=Euan |date=22 February 2022 |title=Watch: Letsosa's screamer that secured dramatic Celtic B comeback |url=https://www.67hailhail.com/celtic-youth/watch-letsosas-screamer-that-secured-dramatic-celtic-b-comeback/ |access-date=8 July 2023 |website=67 Hail Hail}}</ref> before aged 12 joining [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]]'s youth academy in 2017.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":8">{{Cite web |last=McNicol |first=Ben |date=29 August 2023 |title=I'm a former Celtic B team standout and this is what it's really like taking the leap to new league |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-transfer-news/im-former-celtic-b-team-30809188 |access-date=25 March 2024 |publisher=[[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]]}}</ref>

After signing his first professional contract with the ''Hoops'' in July 2020,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2 July 2020 |title=Future's bright as young Celts take next step on football journey |url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/18283/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230708144909/https://www.celticfc.com/news/18283/ |archive-date=8 July 2023 |access-date=8 July 2023 |publisher=[[Celtic FC]] }}</ref> Lets'osa went on to feature for the club's [[Celtic F.C. B Team and Academy|B team]] in the [[Lowland Football League|Lowland League]],<ref name=":8" /><ref name=":3">{{Cite web |last=Claes |first=Sven |date=25 June 2023 |title=Lommel SK plukt Schotse middenvelder weg uit vijfde klasse |url=https://www.hbvl.be/cnt/dmf20230625_96667244 |access-date=8 July 2023 |website=[[Het Belang van Limburg]] |language=nl-BE}}</ref> and established himself as a regular member of the squad throughout the [[2022–23 Lowland Football League|2022–23 season]],<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Lancaster |first=Will |date=24 May 2023 |title=Tsoanelo Letsosa 'set' for Celtic exit as Hoops youngster seeks pastures new in England |url=https://www.glasgowlive.co.uk/sport/tsoanelo-letsosa-set-celtic-exit-26985328 |access-date=25 March 2024 |website=GlasgowLive}}</ref><ref name=":22">{{Cite web |last=Hendry |first=Mark |date=24 June 2023 |title=Celtic midfielder close to sealing transfer after knocking back new deal |url=https://www.footballscotland.co.uk/spfl/scottish-premiership/tsoanelo-letsosa-poised-celtic-transfer-27193166 |access-date=8 July 2023 |website=Football Scotland}}</ref> while also playing in the [[2022–23 UEFA Youth League|UEFA Youth League]]<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" /> and contributing to the victory of the [[Glasgow Cup]].<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |last=Banks |first=Ben |date=10 May 2023 |title=Celtic beat Rangers for Glasgow Cup - RECAP: Relive thrilling night at Ibrox |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/rangers-vs-celtic-live-score-29947435 |access-date=8 July 2023 |publisher=[[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]]}}</ref><ref name=":5">{{Cite web |date=10 May 2023 |title=Glasgow Cup belongs to Celtic after penalty shoot-out drama at Ibrox |url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2023/may/10/glasgow-cup-belongs-to-celtic-after-penalty-shoot-out-drama-at-ibrox/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230708143833/https://www.celticfc.com/news/2023/may/10/glasgow-cup-belongs-to-celtic-after-penalty-shoot-out-drama-at-ibrox/ |archive-date=8 July 2023 |access-date=8 July 2023 |publisher=[[Celtic FC]] }}</ref> During the same campaign, he also started training with the first team under manager [[Ange Postecoglou]].<ref name=":8" />

===Lommel===
After leaving Celtic in the summer of 2023, having turned down an offer for a new deal,<ref name=":8" /><ref name=":22" /> on 7 July of the same year Lets'osa officially joined Belgian side [[Lommel S.K.|Lommel]] on a [[Free transfer (association football)|free transfer]], signing a five-year contract with the club.<ref>{{Cite web |date=7 July 2023 |title=Welkom Ts'onaelo Lets'osa |url=https://www.lommelsk.be/news.php?newsId=1575 |access-date=8 July 2023 |publisher=[[Lommel SK]] |language=nl-BE}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=8 July 2023 |title=Transfers CPL: nieuwkomers bij Lommel, Lierse en Francs Borains |url=https://www.proximus.be/pickx/nl/2351435/transfers-cpl-nieuwkomers-bij-lommel-lierse-en-francs-borains |access-date=8 July 2023 |website=Proximus Pickx |publisher=[[Proximus]] |language=nl-BE}}</ref> 

After two seasons and only seven appearances for Lommel's first team, Lets'osa's contract was terminated by mutual agreement in June 2025.<ref>{{cite web |title=Lommel SK terminates contracts of four players |url=https://www.lommelsk.be/en/nieuws.php?nieuwsId=2346 |website=Lommel SK |access-date=6 October 2026 |date=4 July 2025}}</ref>

===Partick Thistle=== 
In July 2025 Lets'osa signed for [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Partick Thistle F.C.| Partick Thistle]], returning to Glasgow on a two year deal.<ref> 
{{Cite web |title=Ts'oanelo Lets'osa joins Partick Thistle |url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/tsoanelo-letsosa-joins-partick-thistle/ |access-date=2025-07-15 |website=Partick Thistle FC |language=en}}</ref> 

Lets’osa made his Thistle debut, and also scored his first Thistle goal, in a 2–0 home win over Queen of the South in the [[Scottish League Cup]] group stages.<ref>{{cite web | title=Partick Thistle vs Queen of the South: Premier Sports Cup score updates, BBC Sport | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c98w0wg5301t }}</ref> Lets’osa scored his first league goal for Thistle in October 2025, in a 2–1 home win over Ayr United.<ref>{{cite web | title=Partick Thistle vs Ayr United: Championship stats & head-to-head | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c77z4zr83y3t }}</ref>

==International career==
Lets'osa represented Scotland at youth international level, having featured for the [[Scotland national under-16 football team|under-16 national team]] at the [[Victory Shield|2019 Victory Shield]], where they finished as joint winners, together with [[Wales national under-17 football team|Wales]].<ref name=":6">{{Cite news |date=1 November 2019 |title=Wales and Scotland share Victory Shield |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/50267477 |access-date=8 July 2023 |work=[[BBC Sport]]}}</ref><ref name=":7">{{Cite web |date=1 November 2019 |title=Scotland Under-16s crowned joint winners of 2019 Victory Shield |url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/news/scotland-under-16s-crowned-joint-winners-of-2019-victory-shield/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210422002118/https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/news/scotland-under-16s-crowned-joint-winners-of-2019-victory-shield/ |archive-date=22 April 2021 |access-date=8 July 2023 |publisher=[[Scottish FA]] |url-status=live }}</ref> In August 2025, he was called up to the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland U21]] squad.<ref>{{cite web |title=Lets’osa and McPherson set for Scotland Under 21 duty |url=https://www.ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/letsosa-and-mcpherson-set-for-scotland-under-21-duty/ |website=Partick Thistle FC |access-date=6 October 2026 |language=en}}</ref>
== Personal life ==
Lets'osa was born in [[Lesotho]], before moving to Scotland with his family.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Tsoanelo Letsosa |url=https://www.celticfc.com/players/celtic-b/Tsoanelo-Letsosa/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221217195249/https://www.celticfc.com/players/celtic-b/Tsoanelo-Letsosa/ |archive-date=17 December 2022 |access-date=8 July 2023 |website= |publisher=[[Celtic FC]]}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Lancaster |first=Will |date=7 February 2023 |title=5 Celtic starlets on Ange's radar as Hoops youth setup begins to bear fruit again |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/5-celtic-starlets-anges-radar-29146404 |access-date=25 March 2024 |publisher=[[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]]}}</ref> He is a Christian.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Richardson|first1=Aaron |title=Thistle’s crown of thorns: the holiest team in Scottish football |url=https://www.glasgowbell.co.uk/partick-thistle-christian-players-glasgow-football/ |access-date=6 October 2026 |work=The Glasgow Bell |date=3 October 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

'''Liam Sole''' (born 21 December 1999) is an English professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays for {{Scottish football updater|Livingst}} club Inverness Caledonian Thistle.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Liam Sole {{!}} Football Stats {{!}} Livingston {{!}} Age 26 {{!}} Soccer Base |url=https://www.soccerbase.com/players/player.sd?player_id=108588 |access-date=2026-06-22 |website=www.soccerbase.com}}</ref>

==Club career==
Sole began his career in the youth academy of [[Milton Keynes Dons F.C.|MK Dons]], signing his first professional contract in May 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mkdons.com/news/2018/may/sole-signs-first-pro-deal/|title=Sole signs first pro deal|date=25 May 2018|publisher=MK Dons FC}}</ref>

He spent a short spell on loan at [[St Albans City F.C.|St Albans City]] in 2019 before leaving [[Milton Keynes Dons F.C.|MK Dons]] permanently.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mkdons.com/news/2019/february/loan-watch-liam-sole-helps-st-albans-reach-cup-final/|title=Loan Watch: Liam Sole helps St Albans reach Cup Final|date=7 February 2019|publisher=MK Dons FC}}</ref>

In October 2019, Sole signed a short-term contract with [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nottinghampost.com/sport/football/transfer-news/nottingham-forest-sign-young-midfielder-3474840|title=Nottingham Forest sign young midfielder with 'unbelievable feet'|date=28 October 2019|publisher=Nottingham Post}}</ref> However he left the club in 2020 without making a single first team appearance.

The midfielder rejoined [[St Albans City F.C.|St Albans City]] permanently in 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.stalbanscityfc.com/sole-stays/|title=Sole stays|date=22 June 2022|publisher=St Albans City FC}}</ref> He joined [[Kings Langley F.C.|Kings Langley]] on loan in February 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.stalbanscityfc.com/sole-joins-kings-langley-on-loan/|title=Sole joins Kings Langley on loan|date=3 February 2023|publisher=St Albans City FC}}</ref>

Sole signed for [[Maidstone United F.C.|Maidstone United]] ahead of the 2023–2024 season, and was part of the side that knocked then [[English Championship]] side [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]] out of the [[FA Cup]] in January 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/68110763|title=Non-league Maidstone stun Ipswich in FA Cup|date=27 January 2024|publisher=BBC}}</ref>

In May 2024, Sole signed a pre-contract with Scottish side [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.kentonline.co.uk/maidstone/sport/stones-winger-makes-scotland-move-306210/|title=Stones winger makes Scotland move|date=4 May 2024|publisher=Kent Online}}</ref>

In July 2025, Sole went on loan to [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] in Scottish League One.

In May 2026, Sole left Livingston following the expiration of his contract.<ref>{{cite web |title=Squad Update – Retained & Released List|url=https://livingstonfc.co.uk/squad-update-retained-released-list/|website=livingstonfc.co.uk|date=19 May 2026}}</ref> Returning to Inverness on a one year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-06-09 |title=ICT confirm return of fan favourite on permanent basis |url=https://www.inverness-courier.co.uk/sport/ict-confirm-return-of-fan-favourite-on-permanent-basis-437174/ |access-date=2026-06-22 |website=Inverness Courier |language=en}}</ref>

'''Remi Savage''' (born 26 October 2001) is an English professional [[Association football|football]]er who plays as a [[centre-back]] for {{Scottish football updater|InvernCT}} club [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]].<ref>{{soccerbase|125531}}</ref>

== Career ==
Born in [[Liverpool]], Savage played for [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] at youth level;<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-06-18 |title=Meet the Academy: Remi Savage |url=https://legacy.liverpoolfc.com/news/academy/398730-meet-the-academy-remi-savage |access-date=2024-05-12 |website=Liverpool FC}}</ref> he was part of the team that won the [[2018–19 FA Youth Cup|FA Youth Cup]] in 2019 and made his debut for the U21s in a 5–2 away loss to [[Accrington Stanley F.C.|Accrington Stanley]] in the [[EFL Trophy]] later that year,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Accrington Stanley 5-2 Liverpool U21 (Oct 29, 2019) Final Score |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/match/_/gameId/554110/liverpool-u21-accrington-stanley |access-date=2024-05-12 |website=ESPN }}</ref> but failed to break into the senior squad before signing for [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] in July 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ryder |first=Lee |date=2021-06-17 |title=Newcastle United on brink of signing Liverpool teenager on professional deal |url=https://www.chroniclelive.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/remi-savage-liverpool-newcastle-united-20844901 |access-date=2024-05-12 |website=Chronicle Live }}</ref> Savage made his debut for ''The Toon'' in a 3–0 away loss to [[Sheffield Wednesday F.C.|Sheffield Wednesday]] in the [[EFL Cup]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Report: Wednesday 3-0 Newcastle U21s |url=https://www.swfc.co.uk/news/2021/august/report-wednesday-3-0-newcastle-u21s/ |access-date=2024-05-12 |website=www.swfc.co.uk }}</ref> but did not make any appearances in the [[Premier League]].

On 25 January 2024, Savage moved to [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] on a permanent deal,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-01-25 |title=Newcastle United confirm permanent departure of defender on busy day of dealings |url=https://www.thenorthernecho.co.uk/sport/24075855.newcastle-united-confirm-exit-remi-savage-inverness/ |access-date=2024-05-12 |website=The Northern Echo }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-01-25 |title=Three Academy players make moves from Newcastle |url=https://www.newcastleunited.com/news/latest-news/three-academy-players-make-moves-from-newcastle/ |access-date=2024-05-12 |website=Newcastle United Football Club}}</ref> making his debut two days later in a 3–2 away win over league leaders [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]]<ref>{{Cite news |title=Nine-minute Samuel hat-trick dents Raith's title bid |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68039855 |access-date=2024-05-12 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref> before netting his first senior goal in a 3–3 home draw with [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Partick Thistle battle back to draw in Inverness |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68144690 |access-date=2024-05-12 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref>

'''Robbie Fraser'''<ref name="Inverness">{{Soccerway|id=robbie-fraser/637253|accessdate=}}</ref> (born 2 April 2003) is a Scottish professional footballer who plays as a [[defender (association football)|defender]] for {{Scottish football updater|DunfermA}} club [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]]. He has previously played for [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] and [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].

== Career ==
Fraser played through the [[Rangers F.C. B Team and Academy|Rangers Academy]], having joined in 2010 as a seven-year-old and was club captain of the B-Team.<ref name="Fraser debut"/> He signed a one-year contract with the club on 9 May 2023.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://twitter.com/RFC_Youth/status/1655965855908343808|title=RangersFC are today delighted to announce that Robbie Fraser has signed a contract extension until 2024.|work=Rangers FC|publisher=Twitter, Inc|date=9 May 2023}}</ref> Fraser made his debut for Rangers during a [[Scottish Premiership]] match in 5-2 home win at [[Ibrox Stadium]] against [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] on 14 May 2024.<ref name="Fraser debut">{{ cite news | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/crgyg2dk9z8o | title=Debut 'a huge moment for me' - Fraser | work=BBC Sport | date=15 May 2024 }}</ref> On 15 May 2024, Fraser has signed further contract extension until 2026.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.rangers.co.uk/Article/robbie-fraser-signs-contract-extension-to-2026/1v805pq5qf1tW2frwdzRZs|title=Robbie Fraser signs contract extension to 2026|work=Rangers FC|publisher=rangers.co.uk|date=31 May 2024}}</ref> He made his [[UEFA Europa League]] debut in a game on 12 December 2024 against [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] coming on for [[Ridvan Yilmaz]] on 80th minute in a 1-1 draw. On 3 January 2025, Fraser joined [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] on loan for the remainder of the season.<ref>https://www.rangers.co.uk/article/robbie-fraser-joins-livingston-on-loan/5VEhy0N6LSglvkiOPgqVdo</ref>

Fraser moved to [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] in August 2025 for an undisclosed transfer fee.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cx295pnvggzo |title=Defender Fraser moves to Dunfermline |website=BBC Sport |date=16 August 2025 |accessdate=16 August 2025}}</ref>

'''Keith Bray''' (born 1 April 2006) is a Scottish professional footballer who plays as a [[central midfielder]] for [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] in [[Scottish Championship]].

== Career ==
Bray started his career under a dual registration with [[Scottish Championship]] side, [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]], and [[Lewis & Harris Football Association|Lewis and Harris League]] side, [[Stornoway Athletic]], before signing professionally for Inverness in July 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |date=11 July 2022 |title=Trio sign first pro deals |url=https://www.inverness-courier.co.uk/sport/trio-sign-first-pro-deals-281123/ |access-date=4 August 2024 |website=Inverness Courier |language=en}}</ref> On 10 December 2022, Bray made his debut for Inverness in a 2–0 away defeat to [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]] in the [[Scottish Challenge Cup]], playing all 90 minutes in an injury ravaged side.<ref>{{Cite news |date=10 December 2022 |title=Hamilton Academical v Inverness Caledonian Thistle |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/63879706 |access-date=4 August 2024 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> On 20 July 2024, Bray scored his first Inverness goal in a 3–0 win over Bonnyrigg Rose in the League Cup.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Inverness CT vs Bonnyrigg Rose: League Cup |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cjl69l1x463t |access-date=17 November 2024 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> Bray went on to make his first league appearance on 5 August 2023, in a 2–1 home loss to [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]], in which he was booked.<ref>{{Cite news |date=5 August 2023 |title=Inverness Caledonian Thistle 1-2 Queen's Park: Visitors secure opening win |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66194530 |access-date=4 August 2024 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

In January 2024, Bray was sent on loan to [[Scottish League Two|League Two]] side, [[Elgin City F.C.|Elgin City]], for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=23 January 2024 |title=Elgin City sign Inverness Caley Thistle midfielder on loan |url=https://www.northern-scot.co.uk/sport/elgin-city-sign-inverness-caley-thistle-midfielder-on-loan-339998/ |access-date=4 August 2024 |website=Northern Scot |language=en}}</ref>

In July 2024, Bray became a first team regular at Inverness, starting in all 4 [[2024–25 Scottish League Cup group stage#Group D|League Cup]] games and scoring against [[Bonnyrigg Rose F.C.|Bonnyrigg Rose]] in a 3–0 home win,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Inverness CT vs Bonnyrigg Rose: League Cup |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cjl69l1x463t |access-date=4 August 2024 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> before playing 84 minutes of the season opener against [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Inverness CT vs Dumbarton: League One |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cyj4zjrrd0zt |access-date=4 August 2024 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> On 9 November 2024, Bray scored his first league goal for Inverness, in a 2–1 away win over [[Cove Rangers F.C.|Cove Rangers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cove Rangers vs Inverness CT: Scottish League One |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cjr4l4rq52yt?page=2 |access-date=17 November 2024 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

On the last day of the winter 2025 transfer window, Bray signed for [[Scottish Championship|Championship]] side [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] on a four and a half year deal and was immediately loaned back to Inverness until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://dafc.co.uk/keith-bray-is-the-next-to-join/ |title=Keith Bray is the next to join |publisher=DAFC.co.uk |access-date=3 February 2025 |archive-date=3 February 2025 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250203203657/https://dafc.co.uk/keith-bray-is-the-next-to-join/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

'''Aston Jay Oxborough''' (born 9 May 1998) is an English [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] for [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]].

==Early life==

Oxborough was born in 1998 in England, He grew up in [[Norfolk]], England.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3095321/2022/01/27/norwich-aston-oxborough-just-playing-again-is-amazing-even-getting-the-crowd-abuse/|title=Aston Oxborough: 'Just playing again is amazing – even getting the crowd abuse'|publisher=nytimes.com}}</ref>

==Career==
In 2019, Oxborough was sent on loan to English side [[Wealdstone F.C.|Wealdstone]]. He helped the club win the league.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pinkun.com/news/22703414.oxborough-vows-return-injury-former-city-keeper-colleague-signs-salford/|title=Oxborough vows to return from injury as his former City keeper colleague signs for Salford|publisher=punkun.com}}</ref>

On 13 August 2022, Oxborough signed for Scottish side [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Aston Oxborough Joins Motherwell |url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2022/08/13/aston-oxborough-joins-motherwell/ |website=motherwellfc.co.uk/ |publisher=Motherwell F.C. |access-date=13 August 2022 |date=13 August 2022}}</ref> On 3 August 2024, he debuted for the club during a 0–0 draw with [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/motherwell-goalie-looking-keep-gloves-33390534|title=Motherwell goalie looking to keep the gloves for a long time|publisher=dailyrecord.co.uk}}</ref> On 10 October 2024, Oxborough signed a contract extension with Motherwell until the summer of 2027, with an option for an additional season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Aston Oxborough signs contract extension |url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2024/10/10/aston-oxborough-signs-contract-extension/ |website=motherwellfc.co.uk/ |publisher=Motherwell F.C. |accessdate=11 October 2024 |date=10 October 2024}}</ref> On 24 February 2026, Oxborough joined [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] on loan for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{cite '''Musa Dibaga Nimaga''' (born 27 April 2000) is a Gambian footballer who plays as a [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] for [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Musa Dibaga {{!}} Football Stats {{!}} Inverness Caledonian Thistle {{!}} Age 24 {{!}} Soccer Base |url=https://www.soccerbase.com/players/player.sd?player_id=164408 |access-date=2024-08-19 |website=www.soccerbase.com}}</ref><ref>{{Soccerway|musa-dibaga-nimaga/663992}}</ref>

== Career ==
Dibaga started his career playing at Murieston Amateurs (second choice) before moving on to [[CD Robres|Robres]] of the [[Tercera Federación|Spanish Tercera Federación]], being promoted to the first team and making 20 appearances over the 2020–21 season. In July 2021, Dibaga moved to Scotland and joined [[East of Scotland Football League#Premier Division|East of Scotland Premier Division]] side, [[Whitehill Welfare F.C.|Whitehill Welfare]] for a season before leaving them following their relegation to the [[East of Scotland Football League#First Division|First Division]]. In July 2022, Dibaga joined [[Lowland Football League|Lowland League]] side, [[Bo'ness United F.C.|Bo'ness United]] on a two-year deal. In his first season, Dibaga picked up a Lowland League Cup runners up medal, as Bo'ness held [[East Kilbride F.C.|East Kilbride]] to a 2–2 draw before losing on penalties.<ref>{{Cite web |title=East Kilbride vs. Bo'ness United - 21 May 2023 - Soccerway |url=https://uk.soccerway.com/matches/2023/05/21/scotland/lowland-league-cup/east-kilbride/boness-united-football-club/4053865/ |access-date=2024-08-19 |website=uk.soccerway.com}}</ref>

In August 2024, Dibaga got his first move into professional football, joining recently relegated [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] in [[Scottish League One]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-08-10 |title=Caley Thistle complete double swoop |url=https://www.inverness-courier.co.uk/sport/caley-thistle-complete-double-swoop-358010/ |access-date=2024-08-19 |website=Inverness Courier |language=en}}</ref> before making his professional debut a fortnight later in a 1–1 home draw against [[Montrose F.C.|Montrose]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chalk |first=Paul |date=2024-08-19 |title=Goalkeeper Musa Dibaga eager to progress after Caley Thistle debut |url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/inverness-caledonian-thistle/6556388/goalkeeper-musa-dibaga-eager-to-progress-after-caley-thistle-bow/ |access-date=2024-08-19 |website=Press and Journal |language=en-GB}}</ref> After being a big part in keeping the ''Caley Jags'' in League One amidst the club suffering through [[Administration (British football)|administration]], Dibaga departed Inverness in 2025 "with a heavy heart" after not being able to agree on terms for a new contract due to the club's situation.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chalk |first=Paul |date=2025-05-26 |title=EXCLUSIVE: Why Musa Dibaga has REJECTED Caley Thistle contract offer as stunned ICT react to decision |url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/inverness-caledonian-thistle/6765696/why-musa-dibaga-has-rejected-caley-thistle-deal-and-stunned-ict/ |access-date=2025-06-01 |website=Press and Journal |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==International career==
On 11 March 2025, Dibaga was named in the provisional 33 man squad for [[Gambia national football team|The Gambia]]'s [[2026 FIFA World Cup qualification (CAF)|2026 World Cup Qualifying]] campaign ahead of their matches against [[Kenya national football team|Kenya]] and [[Ivory Coast national football team|Ivory Coast]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=MSN |url=https://www.msn.com/en-gb/sport/fifa_world_cup/mckinstry-names-gambia-for-world-cup-qualifier-against-kenya/ar-AA1AF0n2?ocid=BingNewsSerp |access-date=2025-03-12 |website=www.msn.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-03-10 |title=Gambia coach McKinstry names 33-man squad for World Cup qualifiers |url=https://gambiana.com/gambia-coach-mckinstry-names-33-man-squad-for-world-cup-qualifiers/ |access-date=2025-03-12 |website=Gambiana |language=en-GB}}</ref> before being named in the final 24 man squad.

'''Calum Macleod''' (born 25 May 2006) is a Scottish professional footballer who plays for [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] in [[Scottish League One]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Calum MacLeod {{!}} Football Stats {{!}} Inverness Caledonian Thistle {{!}} Age 18 {{!}} Soccer BaseCl|url=https://www.soccerbase.com/players/player.sd?player_id=171019 |access-date=31 August 2024 |website=Soccerbase}}</ref>

== Career ==
MacLeod started his career with his hometown team, [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]], playing his way through the youth setup until 2022, when he was given a professional contract with the club.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Media |first=ICTFC |date=10 August 2023 |title=Three ICTFC Academy Graduates sign deals |url=https://ictfc.com/three-ictfc-academy-graduates-sign-deals/ |access-date=31 August 2024 |website=ICTFC |language=en-GB}}</ref> MacLeod made his debut for the club later that year in October 2022, featuring in an injury ravaged side, as Inverness lost 2–0 away to [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]] in the [[Scottish Challenge Cup]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=10 December 2022 |title=Hamilton Academical v Inverness Caledonian Thistle |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/63879706 |access-date=31 August 2024 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

In February 2024, MacLeod was sent on loan to fellow Invernesian side, [[Clachnacuddin F.C.|Clachnacuddin]], in the [[Highland Football League|Highland League]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Law |first=Callum |date=15 February 2024 |title=Clachnacuddin land Calum MacLeod on loan from Caley Thistle |url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/inverness-caledonian-thistle/6375327/clachnacuddin-land-calum-macleod-on-loan-from-caley-thistle/ |access-date=31 August 2024 |website=Press and Journal |language=en-GB}}</ref> scoring on his debut in a 3–2 away defeat to [[Rothes F.C.|Rothes]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rothes vs. Clachnacuddin - 9 March 2024 - Soccerway |url=https://uk.soccerway.com/matches/2024/03/09/scotland/scottish-football-league/rothes-football-club/clachnacuddin-football-club/4080390/ |access-date=31 August 2024 |website=Soccerway}}</ref>

On 3 August 2024, MacLeod made his professional league debut in a 1–1 home draw against [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Inverness CT vs Dumbarton: League One |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cyj4zjrrd0zt?page=3 |access-date=31 August 2024 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> On 14 September 2024, MacLeod scored his first professional goal in a 2–2 away draw to [[Alloa Athletic F.C.|Alloa Athletic]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alloa Athletic vs Inverness CT: League One |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cpw841d91dwt?page=4 |access-date=14 September 2024 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

== International career ==
On 4 November 2026, MacLeod and fellow Inverness player, [[Alfie Stewart (footballer)|Alfie Stewart]], were called up for the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland U-21]] squad ahead of friendlies against [[Ukraine national under-21 football team|Ukraine]] and the [[United States men's national under-23 soccer team|United States]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Caley Thistle pair national call-ups is inspiration to youngsters |url=https://www.inverness-courier.co.uk/sport/caley-thistle-pair-national-call-ups-is-inspiration-to-young-449400/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20261105230219/https://www.inverness-courier.co.uk/sport/caley-thistle-pair-national-call-ups-is-inspiration-to-young-449400/ |archive-date=2026-11-05 |access-date=2026-11-05 |work=Inverness Courier |language=en-GB}}</ref>

'''Billy Terrell''', also known as '''Billy Terrall''',<ref>{{Cite web |title=Boreham Wood vs Weymouth Matchday Programme 24.08.2024 |url=https://www.borehamwoodfootballclub.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/BWFC-Weymouth-VNLS-24-08-24.pdf}}</ref> (born 31 August 2003) is an English professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] for [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |date=1 August 2025 |title=Welcome Billy Terrell |url=https://dafc.co.uk/welcome-billy-terrell/ |access-date=7 September 2025 |website=Dunfermline Athletic F.C.}}</ref>

== Club career ==

=== AFC Bournemouth ===
Born in [[Southampton]], Terrell previously played within the youth academies of both [[Portsmouth F.C.|Portsmouth]] (2012–2017) and [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] (2017–2018) before joining the youth academy at [[AFC Bournemouth]] in 2018.<ref name=Weymouth1 /><ref name=":2" />

He signed his first professional contract with AFC Bournemouth on 1 January 2021<ref>{{Cite web |title=Billy Terrell - Player profile |url=https://www.soccerbase.com/players/player.sd?player_id=139111 |access-date=6 September 2024 |website=www.soccerbase.com}}</ref> and he was contracted to both their youth academy and their senior team until August 2025,<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0" /> making no appearances for AFC Bournemouth during [[2025–26 AFC Bournemouth season|2025–26]].

==== Wimborne Town (Two loan spells) ====
Terrell was loaned out to [[Wimborne Town F.C.|Wimborne Town]] during the 2020–21 season and he made ten appearances in all competitions,<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Billy Terrell {{!}} Player Profile |url=https://www.aylesburyunitedarchive.com/player/billy-terrell |access-date=6 September 2024 |website=Aylesbury United Archive}}</ref> all coming in 2020 as the league season was curtailed before all matches could be played.

He was loaned out again to Wimborne Town during the 2021–22 season,<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=20 August 2022 |title=Billy Terrell joins on loan! |url=https://uptheterras.co.uk/2022/08/20/billy-terrell-joins-on-loan/ |access-date=6 September 2024 |website=www.uptheterras.co.uk}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Terrell Completes Wimborne Loan |url=https://www.afcb.co.uk/news/under-21s/terrell-completes-wimborne-loan/ |access-date=10 August 2021 |publisher=AFC Bournemouth}}</ref> making a further sixteen appearances for the club.<ref name=":0" />

==== Weymouth (First loan spell) ====
Terrell was loaned out to [[Weymouth F.C.|Weymouth]] between 20 August 2022 and 1 January 2023 and made four appearances for the club.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{cite news |date=20 August 2022 |title=Goalkeeper Terrell Joins The Terras |url=https://www.afcb.co.uk/news/development-squad/goalkeeper-terrell-joins-the-terras/ |access-date=21 August 2022 |publisher=AFC Bournemouth}}</ref>

==== Dover Athletic (Loan) ====
During the first half of the 2023–24 season,{{refn|group=nb|Terrell was initially loaned to Dover Athletic on a season long loan but he was recalled by AFC Bournemouth on 9 January 2023.}} he was loaned out to [[Dover Athletic F.C.|Dover Athletic]]<ref>{{cite news |date=27 July 2023 |title=Terrell completes loan move to Dover |url=https://www.afcb.co.uk/news/development-squad/terrell-completes-loan-move-to-dover/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230727173236/https://www.afcb.co.uk/news/development-squad/terrell-completes-loan-move-to-dover/ |archive-date=27 July 2023 |access-date=27 July 2023 |publisher=AFC Bournemouth}}</ref> after [[Stuart Nelson]] moved to [[Cirencester Town F.C.|Cirencester Town]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reeves |first=Thomas |date=27 July 2023 |title=Goalkeeper Billy Terrell, 19, signs on season-long loan with Dover Athletic from Premier League Bournemouth |url=https://www.kentonline.co.uk/dover/sport/whites-sign-teenager-on-loan-from-premier-league-side-290809/ |access-date=6 September 2024 |website=Kent Online}}</ref> and during his time at the club, Terrell was a regular inclusion in the starting line-up.<ref name=":0" />

==== Dartford (Loan) ====
For the remainder of the 2023–24 season, Terrell was loaned out to [[Dartford F.C.|Dartford]] as a replacement for [[Ryan Sandford]],<ref name="BTerrell">{{cite news |title=Terrell makes Dartford loan move |url=https://www.afcb.co.uk/news/development-squad/terrell-makes-dartford-loan-move/ |access-date=9 January 2024 |publisher=AFC Bournemouth |date=9 January 2024 |archive-date=9 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240109210215/https://www.afcb.co.uk/news/development-squad/terrell-makes-dartford-loan-move/ |url-status=live }}</ref> who had moved to [[Crawley Town F.C.|Crawley Town]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=6 March 2024 |title=DARTFORD FC {{!}} IN CONVERSATION WITH BILLY TERRELL |url=https://www.dartfordfc.com/dartford-fc-in-conversation-with-billy-terrell/ |access-date=6 September 2024 |website=www.dartfordfc.co.uk}}</ref> He played all twelve league matches for Dartford during his time at the club.<ref name=":0" />

==== Weymouth (Second loan spell) ====
Terrell was loaned out to Weymouth for a second time during what was initially planned to be a season-long deal encompassing the [[2024–25 National League#National League South|2024–25 season]] as a replacement for [[Gerard Benfield]],<ref name="Weymouth2">{{cite news |date=3 August 2024 |title=Weymouth loan for goalkeeper Terrell |url=https://www.afcb.co.uk/news/2024/august/03/weymouth-loan-for-goalkeeper-terrell/ |access-date=4 August 2024 |publisher=AFC Bournemouth}}</ref><ref name=Weymouth1>{{Cite web |date=3 August 2024 |title=Billy Terrell Joins On Loan |url=https://uptheterras.co.uk/2024/08/03/billy-terrell-joins-on-loan-2/ |access-date=6 September 2024 |website=www.uptheterras.co.uk}}</ref> who was loaned out by Weymouth to [[Dorchester Town F.C.|Dorchester Town]].{{refn|group=nb|name=Benfield|Benfield was initially loaned to Dorchester Town on a season long loan but he was recalled by Weymouth no later than 7 September 2024 and went back on loan to Dorchester Town on 17 September 2024.}}

Terrell only appeared in seven league for Weymouth during the 2024–25 season, and despite this, he became an unused substitute during a 2–1 away win against [[Dorking Wanderers F.C.|Dorking Wanderers]] on 7 September 2024 as Benfield was recalled from his loan spell at Dorchester Town to play one match for Weymouth.{{refn|group=nb|name=Benfield|}}

Terrell was named as the substitute goalkeeper during Weymouth's 2–0 loss against [[Forest Green Rovers F.C.|Forest Green Rovers]] during the [[2024–25 FA Cup qualifying rounds|FA Cup 4th qualifying round]] match on 13 October 2024. He also featured during a 3–0 win against [[Wimborne Town F.C.|Wimborne Town]] during the [[Dorset Senior Cup|2024–25 Dorset Senior Cup]] quarter-final on 12 November 2024.

Terrell did not play in any league matches for Weymouth since September 2024, with the club favouring to instead start goalkeeper [[Will Buse]], who was signed on a loan deal from [[Yeovil Town F.C.|Yeovil Town]] until June 2025.<ref>{{cite web |date=13 September 2024 |title=Will Buse Signs On Loan |url=https://uptheterras.co.uk/2024/09/13/will-buse-signs-on-loan/ |access-date=21 September 2024 |publisher=www.uptheterras.co.uk}}</ref> Terrell's second loan spell with Weymouth would then end prematurely on 17 January 2025, and he returned to [[AFC Bournemouth|Bournemouth]] on the same day.<ref>{{cite web |date=17 January 2025 |title=Squad Update |url=https://uptheterras.co.uk/2025/01/17/squad-update/ |accessdate=2 March 2025 |website=uptheterras.co.uk}}</ref>

=== Dunfermline Athletic ===
On 1 August 2025, Terrell signed a one-year deal with [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]].<ref name=":2" /> He made his debut for the club on 23 September 2025 during the 1–0 loss against [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]], playing the full match.<ref>{{Cite web |date=24 September 2025 |title=Billy Terrell Reflects on his Dunfermline Debut |url=https://dafc.co.uk/billy-terrell-reflects-on-his-dunfermline-debut/ |access-date=24 September 2025 |website=Dunfermline Athletic Football Club}}</ref> He was a runner-up in the [[2025–26 Scottish Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |date=23 May 2026 |title=Celtic 3-1 Dunfermline: Martin O'Neill leads Hoops to Scottish Cup title to complete domestic double |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11781/13542685/celtic-3-1-dunfermline-martin-oneill-leads-hoops-to-scottish-cup-title-to-complete-domestic-double |accessdate=25 May 2026 |work=Sky Sports}}</ref>

On 13 February 2026, he extended his contract until 2028.<ref>{{Cite web |date=13 February 2026 |title=Billy Terrell Commits Future to Pars |url=https://www.dafc.co.uk/news/2026/february/13/billy-terrell-commits-future-to-pars/ |access-date=10 August 2026 |website=Dunfermline Athletic Football Club}}</ref>

'''Alfie Stewart''' (born 31 July 2006) is a Scottish footballer who currently plays as a midfielder for [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] on loan from [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alfie Stewart {{!}} Football Stats {{!}} Aberdeen {{!}} Age 18 {{!}} Soccer Base |url=https://www.soccerbase.com/players/player.sd?player_id=165905 |access-date=2025-05-16 |website=www.soccerbase.com}}</ref>

== Club career ==

=== Aberdeen ===
Stewart started his career with the youth team of [[Aberdeenshire Amateur Football Association]] side, Newtonhill AFC, before joining [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]]'s academy rising through the ranks before being promoted to the senior team.

In January 2024, Stewart was loaned out to [[Scottish League Two]] side, [[Peterhead F.C.|Peterhead]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Welcome to Peterhead Alfie Stewart {{!}} Peterhead FC |url=https://www.peterheadfc.co.uk/2024/01/19/welcome-to-peterhead-alfie-stewart/ |access-date=2025-05-16 |language=en}}</ref>

In January 2025, Stewart was loaned out to [[Scottish League One]] side, [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]], alongside fellow ''Don'', [[Alfie Bavidge]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-01-04 |title=Head coach pleased with new signings at Inverness Caledonian Thistle |url=https://www.inverness-courier.co.uk/sport/head-coach-pleased-with-new-signings-at-inverness-caledonian-370779/ |access-date=2025-05-16 |website=Inverness Courier |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-01-04 |title=Caley Thistle sign duo on loan from Aberdeen until end of season |url=https://www.inverness-courier.co.uk/sport/caley-thistle-sign-duo-on-loan-from-aberdeen-until-end-of-se-370758/ |access-date=2025-05-16 |website=Inverness Courier |language=en}}</ref>

On 15 July 2025, Stewart returned to Inverness Caledonian Thistle on a half season loan, making his second debut for the club on the same day in a 2–0 home win over [[Elgin City F.C.|Elgin City]] in the League Cup.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-07-15 |title=Aberdeen teenager rejoins Caley Thistle on loan |url=https://www.inverness-courier.co.uk/sport/aberdeen-teenager-rejoins-caley-thistle-on-loan-387183/ |access-date=2025-07-15 |website=Inverness Courier |language=en}}</ref>

During the 2025–26 season, Stewart played an important role in helping his side win the [[Scottish League One|League One]] title, with the trophy and promotion to [[Scottish Championship]] being secured on the final day of the season with a 2–1 win over [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-02 |title=Inverness CT win title as champions East Kilbride make history |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c98re00e3g4o |access-date=2026-05-05 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Chalk |first=Paul |date=2026-05-02 |title=CHAMPIONS: Caley Thistle are League One winners after victory against Hamilton Academical |url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/inverness-caledonian-thistle/7006745/caledonian-thistle-football-hamilton-report/ |access-date=2026-05-05 |website=Press and Journal |language=en-GB}}</ref> His performances across the season drew significant attention, and he was subsequently nominated for the [[PFA Scotland]] League One Player of the Year award.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wilson |first=Luke |date=2026-04-23 |title=POTY Nominations {{!}} Championship, League 1 & League 2 |url=https://pfascotland.co.uk/poty-nominations-championship-league-1-league-2/ |access-date=2026-05-05 |website=PFA Scotland |language=en-US}}</ref>

== International Career ==
On 4 November 2026, Stewart and fellow Inverness player, [[Calum MacLeod (footballer)|Calum MacLeod]], were called up for the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland U-21]] squad ahead of friendlies against [[Ukraine national under-21 football team|Ukraine]] and the [[United States men's national under-23 soccer team|United States]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Caley Thistle pair national call-ups is inspiration to youngsters |url=https://www.inverness-courier.co.uk/sport/caley-thistle-pair-national-call-ups-is-inspiration-to-young-449400/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20261105230219/https://www.inverness-courier.co.uk/sport/caley-thistle-pair-national-call-ups-is-inspiration-to-young-449400/ |archive-date=2026-11-05 |access-date=2026-11-05 |work=Inverness Courier |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Dundee United===
Stirton signed his first professional contract with Dundee United in May 2023.<ref>{{Cite web | title=Owen Stirton: The Dundee United journey so far - and what's next? | url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-united/5122442/owen-stirton-dundee-united-journey-whats-next/ | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241112070705/https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-united/5122442/owen-stirton-dundee-united-journey-whats-next/ | access-date=2025-06-23 | archive-date=2024-11-12}}</ref>

On 9 November 2024 Stirton scored his first professional goal for Dundee United, scoring with his first touch in a 3–0 home win over Ross County.<ref>{{Cite web | title=Dundee United vs Ross County: Scottish Premiership - BBC Sport - BBC Sport | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/ckg050g266jt | access-date=2025-06-23 | website=www.bbc.co.uk}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web | title='Roy of the Rovers stuff' – Owen Stirton goal delights manager Jim Goodwin – The Irish News | url=https://www.irishnews.com/sport/soccer/roy-of-the-rovers-stuff-owen-stirton-goal-delights-manager-jim-goodwin-FSVPPAP545OPJGJVMOO3IT4PSE/ | access-date=2025-06-23 | website=www.irishnews.com}}</ref>

In January 2025 Stirton signed a two-year contract extension with Dundee United.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web | title=OWEN STIRTON PENS NEW DEAL {{!}} Dundee United Football Club | url=https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/news/8772/OWEN-STIRTON-PENS-NEW-DEAL.html | access-date=2025-06-23 | website=www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web | title=Owen Stirton pens new Dundee United deal | url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-united/5169686/owen-stirton-pens-new-dundee-united-deal/ | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250125121810/https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-united/5169686/owen-stirton-pens-new-dundee-united-deal/ | access-date=2025-06-23 | archive-date=2025-01-25}}</ref>

Stirton scored his first goal of the 2025–26 season in a 2–1 away defeat to Kilmarnock in the [[Scottish League Cup]].<ref>https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c7vl1mj96j9t</ref>

====Montrose (loan)====
In January 2025, Stirton joined [[Scottish League One]] club [[Montrose F.C.|Montrose]] on loan until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web | title=Dundee United starlet Owen Stirton joins Montrose | url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-united/5164496/dundee-united-starlet-owen-stirton-joins-montrose/ | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250118093929/https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-united/5164496/dundee-united-starlet-owen-stirton-joins-montrose/ | access-date=2025-06-23 | archive-date=2025-01-18}}</ref>

Stirton scored on his Montrose debut in a 2–2 away draw with Annan Athletic.<ref>{{Cite web | title=Annan Athletic vs Montrose: Scottish League One stats & head-to-head - BBC Sport | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cdxng4n54egt | access-date=2025-06-23 | website=www.bbc.co.uk}}</ref> Stirton then followed this up by scoring a double in his second game and home debut for Montrose.<ref>{{Cite web | title=Owen Stirton: Dundee United kid bags brace, Charlie Dewar shines | url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-united/5179638/dundee-united-scout-report-owen-stirton-dewar/ | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250210002307/https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-united/5179638/dundee-united-scout-report-owen-stirton-dewar/ | access-date=2025-06-23 | archive-date=2025-02-10}}</ref>

Stirton won the Scottish League One player of the month award for February 2025.<ref>{{Cite web | title=Stirton nets League 1 award {{!}} SPFL | url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/stirton-nets-league-1-award | access-date=2025-06-23 | website=spfl.co.uk}}</ref>

==International career==

Stirton was called up to the Scottish International Under 17s team, making his debut and scoring his first international goal against Kazakhstan.<ref name="auto"/>

Stirton was called up to the Scottish International Under 19s team in March 2025.<ref>{{Cite web | title=Dundee United: Stirton, Cleall-Harding in first Scotland U/19 calls | url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-united/5196227/dundee-united-stirton-cleall-harding-scotland-call/ | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250309054818/https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-united/5196227/dundee-united-stirton-cleall-harding-scotland-call/ | access-date=2025-06-23 | archive-date=2025-03-09}}</ref>

'''Ben McPherson''' (born 19 March 2004) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[defender (association football)|defender]] for [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]].

==Club career==

===Celtic===
McPherson has been a part of Celtic's B team since coming through the club's youth academy.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.celticfc.com/players/celtic-b/Ben-McPherson/|title=Ben McPherson|website=Celtic FC|accessdate=4 August 2025}}</ref>

McPherson extended his Celtic deal in December 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.celticfc.com/news/2022/december/23/contract-extension-for-young-celts--joe-morrison-and-ben-mcpherson/|title=Contract extension for young Celts, Joe Morrison and Ben McPherson|date=23 December 2022|website=Celtic FC|accessdate=4 August 2025}}</ref>

====Queen's Park (loan)====
McPherson joined [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]] on a season long loan in August 2023.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://queensparkfc.co.uk/queens-park-bring-in-ben-mcpherson-on-loan/|title=Queen's Park bring in Ben McPherson on loan|first=Ian|last=Cairns|date=10 August 2023|accessdate=4 August 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/czkpzyj4y41o|title=Youngster McPherson joins Queen's Park on loan|date=10 August 2023|website=BBC Sport|accessdate=4 August 2025}}</ref> McPherson made his Queen's Park debut in a 2–1 home win over Arbroath.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://queensparkfc.co.uk/queens-park-2-arbroath-1/|title=Queen's Park 2 Arbroath 1|first=Ian|last=Cairns|date=12 August 2023|accessdate=4 August 2025}}</ref>

====Partick Thistle (loan)====
In August 2025, McPherson joined Scottish Championship club [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] on a season long loan.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/ben-mcpherson-makes-maryhill-loan-move/|title=Ben McPherson makes Maryhill loan move|website=Partick Thistle FC|accessdate=4 August 2025}}</ref>

McPherson scored his first goal for Thistle, opening the scoring in a 2–0 away win against Raith Rovers.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cx248vxgj2jt|title=Raith Rovers 0-2 Partick Thistle: Visitors narrow gap with St Johnstone in Scottish Championship|first=Live|last=Text|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

McPherson, alongside fellow Celtic loanee Josh Clarke, agreed to sign for Partick Thistle on a permanent basis in February 2026.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ptfc.co.uk/ptfc-news/clarke-and-mcpherson-agree-permanent-moves-to-maryhill/|title=Clarke and McPherson agree permanent moves to Maryhill|website=Partick Thistle FC}}</ref>

'''Andrew Tod''' (born 26 February 2006) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]], [[Midfielder#Winger|winger]], or [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline]].

==Early life==
Tod was born on 26 February 2006 in [[Perth, Scotland|Perth]], Scotland. The son of Scottish footballer [[Andy Tod]], he is the older brother of fellow footballer [[John Tod (footballer)|John Tod]].<ref>[https://dafc.co.uk/andrew-and-john-tod-sign-new-deals/ Andrew and John Tod sign new deals], Dunfermline Athletic FC, 11 July 2025</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dunfermlinepress.com/sport/25613657.dunfermlines-andy-tod-call-up-scotland-under-21s/|title=Dunfermline's Andy Tod on the call-up to Scotland under-21s|publisher=[[Dunfermline Press]]|date=11 November 2025|access-date=6 March 2026}}</ref>

==Career==
As a youth player, Tod played for local side Kinross Colts. He joined the [[youth academy]] of [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] in 2016 before signing for [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] in 2018. Ahead of the [[2021–22 Dunfermline Athletic F.C. season|2021–22 season]], he returned to Dunfermline and was promoted to the club's senior squad in 2022.

In February 2023 he was sent on loan to [[Elgin City F.C.|Elgin City]], where he made seven league appearances without scoring. Subsequently, in September 2024 he was loaned to [[East Fife F.C.|East Fife]], where he made five league appearances and scored one goal before a knee injury two months later forced his return to Dunfermline ahead of schedule.<ref>{{WorldFootball.net|andy-tod}}</ref>

==Style of play==
Tod plays as a [[midfielder]], [[Midfielder#Winger|winger]], or [[Forward (association football)|forward]]. Right-footed, he is known for his versatility.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/5392374/dunfermline-athletic-andrew-tod-iain-brunskill-season/|title=How Dunfermline are guiding Andrew Tod after striking start to the season|publisher=[[The Courier (Dundee)|The Courier]]|date=12 December 2025|access-date=6 March 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
Tod is a Scotland youth international. During the autumn of 2025, he played for the [[Scotland national under-21 football team]] for [[2027 UEFA European Under-21 Championship qualification]].
