'''Noa Boutin''' (born 10 September 2003) is a French professional footballer who currently plays for [[Scottish Championship]] side, [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Noa Boutin {{!}} Football Stats {{!}} No Club {{!}} Age 22 {{!}} 2022- |url=https://www.soccerbase.com/players/player.sd?player_id=166091 |access-date=2026-06-16 |website=soccerbase.com}}</ref>

== Early life and career ==
Born in Paris, Boutin played for the [[AC Boulogne-Billancourt (football)|footballing division]] of Parisian sports club [[AC Boulogne-Billancourt]], before being scouted by recently relegated Premier League side, AFC Bournemouth.

In February 2022, Boutin was sent out on loan to [[Southern Football League#Premier South|Southern League Premier Division]] side, [[Poole Town F.C.|Poole Town]], until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-02-22 |title=Two more Cherries youngsters sent out on loan to Southern Premier sides |url=https://www.bournemouthecho.co.uk/sport/19943146.two-cherries-youngsters-sent-loan-southern-premier-sides/ |access-date=2026-06-16 |website=Bournemouth Echo |language=en}}</ref>

In August 2022, Boutin was sent on loan to [[National League South]] side, [[Weymouth F.C.|Weymouth]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Noa BOUTIN – The Terras |url=https://uptheterras.co.uk/player/noa-boutin/ |access-date=2026-06-16 |language=en-GB}}</ref> before returning to Bournemouth in October. Later that season, in January 2023, Boutin returned to the Southern League Premier Division, joining [[Gosport Borough F.C.|Gosport Borough]], on loan until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=BORO’ Sign Bournemouth Defender - Noa Boutin |url=https://www.gosportboroughfc.com/news/boro-sign-bournemouth-defender--noa-boutin-2756838.html |access-date=2026-06-16 |website=gosportboroughfc.com |language=en}}</ref>

In August 2024, Boutin joined [[National League (division)|National League]] side, [[Eastleigh F.C.|Eastleigh]], on loan for a season,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Official: Noa Boutin joins the Spitfires on loan |url=https://eastleighfc.com/2024/08/official-noa-boutin-joins-the-spitfires-on-loan/ |access-date=2026-06-16 |website=eastleighfc.com |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-08-23 |title=Spitfires sign young Cherries defender on loan until January |url=https://www.dailyecho.co.uk/sport/24538330.eastleigh-sign-young-bournemouth-defender-loan-january/ |access-date=2026-06-16 |website=Daily Echo |language=en}}</ref> before returning to the National League again the following August with [[Sutton United F.C.|Sutton United]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Noa Boutin |url=https://www.suttonunited.net/player/noa-boutin/ |access-date=2026-06-16 |website=Sutton United Football Club |language=en-GB}}</ref>

On 16 June 2026, Boutin was released by Bournemouth, and moved to Scotland, signing a pre-contract agreement with [[Scottish Championship]] side, [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-06-16 |title=Caley Thistle add French left-back from Bournemouth |url=https://www.inverness-courier.co.uk/sport/caley-thistle-add-french-left-back-from-bournemouth-437746/ |access-date=2026-06-16 |website=Inverness Courier |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-06-16 |title=Noa Boutin signs for ICTFC |url=https://ictfc.com/noa-boutin-signs-for-ictfc/ |access-date=2026-06-16 |website=ICTFC |language=en-GB}}</ref>

'''Kian Corbally''' (born 31 December 2003) is an Irish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]]. His previous clubs are [[St Patrick's Athletic F.C.|St Patrick's Athletic]], [[Longford Town F.C.|Longford Town]], [[Wexford F.C.|Wexford]] and [[Ballymena United F.C.|Ballymena United]].

==Club career==
===Youth career===
Corbally came through the [[Crumlin United F.C.|Crumlin United]] academy, before joining the academy of [[League of Ireland]] club [[St Patrick's Athletic F.C.|St Patrick's Athletic]] at Under-15 level in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.extratime.com/player/11127506/kian_corbally/|title=Kian Corbally | St Patrick's Athletic U17|website=extratime.com}}</ref> He won the Under-15 league title in his first full season with the club.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.stpatsfc.com/profile.php?id=287|title=Kian Corbally|website=www.stpatsfc.com}}</ref> In October 2019, he was part of the under 17 team that won the 2019 league title, beating [[Bohemian F.C.|Bohemians]] 4–0 in the final at [[Dalymount Park]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.extratime.com/articles/23859/u17-national-league-final-report-st-patricks-athletic-4---0-bohemians/|title=U17 National League Final Report: St Patrick's Athletic 4 - 0 Bohemians|first=Dave|last=Donnelly|website=extratime.com}}</ref> On 22 December 2020, Corbally played in the [[League of Ireland U19 Division]] Final, in a 2–1 win over [[Bohemian F.C.|Bohemians]] [[Overtime (sports)|after extra time]] at the [[UCD Bowl]] to secure a [[UEFA Youth League]] spot for the club.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/soccer/arid-40195782.html|title=Darragh Burns hits the winner as Saints claim U19 League of Ireland crown|first=John|last=Fallon|date=December 22, 2020|website=Irish Examiner}}</ref> He made his [[UEFA Youth League]] debut on 29 September 2021 in a 2–1 loss to [[Serbia]]n side [[Red Star Belgrade]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/st-patricks-athletic-red-star-belgrade-match-report-5561411-Sep2021/|title=St Pat's rally from two goals down but fall just short in Uefa Youth League first leg|first=Dave|last=Donnelly|date=29 September 2021|website=The42}}</ref> He was part of the side that won the [[League of Ireland U19 Division]] in 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.stpatsfc.com/news.php?id=9253|title=U19s Clinch League Title|website=www.stpatsfc.com}}</ref>

===St Patrick's Athletic===
He made his senior debut for [[St Patrick's Athletic F.C.|St Patrick's Athletic]] on 1 November 2019 in a [[Leinster Senior Cup (association football)|Leinster Senior Cup]] Semi-Final tie away to [[Sheriff Y.C.|Sheriff YC]], with Corbally replacing [[Ben McCormack]] from the bench in a Pats team made up of academy players, before scoring the final goal of the game in the 118th minute of a 3–1 win after extra time, at age 15 years 305 days old he become the club's youngest ever goalscorer at senior level in the process at the time (a record that has since overtaken by [[Mason Melia]]).<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.extratime.com/articles/23870/leinster-senior-cup-report-sheriff-yc-1--3-st-patricks-athletic-aet/|title=Leinster Senior Cup Report: Sheriff YC 1 -3 St Patrick's Athletic AET|website=extratime.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/share/1Bcy5mYosG/?mibextid=wwXIfr|title=15 years, 305 days! By our... - St Patrick's Athletic FC}}</ref> On 16 November 2019, he started in the Final of the [[2018–19 Leinster Senior Cup]], as his side defeated [[Athlone Town A.F.C.|Athlone Town]] 4–0 at [[Richmond Park (football ground)|Richmond Park]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.extratime.com/articles/23940/leinster-senior-cup-final-report-st-patricks-athletic-4---0-athlone-town/|title=Leinster Senior Cup Final Report: St Patrick's Athletic 4 - 0 Athlone Town|website=extratime.com}}</ref> On 19 November 2021, Corbally made his [[League of Ireland Premier Division]] debut for the club, replacing [[Jamie Lennon]] from the bench in the final game of the season, a 0–0 draw away to [[Waterford F.C.|Waterford]] at the [[Waterford Regional Sports Centre|RSC]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/share/1V2dSa2bwD/?mibextid=wwXIfr|title=𝙇𝙀𝘼𝙂𝙐𝙀 𝘿𝙀𝘽𝙐𝙏 𝙁𝙊𝙍 𝘾𝙊𝙍𝘽𝘼𝙇𝙇𝙔... - St Patrick's Athletic FC}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/soccer/arid-40748763.html|title=Waterford face into relegation playoff final after draw with St Pat's|first=Adrian|last=Flanagan|date=19 November 2021|website=Irish Examiner}}</ref>

====Longford Town loan====
Having failed to make an appearance in the [[2022 St Patrick's Athletic F.C. season|2022 season]], Corbally was loaned out to [[League of Ireland First Division]] club [[Longford Town F.C.|Longford Town]] until the end of the season in order to gain first team experience.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/share/1Bn4JJXrJg/?mibextid=wwXIfr|title=🚨 Kian Corbally has joined 1st... - St Patrick's Athletic FC}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.longfordleader.ie/sport/soccer/longford-town-away-to-waterford-in-quest-for-positive-result-7754512|title=Longford Town away to Waterford in quest for positive result|date=21 July 2022|website=Longford Live}}</ref> He made a total of 14 appearances for the club during his loan spell.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.extratime.com/player/stats/11127506/kian_corbally/|title=Kian Corbally | Stats|website=extratime.com}}</ref>

===Wexford===
Corbally signed for [[League of Ireland First Division]] club [[Wexford F.C.|Wexford]] ahead of the [[2023 League of Ireland First Division|2023 season]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://wexfordfc.ie/wexford-fc-sign-top-young-talent-kian-corbally/|title=Wexford FC sign top young talent Kian Corbally! – Wexford FC}}</ref> He scored 2 goals in 35 appearances in all competitions in his first season with the club, before signing a new contract for the [[2024 League of Ireland First Division|2024 season]], despite reported interest from [[Millwall F.C.|Millwall]], [[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]] and [[Newport County F.C.|Newport County]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://wexfordfc.ie/kian-corbally-returns-to-wexford-fc/|title=Kian Corbally returns to Wexford FC – Wexford FC}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.irishmirror.ie/sport/soccer/soccer-news/wexford-youngster-set-cross-channel-31233791|title=Wexford youngster set for cross-channel move this winter|first=by Mark|last=McCadden|date=19 October 2023|website=Irish Mirror}}</ref> Corbally scored a total of 5 goals in 77 appearances in all competitions in his two seasons with the club, including a run to the Semi-Final of the [[2024 FAI Cup]].<ref name="auto"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/drogheda-wexford-report-6507304-Oct2024/|title=Foley's injury-time winner sees Drogheda book place in FAI Cup final|first=Barry|last=Landy|date=6 October 2024|website=The 42}}</ref>

===Ballymena United===
In January 2025, Corbally signed for [[NIFL Premiership]] club [[Ballymena United F.C.|Ballymena United]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.newsletter.co.uk/sport/football/kian-corbally-sold-on-ballymena-move-through-former-player-as-braidmen-host-larne-in-shanes-hill-derby-5011848|title=Kian Corbally: 'I think this opportunity was the next step I needed by coming up here'|date=28 February 2025|website=Belfast News Letter}}</ref> In May 2025, he signed a new two-year contract with the club and in January 2026, he drew reported interest from [[Scottish Premiership]], [[EFL League One]] and [[EFL League Two]] clubs.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.newsletter.co.uk/sport/football/northern-ireland/transfer-interest-in-irish-league-pair-heating-up-with-january-window-set-to-open-5459797|title=Transfer interest in Irish League pair heating up with January window set to open|date=31 December 2025|website=Belfast News Letter}}</ref> He scored 7 goals in 58 appearances in all competitions during his 18 months with the club before departing in June 2026.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.newsletter.co.uk/sport/football/kian-corbally-grateful-to-ballymena-united-as-midfielder-seals-full-time-switch-at-dunfermline-athletic-8750473|title=Kian Corbally appreciative of Ballymena United support as midfielder joins Dunfermline Athletic|date=19 June 2026|website=Belfast News Letter}}</ref>

===Dunfermline Athletic===
On 18 June 2026, Corbally signed a two-year contract with the option of a third year, with [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://dafc.co.uk/kian-corbally-joins-dunfermline-athletic/|title=Kian Corbally joins Dunfermline Athletic | Dunfermline Athletic Football Club -|first=Craig|last=Brown|date=18 June 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/5520437/kian-corbally-dunfermline-athletic-fc-signing-ballymena/|title=Who is Kian Corbally? Dunfermline Athletic's new signing who ex-St Mirren boss says 'trains like an absolute demon'|date=18 June 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.irishmirror.ie/sport/soccer/soccer-news/northern-irish-premiership-side-confirms-34485465|title=Northern Irish side confirms signing of ex-St Pat’s and Wexford midfielder|date=15 January 2025|website=Irish Mirror}}</ref>

==International career==
Corbally made his international debut on 11 October 2021, playing the full 90 minutes for the [[Republic of Ireland national under-19 football team|Republic of Ireland U19]] side in a 1–1 draw with [[Sweden men's national under-19 football team|Sweden U19]] in a friendly in [[Marbella]], [[Spain]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fai.ie/latest/report-ireland-mu19-1-1-sweden-mu19/|title=REPORT | Ireland MU19 1-1 Sweden MU19|website=www.fai.ie}}</ref>
